# Design

<!-- Supersedes the 2026-09-25 version of this change in Roam (block LPDwCRT6_). -->

## Context

These facts from `origin/main` shape the design.

**Identity and data**

- **Space accounts.** Plugins sign in as a per-space account with `signInWithPassword` (Supabase's sign-in call) in `packages/database/src/lib/contextFunctions.ts`. This spec calls that credential the **space login**. It is a random secret stored in the plugin; there are no personal user accounts yet. `mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/kPg_0_-lh)) adds the handoff and the `mcp_session` registry (list of handed-over sessions). None of it is in the repo yet.
- **Concepts and content.**
  - `Concept` (the node, type and relation table) holds node instances, schemas and relations, flagged by `is_schema` and `is_relation`.
  - `Content` (the text table) joins it on `(space_id, source_local_id)`. Its variants are `direct` (title), `direct_and_children`, `direct_and_description` (title plus description) and `full` (body).
- **Readability.** The `my_*` views (views filtered to what the caller can read), and helpers such as `in_space` and `can_view_specific_resource`, express read access.

**Discovery and embeddings**

- **Discovery.** [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091) made discovery return shared nodes.
  - `packages/database/src/lib/sharedNodes.ts` returns a `SharedNodeListing`: `{ nodes, spaces }` of `DbCrossAppNode` (shared node format).
  - `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID) reads one readable node by `rid` (global node ID).
  - `dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` converts nodes, node types and relations into that format.
  - Neither the listing nor the converter includes `content.full` (the body); import fetches it separately.
- **Embeddings.** `embedding.sql` stores 1536-dimension `text-embedding-3-small` vectors, each with an `obsolete` flag.
  - `match_content_embeddings` (the existing semantic search query) applies a similarity threshold and has no type filter.
  - Obsidian embeds the title (`direct`). Roam embeds the title plus description (`direct_and_description`) when there is a description, and the title alone otherwise.
  - The website embeds text with the team's OpenAI key (`/api/embeddings/openai/small`).
  - No full-text (keyword) index exists on `Content` today.

**Database access controls**

- **Row-level security.** 61 of the 65 row-level security policies have no `TO` clause, so they apply to every database role. The other four are `TO authenticated` on `storage.objects` (file storage), which retrieval doesn't read. Table grants go only to `authenticated` (the signed-in role) and `service_role`.
- **Function privileges.** `PUBLIC` (every database role) can execute every function in the `public` schema, because no schema file revokes that default. Some write functions are `SECURITY DEFINER` (they run as their owner, not as the caller), such as `create_secret_token` and `accept_group_invitation`. So table grants alone don't stop them.
- **Auth settings.** `config.toml` sets `jwt_expiry = 3600` (a session token lasts one hour). The custom access token hook is commented out.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:**

- One retrieval service: every client, the MCP included, goes through the API.
- Reuse existing data, vectors, converters and access rules.
- The database enforces the agent session's read-only access, not the MCP.
- Sync gaps are reported as errors, never as partial content.

**Non-Goals:**

- A new identity system.
- A hosted MCP.
- A second embedding pipeline.
- Attachment access.
- Auditing.

## Decisions

### 1. The API is the retrieval service; the MCP is its client

```
Roam / Obsidian --connect command--> bundle (shown once)
                                        |
             npx @discourse-graphs/mcp connect --> local state file
                                        |
agent client --stdio--> local MCP (thin client)
                            |
                            | HTTPS + session token
                            v
developer ----------> apps/website /api/v1 --+--> packages/database functions --> Supabase
                                             +--> OpenAI (search queries only)
```

Each capability spec covers one layer:

```
agent client --> MCP tools ----+     discourse-mcp: tools pass API results through
                               v
developer ---------------> API routes     headless-retrieval-api: HTTP, auth, envelope, versioning
                               |
                               v
              retrieval functions in packages/database
                                          discourse-retrieval: what the four operations return
```

- **The API holds all retrieval logic.** It is four routes in `apps/website`. They call `packages/database` functions with the caller's session, so row-level security applies.
- **The MCP** holds a session and maps each tool to one API call. It never reads the database or calls OpenAI.
- **Developers** call the same routes directly.

**The contract is `/api/v1`** (the versioned route prefix).
- Installed MCP copies can't be force-updated, so `/api/v1` changes only additively, and a breaking change needs `/api/v2`.
- Schema, query and converter fixes behind the API ship by deploying the website, without an MCP release.

**Alternatives:**
- **The MCP reads the database directly.**
  - Installed copies would then depend on view shapes, and every fix would need an MCP release.
  - The MCP would bundle database code and call an embedding route outside the API's auth.
  - The API and the MCP would be two adapters to keep in parity.
- **A hosted MCP in `apps/website` (the 2026-09-25 version).** It reaches ChatGPT but needs a hosted credential store. The 2026-11-10 meeting chose a local MCP. A hosted MCP can still wrap this API later.

### 2. Reuse the discovery read path

The API's routes call TypeScript functions in `packages/database`. These build on Sid's discovery code from [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091):

- **Get-node** calls `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID), then fetches the `full` Content (the body) the way import does.
- **Type discovery** reads node types from readable node instances and labels them with `dbNodeSchemasToCrossApp` (converts node types).
- **Discourse context** finds the readable relation instances that touch the node.
  - Candidates come from `refs`, the list of referenced IDs.
  - Direction comes from the `source` and `destination` keys of `reference_content` (the relation's endpoint map).
  - Relations are converted with `dbRelationsToCrossApp` (converts relations).

Only search needs a new RPC (database function); see Decision 6.

**Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** four new RPCs, which would duplicate the converters.

### 3. Hand over a session through `mcp-session-access`

`mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/kPg_0_-lh)) defines the handoff:

- **Handoff.**
  1. The plugin opens a new session for the space account, using a second client that neither persists nor auto-refreshes.
  2. It registers the session with `register_mcp_session(label)`.
  3. It shows the bundle once: Supabase URL, anon key, space ID and refresh token. It keeps no copy.
- **Registry.** `mcp_session` (list of handed-over sessions) records the session ID (taken from the caller's own token), the label, the space account and the creation time.
- **Sign-out.** The holder can sign itself out with local scope (only its own session). Per-session sign-out from the plugin is proposed for right after v0.
- **Emergency switch.** Until then, the cut-off is to sign out every other session of the space account. That also signs out the other plugin instances, which sign back in with the space login.
- **Who can connect.** Any plugin user of the space.

**Tokens.** Two tokens are involved:

- the **session token** is the session's short-lived access token, the one the API takes;
- the **refresh token** renews the session token, and it rotates on every use.

The bundle carries only the refresh token. So the holder's first session token comes from a refresh, and it already carries `mcp_reader` (read-only database role; Decision 4). The plugin discards the `authenticated` session token it used to register.

**Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** Option B, a separate agent account for each grant, with a credential issued from a website page. The 2026-11-10 meeting judged its security gain marginal for the extra work.

### 4. The database makes handed-over sessions read-only (A2)

Under Option A2 ([decision](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/guIcK3Z9M)), the agent signs in as the space account, but the database makes its session read-only. The session token also works against Supabase directly, outside the API, so the database is what enforces read-only.

**The hook.** A custom access token hook (a database function Supabase calls on every token issue and refresh) checks the token's `session_id`. When the session is in `mcp_session` (list of handed-over sessions), it sets the token's `role` claim to `mcp_reader` (read-only database role; name proposed). Other sessions keep `authenticated`.

**The role.** `mcp_reader`:

- is granted to `authenticator` (the role Supabase's REST layer logs in as), so requests can switch to it;
- has `SELECT` on the tables and views retrieval reads, and no `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE`;
- has `EXECUTE` only on an allowlist: the search RPC, plus the access helpers that the policies and views call.

**Locking down functions.** `PUBLIC` (every database role) holds `EXECUTE` on every function, so the allowlist needs two changes:

- `REVOKE EXECUTE ON ALL FUNCTIONS IN SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC`;
- the matching default-privilege change, so new functions aren't executable by default either.

`anon` and `authenticated` keep their explicit grants. A test lists every function `mcp_reader` can execute and compares the list with the allowlist. Policies without a `TO` clause cover `mcp_reader`, so its reads follow the space account's current access.

**Supabase Auth acts on the space account, not on a database role.** The database role doesn't cover Auth requests. Two things follow:

- **Replacing the space login.** With only its session token, a handed-over session could ask Supabase Auth to set a new space login. That would lock out every plugin, and let the holder sign in again with sessions that aren't registered and can write. This change turns on the **space login lock**: the Supabase Auth settings `secure_password_change` and "require current password". Together they refuse any change that doesn't supply the current space login, which the holder never has.
- **Signing out the plugins.** A session could sign out the plugins' sessions. That's disruptive but not an escalation, because the plugins sign back in.

**A switched-off hook fails open.** Handed-over sessions would then get `authenticated`. The MCP refuses to start unless its session token carries `mcp_reader`, which catches a misconfigured project at setup.

**Revocation waits for token expiry.** Sign-out stops refresh, but the current session token stays valid for up to `jwt_expiry` (session token lifetime, 3600 s). The 2026-11-10 meeting accepted this.

**Alternative: plain Option A** (the agent signs in as the space account, with read-only enforced only in the MCP's tools). Any process holding the bundle could then write. The 2026-11-10 meeting chose A2 because the threat is overeager agent harnesses that bypass the MCP.

### 5. Nodes are CrossApp nodes, identified by `rid`

**Identifiers**

- **Nodes.** A node's ID is its `rid` (global node ID), built by `spaceUriAndLocalIdToRid`.
  - For an `http` space URI, it's `<space URI>/<localId>`.
  - Otherwise, it's `orn:<platform>.note:…/<localId>`.
  - Look nodes up by space and `localId`, never by `localId` alone.
- **Types.** A type's ID is its `rid`, from `getNodeTypeRid`, never the space-relative `nodeType`. Type filters take type `rid`s, and same-named types in different spaces stay separate.

**Payload**

- **Envelope.** Each operation returns `DbCrossAppNode`s (shared node format) in discovery's `{ nodes, spaces }` envelope.
- **Extra fields.** Each node gets a `typeRid`. Search also adds a `score` and an `excerpt`. There's no separate agent node type.
- **Title and body.** The title is `content.direct`. Get-node adds `content.full` (the body) as stored text or markdown, never rendered HTML.
- **Links and assets.** Source links stay as text. Assets aren't fetched, and no storage URLs are minted.
- **Provenance.** It's the `rid` plus its `spaces` entry. Nothing implies the node exists in the caller's vault.

**Gaps are errors**

- **Listings and search** skip rows the converter can't convert, as discovery does.
- **Get-node doesn't skip:**
  - `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID) returns `null` for a missing or unreadable node, which maps to `not_found`.
  - A conversion failure or a missing body maps to `content_unavailable`.
- A stored empty body is not a missing row.

**Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** an agent-specific payload keyed by `Concept.id` (internal database row ID), which no plugin uses. It would give each node a second identity.

### 6. Hybrid search, adapted from Supabase's recipe

Search adapts [Supabase's hybrid search recipe](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai/hybrid-search). The recipe is a SQL function to copy, not a built-in. It ranks rows two ways, keyword and semantic, then merges the two rankings with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), where each list adds `weight / (rrf_k + rank)` to a row's score.

**Embedding the query.** The API embeds the query on the server with `text-embedding-3-small` at 1536 dimensions. It uses the OpenAI client that `/api/embeddings/openai/small` builds inline today, extracted into a shared helper. Embedding happens only after the API has authenticated the caller. Neither the MCP nor a developer calls the embedding route.

**Schema addition.** Add a generated full-text column (`tsvector`, a keyword index) to `Content` for the `direct` and `direct_and_description` variants, plus a GIN index on it. Keyword and semantic matching then cover the same text. Use the `simple` text configuration, not `english`, because content isn't only English.

**The search RPC** (`SECURITY INVOKER`, so it runs as the caller) takes the query text, the query vector, optional type `rid`s and a limit.

- **Keyword list:** readable node instances whose text matches `websearch_to_tsquery`, ranked by `ts_rank_cd`.
- **Semantic list:** readable node instances with current, non-obsolete embeddings, ranked by cosine similarity.
- **Each list** applies the type filter and keeps each node's best row once, before taking up to twice the limit as candidates. This follows the recipe's cap.
- **Fusion:** RRF with the recipe's defaults (both weights 1, `rrf_k` 50), fixed in v0. Sort by fused score, then by `rid`, and apply the limit.
- **No relevance cutoff.** The semantic list includes every eligible embedded node up to the candidate cap, so weak matches can still appear.

`score` is the fused RRF score, not a similarity. `match_content_embeddings` (the existing semantic search query) stays unchanged.

**Other behavior**

- Nodes without a usable embedding can still match by keyword. Nodes with neither a match nor an embedding are absent from search, but the other operations still reach them.
- Embedding failures are errors, not empty results.

**The excerpt** is the first 300 Unicode code points of the body (`content.full`). When the body is missing, it falls back to `content.direct` (the title). The excerpt isn't evidence that the body matched.

**Alternative:** semantic search only. It needs no new column, but exact words such as names, acronyms and titles rank poorly when the embedding misses them. The recipe adds roughly a day or two, because the search RPC is being written anyway.

### 7. One-hop discourse context

Return each readable relation instance that touches the node, with:

- its `rid` (global node ID);
- its type;
- its direction;
- a summary of the connected node.

Rules:

- The relation, its type and both endpoints must be readable.
- Keep relations distinct even when they share a label.
- A self-link appears as both incoming and outgoing.
- Don't follow ordinary backlinks, and don't go past one hop.

### 8. API contract

| API route | MCP tool | Input |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}` | `get_node` | node `rid` |
| `POST /api/v1/nodes/search` | `search_nodes` | query, optional type `rid`s, optional limit |
| `GET /api/v1/node-types` | `get_node_types` | none |
| `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}/context` | `get_discourse_context` | node `rid` |

`rid`s (global node IDs) contain `/` and `:`, so they go URL-encoded in the path.

**Each route does three things:**

1. It validates the session token with Supabase Auth, then builds a request-scoped client that acts as the caller. Nothing is held between requests.
2. It validates the input with the shared Zod schemas (typed input and output definitions).
3. It calls one `packages/database` function.

**Any session token is accepted.** The API accepts any valid space-account session token: a plugin's own session, or a handed-over one. The API exposes only reads, and the database keeps handed-over sessions read-only (Decision 4), so the API doesn't check the role.

**Zod schemas.** The input and output schemas live in `packages/database`, so the API and the MCP share them:

- the API validates requests with them;
- the MCP generates its tool input definitions from them;
- the API docs are checked against them.

**Response envelope.** Every response carries a request ID, plus either `data` or an error object with a stable code and a safe message.

**Validation.** Reject the following with `invalid_request`:

- a blank query;
- a malformed `rid`;
- an explicitly empty type list;
- a limit outside 1-30.

The default limit is 10. Unknown type `rid`s match nothing.

**Error codes:**

| Code | HTTP status | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unauthenticated` | 401 | Token is missing, invalid or expired |
| `not_found` | 404 | Node is missing or unreadable |
| `content_unavailable` | 409 | Node lacks its body or can't be converted |
| `invalid_request` | 422 | Input fails validation |
| `result_too_large` | 422 | Response exceeds the budget |
| `dependency_error` | 503 | Database or embedding failure |

The two 422 errors are told apart by the code in the envelope. Errors are never returned as empty results.

**Response budget.** A response is either complete or fails with `result_too_large`. The proposed budget is 1 MiB serialized, to be validated in each client.

**Logs** hold only the request ID, operation, duration, result count and error category. They never include the `Authorization` header (which carries the session token), the query text or node bodies.

### 9. The local MCP

**Tools.**

- Each tool calls exactly one API operation.
- It returns the API's result as structured content, plus a short text form.
- It turns API errors into tool errors with the same code. An unreachable API is a `dependency_error`.
- Every tool is annotated read-only.

**Runtime.** Logs go to stderr, because stdout carries the MCP protocol.

**Session**

- **Connect.** `npx @discourse-graphs/mcp connect --name <name>` does the following:
  - reads the bundle from stdin;
  - refreshes once and checks that the role is `mcp_reader` (read-only database role);
  - writes the session to `~/.discourse-graphs/mcp/<name>.json` with mode 0600.

  The client config then holds only the launch command and `--name`, never a token.
- **Refresh.** The MCP refreshes against Supabase Auth. It writes each rotated refresh token to the state file atomically, before using the new session token. If the state file is lost, the user connects again with a new bundle.
- **One process per connection.** A lock file next to the state file stops a second process. Two processes refreshing the same token can make Supabase revoke the session. A user with two clients connects each one with its own bundle and `--name`.
- **Token for developers.** `npx @discourse-graphs/mcp token --name <name>` prints a current session token for that connection, refreshing it under the lock. A developer connects with their own bundle and never handles refresh-token rotation.

**Distribution and setup**

- **Package.** `@discourse-graphs/mcp` (name proposed), published to npm from `apps/mcp` with semver releases. Setup docs launch it with `npx -y @discourse-graphs/mcp@latest`.
- **Per-client setup** is documented for Claude Code (`claude mcp add`), Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`) and Codex (`~/.codex/config.toml`). The docs also cover:
  - the risk that the state file can read everything the space can read, and that any process running as the user can read it;
  - one bundle per client;
  - search limits;
  - sync-gap errors;
  - that ChatGPT is unsupported.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [The hook runs on every sign-in] → A failing hook blocks every token, including the plugins'. Keep it to one indexed lookup on `mcp_session`, return other claims unchanged, and test plugin sign-in and refresh with the hook on.
- [A switched-off hook fails open] → Handed-over sessions would get `authenticated`, which can write. The MCP's startup role check catches this. A harness that calls Supabase directly would still get a write-capable session.
- [A grant is missing from `mcp_reader`] → Retrieval fails or returns fewer rows. Cucumber scenarios run every operation as `mcp_reader`.
- [Revoking from `PUBLIC` breaks a function that relied on it] → Run the full cucumber suite as `anon` and `authenticated` after the revoke.
- [The MCP depends on the website] → If the website is down, MCP retrieval fails with `dependency_error`, and every call takes one extra network hop. Accepted in exchange for one contract and server-side fixes.
- [`/api/v1` is pinned by installed copies] → Change it only additively. A breaking change ships as `/api/v2` alongside `v1`.
- [Session tokens that can write pass through the website] → The API accepts plugin sessions too. Routes only read, and the `Authorization` header stays out of logs. A leaked token stays valid until it expires, up to one hour.
- [The full-text column adds write cost] → Every `Content` write for the two indexed variants updates the GIN index. That's small next to sync's embedding calls, but measure it on a large space.
- [The state file is readable by any process running as the user] → Accepted for v0, and stated in the setup docs.
- [One session reads one space] → A user with several spaces adds one MCP entry per space.
- [Embedding inputs differ by platform] → Document the difference. Test correctness with deterministic vector fixtures, and tune relevance once real queries exist.
- [Shared nodes look unfamiliar] → Label provenance as origin, and say that results reflect readable synced data, not local imports.

## Migration Plan

1. Land `mcp-session-access` (registry, handoff helper and connect command).
2. Add `mcp_reader`, the function allowlist and the access token hook, and turn on the space login lock. Enable the hook and the lock on the hosted project.
3. Add the full-text column and index, the retrieval functions and the search RPC through the declarative schema workflow. Existing RPCs and clients keep their behavior.
4. Deploy the API routes.
5. Build and publish the MCP.
6. Validate in Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex with Roam and Obsidian closed, then release to a limited cohort.

# Design

<!-- Supersedes the 2026-09-25 version of this change in Roam (block LPDwCRT6_). -->

## Context

These facts from `origin/main` shape the design.

**Identity and data**

- **Space accounts.** Plugins sign in as a per-space account with `signInWithPassword` (Supabase's sign-in call) in `packages/database/src/lib/contextFunctions.ts`. This spec calls that credential the **space login**. It is a random secret stored in the plugin; there are no personal user accounts yet. `mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/kPg_0_-lh)) adds the handoff and the `mcp_session` registry (list of handed-over sessions). None of it is in the repo yet.
- **Concepts and content.**
  - `Concept` (the node, type and relation table) holds node instances, schemas and relations, flagged by `is_schema` and `is_relation`.
  - `Content` (the text table) joins it on `(space_id, source_local_id)`. Its variants are `direct` (title), `direct_and_children`, `direct_and_description` (title plus description) and `full` (body).
- **Readability.** The `my_*` views (views filtered to what the caller can read), and helpers such as `in_space` and `can_view_specific_resource`, express read access.

**Discovery and embeddings**

- **Discovery.** [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091) made discovery return shared nodes.
  - `packages/database/src/lib/sharedNodes.ts` returns a `SharedNodeListing`: `{ nodes, spaces }` of `DbCrossAppNode` (shared node format).
  - `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID) reads one readable node by `rid` (global node ID).
  - `dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` converts nodes, node types and relations into that format.
  - Neither the listing nor the converter includes `content.full` (the body); import fetches it separately.
- **Embeddings.** `embedding.sql` stores 1536-dimension `text-embedding-3-small` vectors, each with an `obsolete` flag.
  - `match_content_embeddings` (the existing semantic search query) applies a similarity threshold and has no type filter.
  - Obsidian embeds the title (`direct`). Roam embeds the title plus description (`direct_and_description`) when there is a description, and the title alone otherwise.
  - The website embeds text with the team's OpenAI key (`/api/embeddings/openai/small`).
  - No full-text (keyword) index exists on `Content` today.

**Database access controls**

- **Row-level security.** 61 of the 65 row-level security policies have no `TO` clause, so they apply to every database role. The other four are `TO authenticated` on `storage.objects` (file storage), which retrieval doesn't read. Table grants go only to `authenticated` (the signed-in role) and `service_role`.
- **Function privileges.** `PUBLIC` (every database role) can execute every function in the `public` schema, because no schema file revokes that default. Some write functions are `SECURITY DEFINER` (they run as their owner, not as the caller), such as `create_secret_token` and `accept_group_invitation`. So table grants alone don't stop them.
- **Auth settings.** `config.toml` sets `jwt_expiry = 3600` (a session token lasts one hour). The custom access token hook is commented out.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:**

- One retrieval service: every client, the MCP included, goes through the API.
- Reuse existing data, vectors, converters and access rules.
- The database enforces the agent session's read-only access, not the MCP.
- Sync gaps are reported as errors, never as partial content.

**Non-Goals:**

- A new identity system.
- A hosted MCP.
- A second embedding pipeline.
- Attachment access.
- Auditing.

## Decisions

### 1. The API is the retrieval service; the MCP is its client

```
Roam / Obsidian --connect command--> bundle (shown once)
                                        |
             npx @discourse-graphs/mcp connect --> local state file
                                        |
agent client --stdio--> local MCP (thin client)
                            |
                            | HTTPS + session token
                            v
developer ----------> apps/website /api/v1 --+--> packages/database functions --> Supabase
                                             +--> OpenAI (search queries only)
```

Each capability spec covers one layer:

```
agent client --> MCP tools ----+     discourse-mcp: tools pass API results through
                               v
developer ---------------> API routes     headless-retrieval-api: HTTP, auth, envelope, versioning
                               |
                               v
              retrieval functions in packages/database
                                          discourse-retrieval: what the four operations return
```

- **The API holds all retrieval logic.** It is four routes in `apps/website`. They call `packages/database` functions with the caller's session, so row-level security applies.
- **The MCP** holds a session and maps each tool to one API call. It never reads the database or calls OpenAI.
- **Developers** call the same routes directly.

**The contract is `/api/v1`** (the versioned route prefix).
- Installed MCP copies can't be force-updated, so `/api/v1` changes only additively, and a breaking change needs `/api/v2`.
- Schema, query and converter fixes behind the API ship by deploying the website, without an MCP release.

**Alternatives:**
- **The MCP reads the database directly.**
  - Installed copies would then depend on view shapes, and every fix would need an MCP release.
  - The MCP would bundle database code and call an embedding route outside the API's auth.
  - The API and the MCP would be two adapters to keep in parity.
- **A hosted MCP in `apps/website` (the 2026-09-25 version).** It reaches ChatGPT but needs a hosted credential store. The 2026-11-10 meeting chose a local MCP. A hosted MCP can still wrap this API later.

### 2. Reuse the discovery read path

The API's routes call TypeScript functions in `packages/database`. These build on Sid's discovery code from [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091):

- **Get-node** calls `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID), then fetches the `full` Content (the body) the way import does.
- **Type discovery** reads node types from readable node instances and labels them with `dbNodeSchemasToCrossApp` (converts node types).
- **Discourse context** finds the readable relation instances that touch the node.
  - Candidates come from `refs`, the list of referenced IDs.
  - Direction comes from the `source` and `destination` keys of `reference_content` (the relation's endpoint map).
  - Relations are converted with `dbRelationsToCrossApp` (converts relations).

Only search needs a new RPC (database function); see Decision 6.

**Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** four new RPCs, which would duplicate the converters.

### 3. Hand over a session through `mcp-session-access`

`mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/kPg_0_-lh)) defines the handoff:

- **Handoff.**
  1. The plugin opens a new session for the space account, using a second client that neither persists nor auto-refreshes.
  2. It registers the session with `register_mcp_session(label)`.
  3. It shows the bundle once: Supabase URL, anon key, space ID and refresh token. It keeps no copy.
- **Registry.** `mcp_session` (list of handed-over sessions) records the session ID (taken from the caller's own token), the label, the space account and the creation time.
- **Sign-out.** The holder can sign itself out with local scope (only its own session). Per-session sign-out from the plugin is proposed for right after v0.
- **Emergency switch.** Until then, the cut-off is to sign out every other session of the space account. That also signs out the other plugin instances, which sign back in with the space login.
- **Who can connect.** Any plugin user of the space.

**Tokens.** Two tokens are involved:

- the **session token** is the session's short-lived access token, the one the API takes;
- the **refresh token** renews the session token, and it rotates on every use.

The bundle carries only the refresh token. So the holder's first session token comes from a refresh, and it already carries `mcp_reader` (read-only database role; Decision 4). The plugin discards the `authenticated` session token it used to register.

**Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** Option B, a separate agent account for each grant, with a credential issued from a website page. The 2026-11-10 meeting judged its security gain marginal for the extra work.

### 4. The database makes handed-over sessions read-only (A2)

Under Option A2 ([decision](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/guIcK3Z9M)), the agent signs in as the space account, but the database makes its session read-only. The session token also works against Supabase directly, outside the API, so the database is what enforces read-only.

**The hook.** A custom access token hook (a database function Supabase calls on every token issue and refresh) checks the token's `session_id`. When the session is in `mcp_session` (list of handed-over sessions), it sets the token's `role` claim to `mcp_reader` (read-only database role; name proposed). Other sessions keep `authenticated`.

**The role.** `mcp_reader`:

- is granted to `authenticator` (the role Supabase's REST layer logs in as), so requests can switch to it;
- has `SELECT` on the tables and views retrieval reads, and no `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE`;
- has `EXECUTE` only on an allowlist: the search RPC, plus the access helpers that the policies and views call.

**Locking down functions.** `PUBLIC` (every database role) holds `EXECUTE` on every function, so the allowlist needs two changes:

- `REVOKE EXECUTE ON ALL FUNCTIONS IN SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC`;
- the matching default-privilege change, so new functions aren't executable by default either.

`anon` and `authenticated` keep their explicit grants. A test lists every function `mcp_reader` can execute and compares the list with the allowlist. Policies without a `TO` clause cover `mcp_reader`, so its reads follow the space account's current access.

**Supabase Auth acts on the space account, not on a database role.** The database role doesn't cover Auth requests. Two things follow:

- **Replacing the space login.** With only its session token, a handed-over session could ask Supabase Auth to set a new space login. That would lock out every plugin, and let the holder sign in again with sessions that aren't registered and can write. This change turns on the **space login lock**: the Supabase Auth settings `secure_password_change` and "require current password". Together they refuse any change that doesn't supply the current space login, which the holder never has.
- **Signing out the plugins.** A session could sign out the plugins' sessions. That's disruptive but not an escalation, because the plugins sign back in.

**A switched-off hook fails open.** Handed-over sessions would then get `authenticated`. The MCP refuses to start unless its session token carries `mcp_reader`, which catches a misconfigured project at setup.

**Revocation waits for token expiry.** Sign-out stops refresh, but the current session token stays valid for up to `jwt_expiry` (session token lifetime, 3600 s). The 2026-11-10 meeting accepted this.

**Alternative: plain Option A** (the agent signs in as the space account, with read-only enforced only in the MCP's tools). Any process holding the bundle could then write. The 2026-11-10 meeting chose A2 because the threat is overeager agent harnesses that bypass the MCP.

### 5. Nodes are CrossApp nodes, identified by `rid`

**Identifiers**

- **Nodes.** A node's ID is its `rid` (global node ID), built by `spaceUriAndLocalIdToRid`.
  - For an `http` space URI, it's `<space URI>/<localId>`.
  - Otherwise, it's `orn:<platform>.note:…/<localId>`.
  - Look nodes up by space and `localId`, never by `localId` alone.
- **Types.** A type's ID is its `rid`, from `getNodeTypeRid`, never the space-relative `nodeType`. Type filters take type `rid`s, and same-named types in different spaces stay separate.

**Payload**

- **Envelope.** Each operation returns `DbCrossAppNode`s (shared node format) in discovery's `{ nodes, spaces }` envelope.
- **Extra fields.** Each node gets a `typeRid`. Search also adds a `score` and an `excerpt`. There's no separate agent node type.
- **Title and body.** The title is `content.direct`. Get-node adds `content.full` (the body) as stored text or markdown, never rendered HTML.
- **Links and assets.** Source links stay as text. Assets aren't fetched, and no storage URLs are minted.
- **Provenance.** It's the `rid` plus its `spaces` entry. Nothing implies the node exists in the caller's vault.

**Gaps are errors**

- **Listings and search** skip rows the converter can't convert, as discovery does.
- **Get-node doesn't skip:**
  - `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID) returns `null` for a missing or unreadable node, which maps to `not_found`.
  - A conversion failure or a missing body maps to `content_unavailable`.
- A stored empty body is not a missing row.

**Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** an agent-specific payload keyed by `Concept.id` (internal database row ID), which no plugin uses. It would give each node a second identity.

### 6. Hybrid search, adapted from Supabase's recipe

Search adapts [Supabase's hybrid search recipe](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai/hybrid-search). The recipe is a SQL function to copy, not a built-in. It ranks rows two ways, keyword and semantic, then merges the two rankings with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), where each list adds `weight / (rrf_k + rank)` to a row's score.

**Embedding the query.** The API embeds the query on the server with `text-embedding-3-small` at 1536 dimensions. It uses the OpenAI client that `/api/embeddings/openai/small` builds inline today, extracted into a shared helper. Embedding happens only after the API has authenticated the caller. Neither the MCP nor a developer calls the embedding route.

**Schema addition.** Add a generated full-text column (`tsvector`, a keyword index) to `Content` for the `direct` and `direct_and_description` variants, plus a GIN index on it. Keyword and semantic matching then cover the same text. Use the `simple` text configuration, not `english`, because content isn't only English.

**The search RPC** (`SECURITY INVOKER`, so it runs as the caller) takes the query text, the query vector, optional type `rid`s and a limit.

- **Keyword list:** readable node instances whose text matches `websearch_to_tsquery`, ranked by `ts_rank_cd`.
- **Semantic list:** readable node instances with current, non-obsolete embeddings, ranked by cosine similarity.
- **Each list** applies the type filter and keeps each node's best row once, before taking up to twice the limit as candidates. This follows the recipe's cap.
- **Fusion:** RRF with the recipe's defaults (both weights 1, `rrf_k` 50), fixed in v0. Sort by fused score, then by `rid`, and apply the limit.
- **No relevance cutoff.** The semantic list includes every eligible embedded node up to the candidate cap, so weak matches can still appear.

`score` is the fused RRF score, not a similarity. `match_content_embeddings` (the existing semantic search query) stays unchanged.

**Other behavior**

- Nodes without a usable embedding can still match by keyword. Nodes with neither a match nor an embedding are absent from search, but the other operations still reach them.
- Embedding failures are errors, not empty results.

**The excerpt** is the first 300 Unicode code points of the body (`content.full`). When the body is missing, it falls back to `content.direct` (the title). The excerpt isn't evidence that the body matched.

**Alternative:** semantic search only. It needs no new column, but exact words such as names, acronyms and titles rank poorly when the embedding misses them. The recipe adds roughly a day or two, because the search RPC is being written anyway.

### 7. One-hop discourse context

Return each readable relation instance that touches the node, with:

- its `rid` (global node ID);
- its type;
- its direction;
- a summary of the connected node.

Rules:

- The relation, its type and both endpoints must be readable.
- Keep relations distinct even when they share a label.
- A self-link appears as both incoming and outgoing.
- Don't follow ordinary backlinks, and don't go past one hop.

### 8. API contract

| API route | MCP tool | Input |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}` | `get_node` | node `rid` |
| `POST /api/v1/nodes/search` | `search_nodes` | query, optional type `rid`s, optional limit |
| `GET /api/v1/node-types` | `get_node_types` | none |
| `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}/context` | `get_discourse_context` | node `rid` |

`rid`s (global node IDs) contain `/` and `:`, so they go URL-encoded in the path.

**Each route does three things:**

1. It validates the session token with Supabase Auth, then builds a request-scoped client that acts as the caller. Nothing is held between requests.
2. It validates the input with the shared Zod schemas (typed input and output definitions).
3. It calls one `packages/database` function.

**Any session token is accepted.** The API accepts any valid space-account session token: a plugin's own session, or a handed-over one. The API exposes only reads, and the database keeps handed-over sessions read-only (Decision 4), so the API doesn't check the role.

**Zod schemas.** The input and output schemas live in `packages/database`, so the API and the MCP share them:

- the API validates requests with them;
- the MCP generates its tool input definitions from them;
- the API docs are checked against them.

**Response envelope.** Every response carries a request ID, plus either `data` or an error object with a stable code and a safe message.

**Validation.** Reject the following with `invalid_request`:

- a blank query;
- a malformed `rid`;
- an explicitly empty type list;
- a limit outside 1-30.

The default limit is 10. Unknown type `rid`s match nothing.

**Error codes:**

| Code | HTTP status | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unauthenticated` | 401 | Token is missing, invalid or expired |
| `not_found` | 404 | Node is missing or unreadable |
| `content_unavailable` | 409 | Node lacks its body or can't be converted |
| `invalid_request` | 422 | Input fails validation |
| `result_too_large` | 422 | Response exceeds the budget |
| `dependency_error` | 503 | Database or embedding failure |

The two 422 errors are told apart by the code in the envelope. Errors are never returned as empty results.

**Response budget.** A response is either complete or fails with `result_too_large`. The proposed budget is 1 MiB serialized, to be validated in each client.

**Logs** hold only the request ID, operation, duration, result count and error category. They never include the `Authorization` header (which carries the session token), the query text or node bodies.

### 9. The local MCP

**Tools.**

- Each tool calls exactly one API operation.
- It returns the API's result as structured content, plus a short text form.
- It turns API errors into tool errors with the same code. An unreachable API is a `dependency_error`.
- Every tool is annotated read-only.

**Runtime.** Logs go to stderr, because stdout carries the MCP protocol.

**Session**

- **Connect.** `npx @discourse-graphs/mcp connect --name <name>` does the following:
  - reads the bundle from stdin;
  - refreshes once and checks that the role is `mcp_reader` (read-only database role);
  - writes the session to `~/.discourse-graphs/mcp/<name>.json` with mode 0600.

  The client config then holds only the launch command and `--name`, never a token.
- **Refresh.** The MCP refreshes against Supabase Auth. It writes each rotated refresh token to the state file atomically, before using the new session token. If the state file is lost, the user connects again with a new bundle.
- **One process per connection.** A lock file next to the state file stops a second process. Two processes refreshing the same token can make Supabase revoke the session. A user with two clients connects each one with its own bundle and `--name`.
- **Token for developers.** `npx @discourse-graphs/mcp token --name <name>` prints a current session token for that connection, refreshing it under the lock. A developer connects with their own bundle and never handles refresh-token rotation.

**Distribution and setup**

- **Package.** `@discourse-graphs/mcp` (name proposed), published to npm from `apps/mcp` with semver releases. Setup docs launch it with `npx -y @discourse-graphs/mcp@latest`.
- **Per-client setup** is documented for Claude Code (`claude mcp add`), Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`) and Codex (`~/.codex/config.toml`). The docs also cover:
  - the risk that the state file can read everything the space can read, and that any process running as the user can read it;
  - one bundle per client;
  - search limits;
  - sync-gap errors;
  - that ChatGPT is unsupported.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [The hook runs on every sign-in] → A failing hook blocks every token, including the plugins'. Keep it to one indexed lookup on `mcp_session`, return other claims unchanged, and test plugin sign-in and refresh with the hook on.
- [A switched-off hook fails open] → Handed-over sessions would get `authenticated`, which can write. The MCP's startup role check catches this. A harness that calls Supabase directly would still get a write-capable session.
- [A grant is missing from `mcp_reader`] → Retrieval fails or returns fewer rows. Cucumber scenarios run every operation as `mcp_reader`.
- [Revoking from `PUBLIC` breaks a function that relied on it] → Run the full cucumber suite as `anon` and `authenticated` after the revoke.
- [The MCP depends on the website] → If the website is down, MCP retrieval fails with `dependency_error`, and every call takes one extra network hop. Accepted in exchange for one contract and server-side fixes.
- [`/api/v1` is pinned by installed copies] → Change it only additively. A breaking change ships as `/api/v2` alongside `v1`.
- [Session tokens that can write pass through the website] → The API accepts plugin sessions too. Routes only read, and the `Authorization` header stays out of logs. A leaked token stays valid until it expires, up to one hour.
- [The full-text column adds write cost] → Every `Content` write for the two indexed variants updates the GIN index. That's small next to sync's embedding calls, but measure it on a large space.
- [The state file is readable by any process running as the user] → Accepted for v0, and stated in the setup docs.
- [One session reads one space] → A user with several spaces adds one MCP entry per space.
- [Embedding inputs differ by platform] → Document the difference. Test correctness with deterministic vector fixtures, and tune relevance once real queries exist.
- [Shared nodes look unfamiliar] → Label provenance as origin, and say that results reflect readable synced data, not local imports.

## Migration Plan

1. Land `mcp-session-access` (registry, handoff helper and connect command).
2. Add `mcp_reader`, the function allowlist and the access token hook, and turn on the space login lock. Enable the hook and the lock on the hosted project.
3. Add the full-text column and index, the retrieval functions and the search RPC through the declarative schema workflow. Existing RPCs and clients keep their behavior.
4. Deploy the API routes.
5. Build and publish the MCP.
6. Validate in Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex with Roam and Obsidian closed, then release to a limited cohort.
7. To roll back, deprecate the npm package, disable the routes and sign out the registered sessions. The additive role, column, functions and RPC can stay.

## Open Questions

- Whether one agent should span several spaces.
- Example queries for the docs, and a relevance evaluation set. Neither changes the architecture.

  - The MCP would bundle database code and call an embedding route outside the API's auth.
  - The API and the MCP would be two adapters to keep in parity.
- **A hosted MCP in `apps/website` (the 2026-09-25 version).** It reaches ChatGPT but needs a hosted credential store. The 2026-11-10 meeting chose a local MCP. A hosted MCP can still wrap this API later.

### 2. Reuse the discovery read path

The API's routes call TypeScript functions in `packages/database`. These build on Sid's discovery code from [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091):

- **Get-node** calls `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID), then fetches the `full` Content (the body) the way import does.
- **Type discovery** reads node types from readable node instances and labels them with `dbNodeSchemasToCrossApp` (converts node types).
- **Discourse context** finds the readable relation instances that touch the node.
  - Candidates come from `refs`, the list of referenced IDs.
  - Direction comes from the `source` and `destination` keys of `reference_content` (the relation's endpoint map).
  - Relations are converted with `dbRelationsToCrossApp` (converts relations).

Only search needs a new RPC (database function); see Decision 6.

**Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** four new RPCs, which would duplicate the converters.

### 3. Hand over a session through `mcp-session-access`

`mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/kPg_0_-lh)) defines the handoff:

- **Handoff.**
  1. The plugin opens a new session for the space account, using a second client that neither persists nor auto-refreshes.
  2. It registers the session with `register_mcp_session(label)`.
  3. It shows the bundle once: Supabase URL, anon key, space ID and refresh token. It keeps no copy.
- **Registry.** `mcp_session` (list of handed-over sessions) records the session ID (taken from the caller's own token), the label, the space account and the creation time.
- **Sign-out.** The holder can sign itself out with local scope (only its own session). Per-session sign-out from the plugin is proposed for right after v0.
- **Emergency switch.** Until then, the cut-off is to sign out every other session of the space account. That also signs out the other plugin instances, which sign back in with the space login.
- **Who can connect.** Any plugin user of the space.

**Tokens.** Two tokens are involved:

- the **session token** is the session's short-lived access token, the one the API takes;
- the **refresh token** renews the session token, and it rotates on every use.

The bundle carries only the refresh token. So the holder's first session token comes from a refresh, and it already carries `mcp_reader` (read-only database role; Decision 4). The plugin discards the `authenticated` session token it used to register.

**Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** Option B, a separate agent account for each grant, with a credential issued from a website page. The 2026-11-10 meeting judged its security gain marginal for the extra work.

### 4. The database makes handed-over sessions read-only (A2)

Under Option A2 ([decision](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/guIcK3Z9M)), the agent signs in as the space account, but the database makes its session read-only. The session token also works against Supabase directly, outside the API, so the database is what enforces read-only.

**The hook.** A custom access token hook (a database function Supabase calls on every token issue and refresh) checks the token's `session_id`. When the session is in `mcp_session` (list of handed-over sessions), it sets the token's `role` claim to `mcp_reader` (read-only database role; name proposed). Other sessions keep `authenticated`.

**The role.** `mcp_reader`:

- is granted to `authenticator` (the role Supabase's REST layer logs in as), so requests can switch to it;
- has `SELECT` on the tables and views retrieval reads, and no `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE`;
- has `EXECUTE` only on an allowlist: the search RPC, plus the access helpers that the policies and views call.

**Locking down functions.** `PUBLIC` (every database role) holds `EXECUTE` on every function, so the allowlist needs two changes:

- `REVOKE EXECUTE ON ALL FUNCTIONS IN SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC`;
- the matching default-privilege change, so new functions aren't executable by default either.

`anon` and `authenticated` keep their explicit grants. A test lists every function `mcp_reader` can execute and compares the list with the allowlist. Policies without a `TO` clause cover `mcp_reader`, so its reads follow the space account's current access.

**Supabase Auth acts on the space account, not on a database role.** The database role doesn't cover Auth requests. Two things follow:

- **Replacing the space login.** With only its session token, a handed-over session could ask Supabase Auth to set a new space login. That would lock out every plugin, and let the holder sign in again with sessions that aren't registered and can write. This change turns on the **space login lock**: the Supabase Auth settings `secure_password_change` and "require current password". Together they refuse any change that doesn't supply the current space login, which the holder never has.
- **Signing out the plugins.** A session could sign out the plugins' sessions. That's disruptive but not an escalation, because the plugins sign back in.

**A switched-off hook fails open.** Handed-over sessions would then get `authenticated`. The MCP refuses to start unless its session token carries `mcp_reader`, which catches a misconfigured project at setup.

**Revocation waits for token expiry.** Sign-out stops refresh, but the current session token stays valid for up to `jwt_expiry` (session token lifetime, 3600 s). The 2026-11-10 meeting accepted this.

**Alternative: plain Option A** (the agent signs in as the space account, with read-only enforced only in the MCP's tools). Any process holding the bundle could then write. The 2026-11-10 meeting chose A2 because the threat is overeager agent harnesses that bypass the MCP.

### 5. Nodes are CrossApp nodes, identified by `rid`

**Identifiers**

- **Nodes.** A node's ID is its `rid` (global node ID), built by `spaceUriAndLocalIdToRid`.
  - For an `http` space URI, it's `<space URI>/<localId>`.
  - Otherwise, it's `orn:<platform>.note:…/<localId>`.
  - Look nodes up by space and `localId`, never by `localId` alone.
- **Types.** A type's ID is its `rid`, from `getNodeTypeRid`, never the space-relative `nodeType`. Type filters take type `rid`s, and same-named types in different spaces stay separate.

**Payload**

- **Envelope.** Each operation returns `DbCrossAppNode`s (shared node format) in discovery's `{ nodes, spaces }` envelope.
- **Extra fields.** Each node gets a `typeRid`. Search also adds a `score` and an `excerpt`. There's no separate agent node type.
- **Title and body.** The title is `content.direct`. Get-node adds `content.full` (the body) as stored text or markdown, never rendered HTML.
- **Links and assets.** Source links stay as text. Assets aren't fetched, and no storage URLs are minted.
- **Provenance.** It's the `rid` plus its `spaces` entry. Nothing implies the node exists in the caller's vault.

**Gaps are errors**

- **Listings and search** skip rows the converter can't convert, as discovery does.
- **Get-node doesn't skip:**
  - `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID) returns `null` for a missing or unreadable node, which maps to `not_found`.
  - A conversion failure or a missing body maps to `content_unavailable`.
- A stored empty body is not a missing row.

**Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** an agent-specific payload keyed by `Concept.id` (internal database row ID), which no plugin uses. It would give each node a second identity.

### 6. Hybrid search, adapted from Supabase's recipe

Search adapts [Supabase's hybrid search recipe](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai/hybrid-search). The recipe is a SQL function to copy, not a built-in. It ranks rows two ways, keyword and semantic, then merges the two rankings with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), where each list adds `weight / (rrf_k + rank)` to a row's score.

**Embedding the query.** The API embeds the query on the server with `text-embedding-3-small` at 1536 dimensions. It uses the OpenAI client that `/api/embeddings/openai/small` builds inline today, extracted into a shared helper. Embedding happens only after the API has authenticated the caller. Neither the MCP nor a developer calls the embedding route.

**Schema addition.** Add a generated full-text column (`tsvector`, a keyword index) to `Content` for the `direct` and `direct_and_description` variants, plus a GIN index on it. Keyword and semantic matching then cover the same text. Use the `simple` text configuration, not `english`, because content isn't only English.

**The search RPC** (`SECURITY INVOKER`, so it runs as the caller) takes the query text, the query vector, optional type `rid`s and a limit.

- **Keyword list:** readable node instances whose text matches `websearch_to_tsquery`, ranked by `ts_rank_cd`.
- **Semantic list:** readable node instances with current, non-obsolete embeddings, ranked by cosine similarity.
- **Each list** applies the type filter and keeps each node's best row once, before taking up to twice the limit as candidates. This follows the recipe's cap.
- **Fusion:** RRF with the recipe's defaults (both weights 1, `rrf_k` 50), fixed in v0. Sort by fused score, then by `rid`, and apply the limit.
- **No relevance cutoff.** The semantic list includes every eligible embedded node up to the candidate cap, so weak matches can still appear.

`score` is the fused RRF score, not a similarity. `match_content_embeddings` (the existing semantic search query) stays unchanged.

**Other behavior**

- Nodes without a usable embedding can still match by keyword. Nodes with neither a match nor an embedding are absent from search, but the other operations still reach them.
- Embedding failures are errors, not empty results.

**The excerpt** is the first 300 Unicode code points of the body (`content.full`). When the body is missing, it falls back to `content.direct` (the title). The excerpt isn't evidence that the body matched.

**Alternative:** semantic search only. It needs no new column, but exact words such as names, acronyms and titles rank poorly when the embedding misses them. The recipe adds roughly a day or two, because the search RPC is being written anyway.

### 7. One-hop discourse context

Return each readable relation instance that touches the node, with:

- its `rid` (global node ID);
- its type;
- its direction;
- a summary of the connected node.

Rules:

- The relation, its type and both endpoints must be readable.
- Keep relations distinct even when they share a label.
- A self-link appears as both incoming and outgoing.
- Don't follow ordinary backlinks, and don't go past one hop.

### 8. API contract

| API route | MCP tool | Input |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}` | `get_node` | node `rid` |
| `POST /api/v1/nodes/search` | `search_nodes` | query, optional type `rid`s, optional limit |
| `GET /api/v1/node-types` | `get_node_types` | none |
| `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}/context` | `get_discourse_context` | node `rid` |

`rid`s (global node IDs) contain `/` and `:`, so they go URL-encoded in the path.

**Each route does three things:**

1. It validates the session token with Supabase Auth, then builds a request-scoped client that acts as the caller. Nothing is held between requests.
2. It validates the input with the shared Zod schemas (typed input and output definitions).
3. It calls one `packages/database` function.

**Any session token is accepted.** The API accepts any valid space-account session token: a plugin's own session, or a handed-over one. The API exposes only reads, and the database keeps handed-over sessions read-only (Decision 4), so the API doesn't check the role.

**Zod schemas.** The input and output schemas live in `packages/database`, so the API and the MCP share them:

- the API validates requests with them;
- the MCP generates its tool input definitions from them;
- the API docs are checked against them.

**Response envelope.** Every response carries a request ID, plus either `data` or an error object with a stable code and a safe message.

**Validation.** Reject the following with `invalid_request`:

- a blank query;
- a malformed `rid`;
- an explicitly empty type list;
- a limit outside 1-30.

The default limit is 10. Unknown type `rid`s match nothing.

**Error codes:**

| Code | HTTP status | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unauthenticated` | 401 | Token is missing, invalid or expired |
| `not_found` | 404 | Node is missing or unreadable |
| `content_unavailable` | 409 | Node lacks its body or can't be converted |
| `invalid_request` | 422 | Input fails validation |
| `result_too_large` | 422 | Response exceeds the budget |
| `dependency_error` | 503 | Database or embedding failure |

The two 422 errors are told apart by the code in the envelope. Errors are never returned as empty results.

**Response budget.** A response is either complete or fails with `result_too_large`. The proposed budget is 1 MiB serialized, to be validated in each client.

**Logs** hold only the request ID, operation, duration, result count and error category. They never include the `Authorization` header (which carries the session token), the query text or node bodies.

### 9. The local MCP

**Tools.**

- Each tool calls exactly one API operation.
- It returns the API's result as structured content, plus a short text form.
- It turns API errors into tool errors with the same code. An unreachable API is a `dependency_error`.
- Every tool is annotated read-only.

**Runtime.** Logs go to stderr, because stdout carries the MCP protocol.

**Session**

- **Connect.** `npx @discourse-graphs/mcp connect --name <name>` does the following:
  - reads the bundle from stdin;
  - refreshes once and checks that the role is `mcp_reader` (read-only database role);
  - writes the session to `~/.discourse-graphs/mcp/<name>.json` with mode 0600.

  The client config then holds only the launch command and `--name`, never a token.
- **Refresh.** The MCP refreshes against Supabase Auth. It writes each rotated refresh token to the state file atomically, before using the new session token. If the state file is lost, the user connects again with a new bundle.
- **One process per connection.** A lock file next to the state file stops a second process. Two processes refreshing the same token can make Supabase revoke the session. A user with two clients connects each one with its own bundle and `--name`.
- **Token for developers.** `npx @discourse-graphs/mcp token --name <name>` prints a current session token for that connection, refreshing it under the lock. A developer connects with their own bundle and never handles refresh-token rotation.

**Distribution and setup**

- **Package.** `@discourse-graphs/mcp` (name proposed), published to npm from `apps/mcp` with semver releases. Setup docs launch it with `npx -y @discourse-graphs/mcp@latest`.
- **Per-client setup** is documented for Claude Code (`claude mcp add`), Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`) and Codex (`~/.codex/config.toml`). The docs also cover:
  - the risk that the state file can read everything the space can read, and that any process running as the user can read it;
  - one bundle per client;
  - search limits;
  - sync-gap errors;
  - that ChatGPT is unsupported.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [The hook runs on every sign-in] → A failing hook blocks every token, including the plugins'. Keep it to one indexed lookup on `mcp_session`, return other claims unchanged, and test plugin sign-in and refresh with the hook on.
- [A switched-off hook fails open] → Handed-over sessions would get `authenticated`, which can write. The MCP's startup role check catches this. A harness that calls Supabase directly would still get a write-capable session.
- [A grant is missing from `mcp_reader`] → Retrieval fails or returns fewer rows. Cucumber scenarios run every operation as `mcp_reader`.
- [Revoking from `PUBLIC` breaks a function that relied on it] → Run the full cucumber suite as `anon` and `authenticated` after the revoke.
- [The MCP depends on the website] → If the website is down, MCP retrieval fails with `dependency_error`, and every call takes one extra network hop. Accepted in exchange for one contract and server-side fixes.
- [`/api/v1` is pinned by installed copies] → Change it only additively. A breaking change ships as `/api/v2` alongside `v1`.
- [Session tokens that can write pass through the website] → The API accepts plugin sessions too. Routes only read, and the `Authorization` header stays out of logs. A leaked token stays valid until it expires, up to one hour.
- [The full-text column adds write cost] → Every `Content` write for the two indexed variants updates the GIN index. That's small next to sync's embedding calls, but measure it on a large space.
- [The state file is readable by any process running as the user] → Accepted for v0, and stated in the setup docs.
- [One session reads one space] → A user with several spaces adds one MCP entry per space.
- [Embedding inputs differ by platform] → Document the difference. Test correctness with deterministic vector fixtures, and tune relevance once real queries exist.
- [Shared nodes look unfamiliar] → Label provenance as origin, and say that results reflect readable synced data, not local imports.

## Migration Plan

1. Land `mcp-session-access` (registry, handoff helper and connect command).
2. Add `mcp_reader`, the function allowlist and the access token hook, and turn on the space login lock. Enable the hook and the lock on the hosted project.
3. Add the full-text column and index, the retrieval functions and the search RPC through the declarative schema workflow. Existing RPCs and clients keep their behavior.
4. Deploy the API routes.
5. Build and publish the MCP.
6. Validate in Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex with Roam and Obsidian closed, then release to a limited cohort.
7. To roll back, deprecate the npm package, disable the routes and sign out the registered sessions. The additive role, column, functions and RPC can stay.
