- # Proposal
  - ## Why
    - Users want to retrieve relevant synced discourse nodes from their agent, or from their own code, without opening Roam or Obsidian, and without a separate integration for each platform. This v0 ships a retrieval API and a local MCP that exposes that API to agent clients. The MCP uses a read-only session of the space account, handed over by the plugin.
  - ## What Changes
    - **A retrieval API** at `/api/v1` (versioned HTTP routes) in `apps/website`, with four read-only operations: get a node, search nodes, list node types, and get discourse context. It is the one retrieval service: documented for developers, and the only backend of the MCP.
    - **A local MCP** that exposes each API operation as a tool. Users install it from npm, and the agent client launches it. Supported clients: Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex.
    - **Identity follows Option A2** ([decision](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/guIcK3Z9M), [options compared](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/bTMUCrCnD)): the agent signs in as the space account, but the database makes its session read-only. It was decided at the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product meeting. The session is handed over through `mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/kPg_0_-lh)).
    - **Coverage.** Retrieval covers every synced discourse node the space account can read under its current access, including shared nodes that were never imported into the client.
    - **Node shape.** Nodes come back as `DbCrossAppNode`s (the shared node format from [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091)), identified by `rid` (global node ID). They reuse discovery's converters and its `{ nodes, spaces }` envelope. Node types are identified by type `rid`.
    - **Search is hybrid.** It combines keyword matching with the stored embeddings, adapting [Supabase's hybrid search recipe](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai/hybrid-search). It supports type filtering and applies no relevance cutoff.
  - ## Capabilities
    - ### New Capabilities
      - `discourse-retrieval`: **what the API's four operations return.** Covers which nodes are eligible, node payloads, hybrid search, type discovery and one-hop discourse context.
      - `headless-retrieval-api`: **how callers reach those operations.** Covers the HTTP routes, session auth, the response envelope and the versioned contract.
      - `discourse-mcp`: **how agent clients reach the API.** Covers four tools that pass API results through, plus setup and distribution.
      - `agent-read-access`: **the session an agent holds.** It is handed over by the plugin, reads with the space account's current access, and the database keeps it read-only.
    - ### Modified Capabilities
      - None. The repository has no OpenSpec capability specs yet.
  - ## Out of scope for v0
    - A hosted MCP and ChatGPT support. ChatGPT can't launch a local MCP; a hosted MCP can later wrap the same API.
    - Option B, a separate agent account.
    - Writes, candidate nodes, non-discourse content, canvas functions, and attachment contents.
    - Multi-hop traversal, re-embedding, pagination, relevance thresholds, and imported-only filtering.
    - One session that spans several spaces.
  - ## Impact
    - **`packages/database`:**
      - `mcp_reader` (read-only database role);
      - a custom access token hook (assigns that role at sign-in);
      - an `EXECUTE` allowlist (which database functions the role may call);
      - the space login lock (stops a session from replacing the space login);
      - retrieval functions built on the discovery converters;
      - one hybrid search RPC (database function), plus a full-text column and index.
    - **`apps/website`:** the four API routes and their documentation.
    - **A new MCP package** (`apps/mcp`, location proposed), published to npm.
    - **Hosted Supabase settings:** the access token hook and the space login lock (design Decision 4).
    - **Depends on `mcp-session-access`** (the [session handoff spec](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/kPg_0_-lh)) for the handoff, the `mcp_session` registry (list of handed-over sessions) and sign-out.
    - **Builds on** [ENG-1985](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1985) (database-to-node converter) and [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091) (discovery returns shared nodes), both merged. They provide `dbNodeToCrossApp` (converts one node), `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID) and `SharedNodeListing` (nodes plus their spaces).
  - ## Open decisions
    - Whether one agent should span several spaces.
    - Michael hasn't confirmed reusing `CrossAppNode` (the shared node format) and `rid` (global node ID) for the agent API ([Roam block](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/SRa9xHk30)).
    - No relevance or latency target is agreed, and the real-query evaluation set doesn't exist yet.

# Proposal

- **Node shape.** Nodes come back as `DbCrossAppNode`s (the shared node format from [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091)), identified by `rid` (global node ID). They reuse discovery's converters and its `{ nodes, spaces }` envelope. Node types are identified by type `rid`.
- **Search is hybrid.** It combines keyword matching with the stored embeddings, adapting [Supabase's hybrid search recipe](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai/hybrid-search). It supports type filtering and applies no relevance cutoff.

### New Capabilities

- `discourse-retrieval`: **what the API's four operations return.** Covers which nodes are eligible, node payloads, hybrid search, type discovery and one-hop discourse context.
- `headless-retrieval-api`: **how callers reach those operations.** Covers the HTTP routes, session auth, the response envelope and the versioned contract.
- `discourse-mcp`: **how agent clients reach the API.** Covers four tools that pass API results through, plus setup and distribution.
- `agent-read-access`: **the session an agent holds.** It is handed over by the plugin, reads with the space account's current access, and the database keeps it read-only.

### Modified Capabilities

- None. The repository has no OpenSpec capability specs yet.

## Out of scope for v0

- A hosted MCP and ChatGPT support. ChatGPT can't launch a local MCP; a hosted MCP can later wrap the same API.
- Option B, a separate agent account.
- Writes, candidate nodes, non-discourse content, canvas functions, and attachment contents.
- Multi-hop traversal, re-embedding, pagination, relevance thresholds, and imported-only filtering.

  - a custom access token hook (assigns that role at sign-in);

# Spec Delta

## Purpose

What the API's four retrieval operations return, whichever client calls them: which nodes are eligible, node payloads, hybrid search, type discovery, and one-hop discourse context. All of it stays within the caller's current read access. The API exposes these operations over HTTP (`headless-retrieval-api`), and the MCP passes their results through (`discourse-mcp`).

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Readable synced collection <!-- roam:RfGa1ASkz -->

All retrieval operations SHALL use already-synced discourse data readable by the caller's space account. Local import status and authorship SHALL NOT restrict that collection. Results MUST NOT imply that the returned nodes were imported into the client application.

#### Scenario: Readable but unimported node

- **GIVEN** a synced discourse node is readable by the caller, but was authored elsewhere and never imported into its client
- **WHEN** the caller fetches it or searches for it
- **THEN** the node is eligible for retrieval and search ranking
- **AND** the response does not claim the node was imported locally

#### Scenario: Unreadable node

- **WHEN** a caller requests a node it cannot read
- **THEN** retrieval returns neither the node's content nor its metadata

### Requirement: Nodes and types are identified by rid

Every operation SHALL identify a node by its `rid` (global node ID), and a node type by the type's `rid`. Type filters SHALL take type `rid`s. Types with the same name in different spaces SHALL stay separate.

#### Scenario: Same-named types in two spaces

- **GIVEN** two readable spaces each define a type named "Claim"
- **WHEN** the caller discovers node types
- **THEN** it sees two types with different `rid`s

### Requirement: Full node text <!-- roam:M6O5NmufQ -->

Getting a readable node SHALL return the following:

- its `rid` (global node ID);
- its title;
- its type `rid`;
- its full synced text body;
- its provenance.

The body SHALL be the stored synced text, not content fetched live from the client application. Attachment downloads and file contents SHALL stay outside this operation.

#### Scenario: Get a node with body text and attachment links

- **WHEN** a caller fetches a readable synced node whose text links to an attachment
- **THEN** it receives the required node fields and the full stored text, including the source links in that text
- **AND** the response doesn't download or embed the attachment's file contents

### Requirement: Hybrid search over titles and descriptions <!-- roam:Mcp8fO0Ya -->

Search SHALL rank nodes by combining keyword matching with the stored embeddings, including Roam's title-plus-description embeddings, without re-embedding. Both SHALL cover the same text: the title, plus the description where one exists. Neither promises full-body coverage.

#### Scenario: Matching by meaning

- **WHEN** a caller submits a query, and eligible nodes have current embeddings
- **THEN** a node can rank even when its title lacks the query's exact words

#### Scenario: Matching an exact word

- **GIVEN** a readable node whose title contains a rare term, such as an acronym
- **WHEN** a caller searches for that term
- **THEN** the node ranks among the results, even if its embedding is a weak match

#### Scenario: Existing title-plus-description embedding

- **GIVEN** a readable Roam node has an embedding generated from its title and description
- **WHEN** the caller searches
- **THEN** that embedding contributes to ranking

#### Scenario: Body-only changes

- **GIVEN** the title, description, permissions and filters are unchanged
- **WHEN** only a node's full synced body changes
- **THEN** the node's search ranking doesn't change

### Requirement: Search result fields

Each search result SHALL contain the node's `rid` (global node ID), title, type `rid`, a short excerpt, provenance and a relevance score. Results SHALL be ordered by relevance.

#### Scenario: Result fields

- **WHEN** a search returns results
- **THEN** each result has those fields, and the results are ordered by score

### Requirement: Bounded search without a relevance cutoff <!-- roam:C7DJ2nVgj -->

Search SHALL default to 10 results and accept a limit from 1 to 30. A limit outside that range SHALL be rejected. V0 SHALL NOT paginate. Search SHALL NOT discard eligible nodes because their relevance is low. An empty result SHALL mean that no searchable nodes meet the access and type constraints.

#### Scenario: Default and explicit limits

- **GIVEN** at least 30 eligible searchable nodes
- **WHEN** the caller searches without a limit, and then with a limit of 20
- **THEN** the responses contain 10 results and 20 results
- **AND** neither response offers a continuation page

#### Scenario: Weak matches

- **GIVEN** three eligible searchable nodes that match the query weakly, and a limit of 10
- **WHEN** the caller searches
- **THEN** all three are returned in relevance order

#### Scenario: Limit above the maximum

- **WHEN** a request asks for more than 30 results
- **THEN** it is rejected as an invalid request

#### Scenario: Empty eligible collection

- **WHEN** no searchable nodes meet the caller's access and type constraints
- **THEN** search returns an empty result

### Requirement: Readable type discovery and filtering <!-- roam:xtDHC9uuv -->

Type discovery SHALL return type `rid`s (global type IDs) and names, only for types present on nodes the caller can currently read. That includes types on shared nodes. Search SHALL accept one or more type `rid`s and match any of them. Without a filter, search SHALL cover all eligible types.

#### Scenario: Discover types from readable nodes

- **GIVEN** type A is on a readable shared node, and type B is only on unreadable nodes
- **WHEN** the caller discovers node types
- **THEN** type A is listed and type B is not

#### Scenario: Multiple selected types

- **WHEN** the caller searches with types A and B selected
- **THEN** every result has type A or B, and is readable by the caller

#### Scenario: No type filter

- **WHEN** the caller searches without a type filter
- **THEN** no eligible node is excluded because of its type

### Requirement: One-hop discourse context <!-- roam:IffvWYML9 -->

Discourse context SHALL return the incoming and outgoing explicit discourse relationships of a readable node. Each relationship SHALL give:

- its type;
- its direction relative to the requested node;
- the connected node's `rid` (global node ID), title and type `rid`.

Both endpoints MUST be readable. Ordinary backlinks SHALL be excluded. Connected bodies SHALL be retrieved separately, through get-node. A single call SHALL NOT go past one hop.

# Spec Delta

## Purpose

What the API's four retrieval operations return, whichever client calls them: which nodes are eligible, node payloads, semantic search, type discovery, and one-hop discourse context. All of it stays within the caller's current read access. The API exposes these operations over HTTP (`headless-retrieval-api`), and the MCP passes their results through (`discourse-mcp`).

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Readable synced collection <!-- roam:RfGa1ASkz -->

All retrieval operations SHALL use already-synced discourse data readable by the caller's space account. Local import status and authorship SHALL NOT restrict that collection. Results MUST NOT imply that the returned nodes were imported into the client application.

#### Scenario: Readable but unimported node

- **GIVEN** a synced discourse node is readable by the caller, but was authored elsewhere and never imported into its client
- **WHEN** the caller fetches it or searches for it
- **THEN** the node is eligible for retrieval and search ranking
- **AND** the response does not claim the node was imported locally

#### Scenario: Unreadable node

- **WHEN** a caller requests a node it cannot read
- **THEN** retrieval returns neither the node's content nor its metadata

### Requirement: Nodes and types are identified by rid

Every operation SHALL identify a node by its `rid` (global node ID), and a node type by the type's `rid`. Type filters SHALL take type `rid`s. Types with the same name in different spaces SHALL stay separate.

#### Scenario: Same-named types in two spaces

- **GIVEN** two readable spaces each define a type named "Claim"
- **WHEN** the caller discovers node types
- **THEN** it sees two types with different `rid`s

### Requirement: Full node text <!-- roam:M6O5NmufQ -->

Getting a readable node SHALL return the following:

- its `rid` (global node ID);
- its title;
- its type `rid`;
- its full synced text body;
- its provenance.

The body SHALL be the stored synced text, not content fetched live from the client application. Attachment downloads and file contents SHALL stay outside this operation.

#### Scenario: Get a node with body text and attachment links

- **WHEN** a caller fetches a readable synced node whose text links to an attachment
- **THEN** it receives the required node fields and the full stored text, including the source links in that text
- **AND** the response doesn't download or embed the attachment's file contents

### Requirement: Hybrid search over titles and descriptions <!-- roam:Mcp8fO0Ya -->

Search SHALL rank nodes by combining keyword matching with the stored embeddings, including Roam's title-plus-description embeddings, without re-embedding. Both SHALL cover the same text: the title, plus the description where one exists. Neither promises full-body coverage.

#### Scenario: Matching by meaning

- **WHEN** a caller submits a query, and eligible nodes have current embeddings
- **THEN** a node can rank even when its title lacks the query's exact words

#### Scenario: Matching an exact word

- **GIVEN** a readable node whose title contains a rare term, such as an acronym
- **WHEN** a caller searches for that term
- **THEN** the node ranks among the results, even if its embedding is a weak match

#### Scenario: Existing title-plus-description embedding

- **GIVEN** a readable Roam node has an embedding generated from its title and description
- **WHEN** the caller searches
- **THEN** that embedding contributes to ranking

#### Scenario: Body-only changes

- **GIVEN** the title, description, permissions and filters are unchanged
- **WHEN** only a node's full synced body changes
- **THEN** the node's search ranking doesn't change

### Requirement: Search result fields

Each search result SHALL contain the node's `rid` (global node ID), title, type `rid`, a short excerpt, provenance and a relevance score. Results SHALL be ordered by relevance.

#### Scenario: Result fields

- **WHEN** a search returns results
- **THEN** each result has those fields, and the results are ordered by score

### Requirement: Bounded search without a relevance cutoff <!-- roam:C7DJ2nVgj -->

Search SHALL default to 10 results and accept a limit from 1 to 30. A limit outside that range SHALL be rejected. V0 SHALL NOT paginate. Search SHALL NOT discard eligible nodes because their relevance is low. An empty result SHALL mean that no searchable nodes meet the access and type constraints.

#### Scenario: Default and explicit limits

- **GIVEN** at least 30 eligible searchable nodes
- **WHEN** the caller searches without a limit, and then with a limit of 20
- **THEN** the responses contain 10 results and 20 results
- **AND** neither response offers a continuation page

#### Scenario: Weak matches

- **GIVEN** three eligible searchable nodes that match the query weakly, and a limit of 10
- **WHEN** the caller searches
- **THEN** all three are returned in relevance order

#### Scenario: Limit above the maximum

- **WHEN** a request asks for more than 30 results
- **THEN** it is rejected as an invalid request

#### Scenario: Empty eligible collection

- **WHEN** no searchable nodes meet the caller's access and type constraints
- **THEN** search returns an empty result

### Requirement: Readable type discovery and filtering <!-- roam:xtDHC9uuv -->

Type discovery SHALL return type `rid`s (global type IDs) and names, only for types present on nodes the caller can currently read. That includes types on shared nodes. Search SHALL accept one or more type `rid`s and match any of them. Without a filter, search SHALL cover all eligible types.

#### Scenario: Discover types from readable nodes

- **GIVEN** type A is on a readable shared node, and type B is only on unreadable nodes
- **WHEN** the caller discovers node types
- **THEN** type A is listed and type B is not

#### Scenario: Multiple selected types

- **WHEN** the caller searches with types A and B selected
- **THEN** every result has type A or B, and is readable by the caller

#### Scenario: No type filter

- **WHEN** the caller searches without a type filter
- **THEN** no eligible node is excluded because of its type

### Requirement: One-hop discourse context <!-- roam:IffvWYML9 -->

Discourse context SHALL return the incoming and outgoing explicit discourse relationships of a readable node. Each relationship SHALL give:

- its type;
- its direction relative to the requested node;
- the connected node's `rid` (global node ID), title and type `rid`.

Both endpoints MUST be readable. Ordinary backlinks SHALL be excluded. Connected bodies SHALL be retrieved separately, through get-node. A single call SHALL NOT go past one hop.

#### Scenario: Incoming and outgoing relationships

- **GIVEN** readable nodes A and B have an explicit relationship from A to B
- **WHEN** the caller requests discourse context for A, and then for B
- **THEN** the relationship is outgoing for A and incoming for B, each with the connected node's summary

#### Scenario: Inaccessible endpoint and ordinary backlink

- **GIVEN** readable node A has an explicit relationship to unreadable node B, and an ordinary backlink from readable node C
- **WHEN** the caller requests A's discourse context
- **THEN** neither the relationship to B nor the backlink from C is returned

#### Scenario: Repeated one-hop calls

- **GIVEN** readable nodes A, B and C have relationships from A to B and from B to C, and none from A to C
- **WHEN** the caller requests A's discourse context
- **THEN** the call doesn't traverse B to return C
- **AND** a later request for B's discourse context returns the relationship to C

# Spec Delta

## Purpose

How callers reach the retrieval operations: HTTP routes, session auth, the response envelope and the versioned contract. Developers call the API directly, and the MCP calls it on behalf of agent clients. What the operations return is specified in `discourse-retrieval` (retrieval behavior).

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Four retrieval operations <!-- roam:9iZVchr-f -->

The system SHALL provide an HTTP API for four operations: get-node, search-nodes, discover-node-types and get-discourse-context. These operations SHALL follow the `discourse-retrieval` (retrieval behavior) contract. The API SHALL be the only retrieval backend for the MCP.

#### Scenario: Developer calls each operation directly

- **WHEN** a developer calls each of the four operations with a valid session token
- **THEN** each operation applies the shared retrieval and authorization rules
- **AND** no MCP is required

### Requirement: Response envelope

Every API response SHALL carry a request ID, plus either `data` or an error object with a stable code and a safe message. An error SHALL NOT be returned as an empty `data` collection.

#### Scenario: Failed request

- **WHEN** an operation fails
- **THEN** the response has a request ID and an error object, with a stable code and a message that doesn't expose internals
- **AND** the response has no `data`

### Requirement: Authenticated sessions

The API SHALL accept a valid session token for a space account. It SHALL reject missing, invalid and expired tokens, and SHALL NOT store tokens between requests. The API SHALL expose only read operations. Read-only access for agent sessions is enforced by the database, as specified in `agent-read-access` (the agent's session).

#### Scenario: Missing or expired token

- **WHEN** a request carries no token, or an expired one
- **THEN** the API rejects it as unauthenticated, and returns no discourse data

### Requirement: Versioned contract

The API SHALL serve its operations under a version prefix such as `/api/v1`. Changes within a version SHALL be additive. A breaking change SHALL ship under a new version, alongside the old one.

#### Scenario: An installed MCP after a server change

- **GIVEN** an installed MCP built against `/api/v1`
- **WHEN** the website deploys a change within `/api/v1`
- **THEN** the installed MCP's requests keep working

### Requirement: Documented developer contract <!-- roam:OlfosIASW -->

The API documentation SHALL cover:

- authentication, including how to get a session token;
- inputs and outputs;
- errors;
- search limits;
- type-filter semantics;
- the per-space access model.

The documentation SHALL also explain that:

- readable nodes can appear even if they were never imported;
- search matches titles and descriptions, by keyword and by meaning;
- search can return weak matches;
- v0 search has no pagination.

#### Scenario: Set up a direct integration

- **WHEN** a developer follows the API documentation with a session token
- **THEN** the documentation gives a working example for each of the four operations, and explains their results and errors

### Requirement: Headless retrieval after setup <!-- roam:UCHDnQtCv -->

After handoff and sync, the API SHALL work without Roam or Obsidian open. Responses SHALL come from the database's synced state.

#### Scenario: Source application is closed

- **GIVEN** a user has synced nodes and a session token
- **WHEN** Roam and Obsidian are closed, and a caller calls the API
- **THEN** eligible synced data is returned

- # Proposal
  - ## Why
    - Users want to retrieve relevant synced discourse nodes from their agent, or from their own code, without opening Roam or Obsidian, and without a separate integration for each platform. This v0 ships a retrieval API and a local MCP that exposes that API to agent clients. The MCP uses a read-only session of the space account, handed over by the plugin.
  - ## What Changes
    - **A retrieval API** at `/api/v1` (versioned HTTP routes) in `apps/website`, with four read-only operations: get a node, search nodes, list node types, and get discourse context. It is the one retrieval service: documented for developers, and the only backend of the MCP.
    - **A local MCP** that exposes each API operation as a tool. Users install it from npm, and the agent client launches it. Supported clients: Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex.
    - **Identity follows Option A2** ([decision](((guIcK3Z9M))), [options compared](((bTMUCrCnD)))): the agent signs in as the space account, but the database makes its session read-only. It was decided at the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product meeting. The session is handed over through `mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec]([[Spec: MCP token handoff]])).
    - **Coverage.** Retrieval covers every synced discourse node the space account can read under its current access, including shared nodes that were never imported into the client.
    - **Node shape.** Nodes come back as `DbCrossAppNode`s (the shared node format from [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091)), identified by `rid` (global node ID). They reuse discovery's converters and its `{ nodes, spaces }` envelope. Node types are identified by type `rid`.
    - **Search is semantic.** It reuses the stored embeddings through one new search RPC (database function), with type filtering and no relevance cutoff.
  - ## Capabilities
    - ### New Capabilities
      - `discourse-retrieval`: **what the API's four operations return.** Covers which nodes are eligible, node payloads, semantic search, type discovery and one-hop discourse context.
      - `headless-retrieval-api`: **how callers reach those operations.** Covers the HTTP routes, session auth, the response envelope and the versioned contract.
      - `discourse-mcp`: **how agent clients reach the API.** Covers four tools that pass API results through, plus setup and distribution.
      - `agent-read-access`: **the session an agent holds.** It is handed over by the plugin, reads with the space account's current access, and the database keeps it read-only.
    - ### Modified Capabilities
      - None. The repository has no OpenSpec capability specs yet.
  - ## Out of scope for v0
    - A hosted MCP and ChatGPT support. ChatGPT can't launch a local MCP; a hosted MCP can later wrap the same API.
    - Option B, a separate agent account.
    - Writes, candidate nodes, non-discourse content, canvas functions, and attachment contents.
    - Multi-hop traversal, re-embedding, pagination, relevance thresholds, and imported-only filtering.
    - Keyword or hybrid search. It's proposed for after v0, adapting [Supabase's hybrid search recipe](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai/hybrid-search) (design Decision 6).
    - One session that spans several spaces.
  - ## Impact
    - **`packages/database`:**
      - `mcp_reader` (read-only database role);
      - a custom access token hook (assigns that role at sign-in);
      - an `EXECUTE` allowlist (which database functions the role may call);
      - the space login lock (stops a session from replacing the space login);
      - retrieval functions built on the discovery converters;
      - one semantic search RPC (database function).
    - **`apps/website`:** the four API routes and their documentation.
    - **A new MCP package** (`apps/mcp`, location proposed), published to npm.
    - **Hosted Supabase settings:** the access token hook and the space login lock (design Decision 4).
    - **Depends on `mcp-session-access`** (the [session handoff spec]([[Spec: MCP token handoff]])) for the handoff, the `mcp_session` registry (list of handed-over sessions) and sign-out.
    - **Builds on** [ENG-1985](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1985) (database-to-node converter) and [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091) (discovery returns shared nodes), both merged. They provide `dbNodeToCrossApp` (converts one node), `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID) and `SharedNodeListing` (nodes plus their spaces).
  - ## Open decisions
    - Whether one agent should span several spaces.
    - Michael hasn't confirmed reusing `CrossAppNode` (the shared node format) and `rid` (global node ID) for the agent API ([Roam block](((SRa9xHk30)))).
    - No relevance or latency target is agreed, and the real-query evaluation set doesn't exist yet.

1	- # Design
2	  - ## Context
3	    - These facts from `origin/main` shape the design.
4	    - **Identity and data**
5	      - **Space accounts.** Plugins sign in as a per-space account with `signInWithPassword` (Supabase's sign-in call) in `packages/database/src/lib/contextFunctions.ts`. This spec calls that credential the **space login**. It is a random secret stored in the plugin; there are no personal user accounts yet. `mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec]([[Spec: MCP token handoff]])) adds the handoff and the `mcp_session` registry (list of handed-over sessions). None of it is in the repo yet.
6	      - **Concepts and content.**
7	        - `Concept` (the node, type and relation table) holds node instances, schemas and relations, flagged by `is_schema` and `is_relation`.
8	        - `Content` (the text table) joins it on `(space_id, source_local_id)`. Its variants are `direct` (title), `direct_and_children`, `direct_and_description` (title plus description) and `full` (body).
9	      - **Readability.** The `my_*` views (views filtered to what the caller can read), and helpers such as `in_space` and `can_view_specific_resource`, express read access.
10	    - **Discovery and embeddings**
11	      - **Discovery.** [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091) made discovery return shared nodes.
12	        - `packages/database/src/lib/sharedNodes.ts` returns a `SharedNodeListing`: `{ nodes, spaces }` of `DbCrossAppNode` (shared node format).
13	        - `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID) reads one readable node by `rid` (global node ID).
14	        - `dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` converts nodes, node types and relations into that format.
15	        - Neither the listing nor the converter includes `content.full` (the body); import fetches it separately.
16	      - **Embeddings.** `embedding.sql` stores 1536-dimension `text-embedding-3-small` vectors, each with an `obsolete` flag.
17	        - `match_content_embeddings` (the existing semantic search query) applies a similarity threshold and has no type filter.
18	        - Obsidian embeds the title (`direct`). Roam embeds the title plus description (`direct_and_description`) when there is a description, and the title alone otherwise.
19	        - The website embeds text with the team's OpenAI key (`/api/embeddings/openai/small`).
20	    - **Database access controls**
21	      - **Row-level security.** 61 of the 65 row-level security policies have no `TO` clause, so they apply to every database role. The other four are `TO authenticated` on `storage.objects` (file storage), which retrieval doesn't read. Table grants go only to `authenticated` (the signed-in role) and `service_role`.
22	      - **Function privileges.** `PUBLIC` (every database role) can execute every function in the `public` schema, because no schema file revokes that default. Some write functions are `SECURITY DEFINER` (they run as their owner, not as the caller), such as `create_secret_token` and `accept_group_invitation`. So table grants alone don't stop them.
23	      - **Auth settings.** `config.toml` sets `jwt_expiry = 3600` (a session token lasts one hour). The custom access token hook is commented out.
24	  - ## Goals / Non-Goals
25	    - **Goals:**
26	      - One retrieval service: every client, the MCP included, goes through the API.
27	      - Reuse existing data, vectors, converters and access rules.
28	      - The database enforces the agent session's read-only access, not the MCP.
29	      - Sync gaps are reported as errors, never as partial content.
30	    - **Non-Goals:**
31	      - A new identity system.
32	      - A hosted MCP.
33	      - A second embedding pipeline.
34	      - Attachment access.
35	      - Auditing.
36	  - ## Decisions
37	    - ### 1. The API is the retrieval service; the MCP is its client
38	      - DIAGRAM_PLACEHOLDER_1
39	      - Each capability spec covers one layer:
40	      - DIAGRAM_PLACEHOLDER_2
41	      - **The API holds all retrieval logic.** It is four routes in `apps/website`. They call `packages/database` functions with the caller's session, so row-level security applies.
42	      - **The MCP** holds a session and maps each tool to one API call. It never reads the database or calls OpenAI.
43	      - **Developers** call the same routes directly.
44	      - **The contract is `/api/v1`** (the versioned route prefix).
45	      - Installed MCP copies can't be force-updated, so `/api/v1` changes only additively, and a breaking change needs `/api/v2`.
46	      - Schema, query and converter fixes behind the API ship by deploying the website, without an MCP release.
47	      - **Alternatives:**
48	        - **The MCP reads the database directly.**
49	          - Installed copies would then depend on view shapes, and every fix would need an MCP release.
50	          - The MCP would bundle database code and call an embedding route outside the API's auth.
51	          - The API and the MCP would be two adapters to keep in parity.
52	        - **A hosted MCP in `apps/website` (the 2026-09-25 version).** It reaches ChatGPT but needs a hosted credential store. The 2026-11-10 meeting chose a local MCP. A hosted MCP can still wrap this API later.
53	    - ### 2. Reuse the discovery read path
54	      - The API's routes call TypeScript functions in `packages/database`. These build on Sid's discovery code from [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091):
55	        - **Get-node** calls `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID), then fetches the `full` Content (the body) the way import does.
56	        - **Type discovery** reads node types from readable node instances and labels them with `dbNodeSchemasToCrossApp` (converts node types).
57	        - **Discourse context** finds the readable relation instances that touch the node.
58	          - Candidates come from `refs`, the list of referenced IDs.
59	          - Direction comes from the `source` and `destination` keys of `reference_content` (the relation's endpoint map).
60	          - Relations are converted with `dbRelationsToCrossApp` (converts relations).
61	      - Only search needs a new RPC (database function); see Decision 6.
62	      - **Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** four new RPCs, which would duplicate the converters.
63	    - ### 3. Hand over a session through `mcp-session-access`
64	      - `mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec]([[Spec: MCP token handoff]])) defines the handoff:
65	        - **Handoff.**
66	          - 1. The plugin opens a new session for the space account, using a second client that neither persists nor auto-refreshes.
67	          - 2. It registers the session with `register_mcp_session(label)`.
68	          - 3. It shows the bundle once: Supabase URL, anon key, space ID and refresh token. It keeps no copy.
69	        - **Registry.** `mcp_session` (list of handed-over sessions) records the session ID (taken from the caller's own token), the label, the space account and the creation time.
70	        - **Sign-out.** The holder can sign itself out with local scope (only its own session). Per-session sign-out from the plugin is proposed for right after v0.
71	        - **Emergency switch.** Until then, the cut-off is to sign out every other session of the space account. That also signs out the other plugin instances, which sign back in with the space login.
72	        - **Who can connect.** Any plugin user of the space.
73	      - **Tokens.** Two tokens are involved:
74	        - the **session token** is the session's short-lived access token, the one the API takes;
75	        - the **refresh token** renews the session token, and it rotates on every use.
76	      - The bundle carries only the refresh token. So the holder's first session token comes from a refresh, and it already carries `mcp_reader` (read-only database role; Decision 4). The plugin discards the `authenticated` session token it used to register.
77	      - **Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** Option B, a separate agent account for each grant, with a credential issued from a website page. The 2026-11-10 meeting judged its security gain marginal for the extra work.
78	    - ### 4. The database makes handed-over sessions read-only (A2)
79	      - Under Option A2 ([decision](((guIcK3Z9M)))), the agent signs in as the space account, but the database makes its session read-only. The session token also works against Supabase directly, outside the API, so the database is what enforces read-only.
80	      - **The hook.** A custom access token hook (a database function Supabase calls on every token issue and refresh) checks the token's `session_id`. When the session is in `mcp_session` (list of handed-over sessions), it sets the token's `role` claim to `mcp_reader` (read-only database role; name proposed). Other sessions keep `authenticated`.
81	      - **The role.** `mcp_reader`:
82	        - is granted to `authenticator` (the role Supabase's REST layer logs in as), so requests can switch to it;
83	        - has `SELECT` on the tables and views retrieval reads, and no `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE`;
84	        - has `EXECUTE` only on an allowlist: the search RPC, plus the access helpers that the policies and views call.
85	      - **Locking down functions.** `PUBLIC` (every database role) holds `EXECUTE` on every function, so the allowlist needs two changes:
86	        - `REVOKE EXECUTE ON ALL FUNCTIONS IN SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC`;
87	        - the matching default-privilege change, so new functions aren't executable by default either.
88	      - `anon` and `authenticated` keep their explicit grants. A test lists every function `mcp_reader` can execute and compares the list with the allowlist. Policies without a `TO` clause cover `mcp_reader`, so its reads follow the space account's current access.
89	      - **Supabase Auth acts on the space account, not on a database role.** The database role doesn't cover Auth requests. Two things follow:
90	        - **Replacing the space login.** With only its session token, a handed-over session could ask Supabase Auth to set a new space login. That would lock out every plugin, and let the holder sign in again with sessions that aren't registered and can write. This change turns on the **space login lock**: the Supabase Auth settings `secure_password_change` and "require current password". Together they refuse any change that doesn't supply the current space login, which the holder never has.
91	        - **Signing out the plugins.** A session could sign out the plugins' sessions. That's disruptive but not an escalation, because the plugins sign back in.
92	      - **A switched-off hook fails open.** Handed-over sessions would then get `authenticated`. The MCP refuses to start unless its session token carries `mcp_reader`, which catches a misconfigured project at setup.
93	      - **Revocation waits for token expiry.** Sign-out stops refresh, but the current session token stays valid for up to `jwt_expiry` (session token lifetime, 3600 s). The 2026-11-10 meeting accepted this.
94	      - **Alternative: plain Option A** (the agent signs in as the space account, with read-only enforced only in the MCP's tools). Any process holding the bundle could then write. The 2026-11-10 meeting chose A2 because the threat is overeager agent harnesses that bypass the MCP.
95	    - ### 5. Nodes are CrossApp nodes, identified by `rid`
96	      - **Identifiers**
97	        - **Nodes.** A node's ID is its `rid` (global node ID), built by `spaceUriAndLocalIdToRid`.
98	          - For an `http` space URI, it's `<space URI>/<localId>`.
99	          - Otherwise, it's `orn:<platform>.note:…/<localId>`.
100	          - Look nodes up by space and `localId`, never by `localId` alone.
101	        - **Types.** A type's ID is its `rid`, from `getNodeTypeRid`, never the space-relative `nodeType`. Type filters take type `rid`s, and same-named types in different spaces stay separate.
102	      - **Payload**
103	        - **Envelope.** Each operation returns `DbCrossAppNode`s (shared node format) in discovery's `{ nodes, spaces }` envelope.
104	        - **Extra fields.** Each node gets a `typeRid`. Search also adds a `score` and an `excerpt`. There's no separate agent node type.
105	        - **Title and body.** The title is `content.direct`. Get-node adds `content.full` (the body) as stored text or markdown, never rendered HTML.
106	        - **Links and assets.** Source links stay as text. Assets aren't fetched, and no storage URLs are minted.
107	        - **Provenance.** It's the `rid` plus its `spaces` entry. Nothing implies the node exists in the caller's vault.
108	      - **Gaps are errors**
109	        - **Listings and search** skip rows the converter can't convert, as discovery does.
110	        - **Get-node doesn't skip:**
111	          - `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID) returns `null` for a missing or unreadable node, which maps to `not_found`.
112	          - A conversion failure or a missing body maps to `content_unavailable`.
113	        - A stored empty body is not a missing row.
114	      - **Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** an agent-specific payload keyed by `Concept.id` (internal database row ID), which no plugin uses. It would give each node a second identity.
115	    - ### 6. Semantic search through one new RPC
116	      - **Embedding the query.** The API embeds the query on the server with `text-embedding-3-small` at 1536 dimensions. It uses the OpenAI client that `/api/embeddings/openai/small` builds inline today, extracted into a shared helper. Embedding happens only after the API has authenticated the caller. Neither the MCP nor a developer calls the embedding route.
117	      - **The search RPC** (`SECURITY INVOKER`, so it runs as the caller) takes the query vector, optional type `rid`s and a limit. It:
118	        - joins the current, non-obsolete `direct` (title) and `direct_and_description` (title plus description) embeddings of readable node instances;
119	        - keeps each node's best similarity, once;
120	        - applies authorization, the type filter and deduplication before the limit;
121	        - sorts by similarity, then by `rid`;
122	        - has no similarity threshold, so negative similarities stay eligible.
123	      - `score` is the cosine similarity. `match_content_embeddings` (the existing semantic search query) stays unchanged.
124	      - **Other behavior**
125	        - Nodes without a usable embedding are absent from search, but the other operations still reach them.
126	        - Embedding failures are errors, not empty results.
127	      - **The excerpt** is the first 300 Unicode code points of the body (`content.full`). When the body is missing, it falls back to `content.direct` (the title). The excerpt isn't evidence that the body matched.
128	      - **Proposed for after v0: hybrid search.** Adapt [Supabase's hybrid search recipe](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai/hybrid-search). The recipe is a SQL function to copy, not a built-in. It:
129	        - ranks rows by keyword (`websearch_to_tsquery`) and by vector similarity;
130	        - merges the two rankings with Reciprocal Rank Fusion.
131	      - Here it would need two schema additions on `Content` (the text table): a generated full-text column and a GIN index. The search RPC would gain a keyword list and a fusion step. The `/api/v1` search route keeps its inputs, so this is an additive change. Exact words such as names, acronyms and titles would then rank well even when the embedding misses them.
132	    - ### 7. One-hop discourse context
133	      - Return each readable relation instance that touches the node, with:
134	        - its `rid` (global node ID);
135	        - its type;
136	        - its direction;
137	        - a summary of the connected node.
138	      - Rules:
139	        - The relation, its type and both endpoints must be readable.
140	        - Keep relations distinct even when they share a label.
141	        - A self-link appears as both incoming and outgoing.
142	        - Don't follow ordinary backlinks, and don't go past one hop.
143	    - ### 8. API contract
144	      - {{[[table]]}}
145	        - API route
146	          - MCP tool
147	            - Input
148	        - `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}`
149	          - `get_node`
150	            - node `rid`
151	        - `POST /api/v1/nodes/search`
152	          - `search_nodes`
153	            - query, optional type `rid`s, optional limit
154	        - `GET /api/v1/node-types`
155	          - `get_node_types`
156	            - none
157	        - `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}/context`
158	          - `get_discourse_context`
159	            - node `rid`
160	      - `rid`s (global node IDs) contain `/` and `:`, so they go URL-encoded in the path.
161	      - **Each route does three things:**
162	        - 1. It validates the session token with Supabase Auth, then builds a request-scoped client that acts as the caller. Nothing is held between requests.
163	        - 2. It validates the input with the shared Zod schemas (typed input and output definitions).
164	        - 3. It calls one `packages/database` function.
165	      - **Any session token is accepted.** The API accepts any valid space-account session token: a plugin's own session, or a handed-over one. The API exposes only reads, and the database keeps handed-over sessions read-only (Decision 4), so the API doesn't check the role.
166	      - **Zod schemas.** The input and output schemas live in `packages/database`, so the API and the MCP share them:
167	        - the API validates requests with them;
168	        - the MCP generates its tool input definitions from them;
169	        - the API docs are checked against them.
170	      - **Response envelope.** Every response carries a request ID, plus either `data` or an error object with a stable code and a safe message.
171	      - **Validation.** Reject the following with `invalid_request`:
172	        - a blank query;
173	        - a malformed `rid`;
174	        - an explicitly empty type list;
175	        - a limit outside 1-30.
176	      - The default limit is 10. Unknown type `rid`s match nothing.
177	      - **Error codes:**
178	      - {{[[table]]}}
179	        - Code
180	          - HTTP status
181	            - When
182	        - `unauthenticated`
183	          - 401

- # Design
  - ## Context
    - These facts from `origin/main` shape the design.
    - **Identity and data**
      - **Space accounts.** Plugins sign in as a per-space account with `signInWithPassword` (Supabase's sign-in call) in `packages/database/src/lib/contextFunctions.ts`. This spec calls that credential the **space login**. It is a random secret stored in the plugin; there are no personal user accounts yet. `mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec]([[Spec: MCP token handoff]])) adds the handoff and the `mcp_session` registry (list of handed-over sessions). None of it is in the repo yet.
      - **Concepts and content.**
        - `Concept` (the node, type and relation table) holds node instances, schemas and relations, flagged by `is_schema` and `is_relation`.
        - `Content` (the text table) joins it on `(space_id, source_local_id)`. Its variants are `direct` (title), `direct_and_children`, `direct_and_description` (title plus description) and `full` (body).
      - **Readability.** The `my_*` views (views filtered to what the caller can read), and helpers such as `in_space` and `can_view_specific_resource`, express read access.
    - **Discovery and embeddings**
      - **Discovery.** [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091) made discovery return shared nodes.
        - `packages/database/src/lib/sharedNodes.ts` returns a `SharedNodeListing`: `{ nodes, spaces }` of `DbCrossAppNode` (shared node format).
        - `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID) reads one readable node by `rid` (global node ID).
        - `dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` converts nodes, node types and relations into that format.
        - Neither the listing nor the converter includes `content.full` (the body); import fetches it separately.
      - **Embeddings.** `embedding.sql` stores 1536-dimension `text-embedding-3-small` vectors, each with an `obsolete` flag.
        - `match_content_embeddings` (the existing semantic search query) applies a similarity threshold and has no type filter.
        - Obsidian embeds the title (`direct`). Roam embeds the title plus description (`direct_and_description`) when there is a description, and the title alone otherwise.
        - The website embeds text with the team's OpenAI key (`/api/embeddings/openai/small`).
    - **Database access controls**
      - **Row-level security.** 61 of the 65 row-level security policies have no `TO` clause, so they apply to every database role. The other four are `TO authenticated` on `storage.objects` (file storage), which retrieval doesn't read. Table grants go only to `authenticated` (the signed-in role) and `service_role`.
      - **Function privileges.** `PUBLIC` (every database role) can execute every function in the `public` schema, because no schema file revokes that default. Some write functions are `SECURITY DEFINER` (they run as their owner, not as the caller), such as `create_secret_token` and `accept_group_invitation`. So table grants alone don't stop them.
      - **Auth settings.** `config.toml` sets `jwt_expiry = 3600` (a session token lasts one hour). The custom access token hook is commented out.
  - ## Goals / Non-Goals
    - **Goals:**
      - One retrieval service: every client, the MCP included, goes through the API.
      - Reuse existing data, vectors, converters and access rules.
      - The database enforces the agent session's read-only access, not the MCP.
      - Sync gaps are reported as errors, never as partial content.
    - **Non-Goals:**
      - A new identity system.
      - A hosted MCP.
      - A second embedding pipeline.
      - Attachment access.
      - Auditing.
  - ## Decisions
    - ### 1. The API is the retrieval service; the MCP is its client
      - DIAGRAM_PLACEHOLDER_1
      - Each capability spec covers one layer:
      - DIAGRAM_PLACEHOLDER_2
      - **The API holds all retrieval logic.** It is four routes in `apps/website`. They call `packages/database` functions with the caller's session, so row-level security applies.
      - **The MCP** holds a session and maps each tool to one API call. It never reads the database or calls OpenAI.
      - **Developers** call the same routes directly.
      - **The contract is `/api/v1`** (the versioned route prefix).
      - Installed MCP copies can't be force-updated, so `/api/v1` changes only additively, and a breaking change needs `/api/v2`.
      - Schema, query and converter fixes behind the API ship by deploying the website, without an MCP release.
      - **Alternatives:**
        - **The MCP reads the database directly.**
          - Installed copies would then depend on view shapes, and every fix would need an MCP release.
          - The MCP would bundle database code and call an embedding route outside the API's auth.
          - The API and the MCP would be two adapters to keep in parity.
        - **A hosted MCP in `apps/website` (the 2026-09-25 version).** It reaches ChatGPT but needs a hosted credential store. The 2026-11-10 meeting chose a local MCP. A hosted MCP can still wrap this API later.
    - ### 2. Reuse the discovery read path
      - The API's routes call TypeScript functions in `packages/database`. These build on Sid's discovery code from [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091):
        - **Get-node** calls `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID), then fetches the `full` Content (the body) the way import does.
        - **Type discovery** reads node types from readable node instances and labels them with `dbNodeSchemasToCrossApp` (converts node types).
        - **Discourse context** finds the readable relation instances that touch the node.
          - Candidates come from `refs`, the list of referenced IDs.
          - Direction comes from the `source` and `destination` keys of `reference_content` (the relation's endpoint map).
          - Relations are converted with `dbRelationsToCrossApp` (converts relations).
      - Only search needs a new RPC (database function); see Decision 6.
      - **Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** four new RPCs, which would duplicate the converters.
    - ### 3. Hand over a session through `mcp-session-access`
      - `mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec]([[Spec: MCP token handoff]])) defines the handoff:
        - **Handoff.**
          - 1. The plugin opens a new session for the space account, using a second client that neither persists nor auto-refreshes.
          - 2. It registers the session with `register_mcp_session(label)`.
          - 3. It shows the bundle once: Supabase URL, anon key, space ID and refresh token. It keeps no copy.
        - **Registry.** `mcp_session` (list of handed-over sessions) records the session ID (taken from the caller's own token), the label, the space account and the creation time.
        - **Sign-out.** The holder can sign itself out with local scope (only its own session). Per-session sign-out from the plugin is proposed for right after v0.
        - **Emergency switch.** Until then, the cut-off is to sign out every other session of the space account. That also signs out the other plugin instances, which sign back in with the space login.
        - **Who can connect.** Any plugin user of the space.
      - **Tokens.** Two tokens are involved:
        - the **session token** is the session's short-lived access token, the one the API takes;
        - the **refresh token** renews the session token, and it rotates on every use.
      - The bundle carries only the refresh token. So the holder's first session token comes from a refresh, and it already carries `mcp_reader` (read-only database role; Decision 4). The plugin discards the `authenticated` session token it used to register.
      - **Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** Option B, a separate agent account for each grant, with a credential issued from a website page. The 2026-11-10 meeting judged its security gain marginal for the extra work.
    - ### 4. The database makes handed-over sessions read-only (A2)
      - Under Option A2 ([decision](((guIcK3Z9M)))), the agent signs in as the space account, but the database makes its session read-only. The session token also works against Supabase directly, outside the API, so the database is what enforces read-only.
      - **The hook.** A custom access token hook (a database function Supabase calls on every token issue and refresh) checks the token's `session_id`.       - **The role.** `mcp_reader`:
        - is granted to `authenticator` (the role Supabase's REST layer logs in as), so requests can switch to it;
        - has `SELECT` on the tables and views retrieval reads, and no `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE`;
        - has `EXECUTE` only on an allowlist: the search RPC, plus the access helpers that the policies and views call.
      - **Locking down functions.** `PUBLIC` (every database role) holds `EXECUTE` on every function, so the allowlist needs two changes:
        - `REVOKE EXECUTE ON ALL FUNCTIONS IN SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC`;
        - the matching default-privilege change, so new functions aren't executable by default either.
      - `anon` and `authenticated` keep their explicit grants. A test lists every function `mcp_reader` can execute and compares the list with the allowlist. Policies without a `TO` clause cover `mcp_reader`, so its reads follow the space account's current access.
      - **Supabase Auth acts on the space account, not on a database role.** The database role doesn't cover Auth requests. Two things follow:
        - **Replacing the space login.** With only its session token, a handed-over session could ask Supabase Auth to set a new space login. That would lock out every plugin, and let the holder sign in again with sessions that aren't registered and can write. This change turns on the **space login lock**: the Supabase Auth settings `secure_password_change` and "require current password". Together they refuse any change that doesn't supply the current space login, which the holder never has.
        - **Signing out the plugins.** A session could sign out the plugins' sessions. That's disruptive but not an escalation, because the plugins sign back in.
      - **A switched-off hook fails open.** Handed-over sessions would then get `authenticated`. The MCP refuses to start unless its session token carries `mcp_reader`, which catches a misconfigured project at setup.
      - **Revocation waits for token expiry.** Sign-out stops refresh, but the current session token stays valid for up to `jwt_expiry` (session token lifetime, 3600 s). The 2026-11-10 meeting accepted this.
      - **Alternative: plain Option A** (the agent signs in as the space account, with read-only enforced only in the MCP's tools). Any process holding the bundle could then write. The 2026-11-10 meeting chose A2 because the threat is overeager agent harnesses that bypass the MCP.
    - ### 5. Nodes are CrossApp nodes, identified by `rid`
      - **Identifiers**
        - **Nodes.** A node's ID is its `rid` (global node ID), built by `spaceUriAndLocalIdToRid`.
          - For an `http` space URI, it's `<space URI>/<localId>`.
          - Otherwise, it's `orn:<platform>.note:…/<localId>`.
          - Look nodes up by space and `localId`, never by `localId` alone.
        - **Types.** A type's ID is its `rid`, from `getNodeTypeRid`, never the space-relative `nodeType`. Type filters take type `rid`s, and same-named types in different spaces stay separate.
      - **Payload**
        - **Envelope.** Each operation returns `DbCrossAppNode`s (shared node format) in discovery's `{ nodes, spaces }` envelope.
        - **Extra fields.** Each node gets a `typeRid`. Search also adds a `score` and an `excerpt`. There's no separate agent node type.
        - **Title and body.** The title is `content.direct`. Get-node adds `content.full` (the body) as stored text or markdown, never rendered HTML.
        - **Links and assets.** Source links stay as text. Assets aren't fetched, and no storage URLs are minted.
        - **Provenance.** It's the `rid` plus its `spaces` entry. Nothing implies the node exists in the caller's vault.
      - **Gaps are errors**
        - **Listings and search** skip rows the converter can't convert, as discovery does.
        - **Get-node doesn't skip:**
          - `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID) returns `null` for a missing or unreadable node, which maps to `not_found`.
          - A conversion failure or a missing body maps to `content_unavailable`.
        - A stored empty body is not a missing row.
      - **Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** an agent-specific payload keyed by `Concept.id` (internal database row ID), which no plugin uses. It would give each node a second identity.
    - ### 6. Semantic search through one new RPC
      - **Embedding the query.** The API embeds the query on the server with `text-embedding-3-small` at 1536 dimensions. It uses the OpenAI client that `/api/embeddings/openai/small` builds inline today, extracted into a shared helper. Embedding happens only after the API has authenticated the caller. Neither the MCP nor a developer calls the embedding route.
      - **The search RPC** (`SECURITY INVOKER`, so it runs as the caller) takes the query vector, optional type `rid`s and a limit. It:
        - joins the current, non-obsolete `direct` (title) and `direct_and_description` (title plus description) embeddings of readable node instances;
        - keeps each node's best similarity, once;
        - applies authorization, the type filter and deduplication before the limit;
        - sorts by similarity, then by `rid`;
        - has no similarity threshold, so negative similarities stay eligible.
      - `score` is the cosine similarity. `match_content_embeddings` (the existing semantic search query) stays unchanged.
      - **Other behavior**
        - Nodes without a usable embedding are absent from search, but the other operations still reach them.
        - Embedding failures are errors, not empty results.
      - **The excerpt** is the first 300 Unicode code points of the body (`content.full`). When the body is missing, it falls back to `content.direct` (the title). The excerpt isn't evidence that the body matched.
      - **Proposed for after v0: hybrid search.** Adapt [Supabase's hybrid search recipe](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai/hybrid-search). The recipe is a SQL function to copy, not a built-in. It:
        - ranks rows by keyword (`websearch_to_tsquery`) and by vector similarity;
        - merges the two rankings with Reciprocal Rank Fusion.
      - Here it would need two schema additions on `Content` (the text table): a generated full-text column and a GIN index. The search RPC would gain a keyword list and a fusion step.     - ### 7. One-hop discourse context
      - Return each readable relation instance that touches the node, with:
        - its `rid` (global node ID);
        - its type;
        - its direction;
        - a summary of the connected node.
      - Rules:
        - The relation, its type and both endpoints must be readable.
        - Keep relations distinct even when they share a label.
        - A self-link appears as both incoming and outgoing.

        - API route
          - MCP tool
            - Input

          - `get_node`
            - node `rid`
        - `POST /api/v1/nodes/search`

        - `GET /api/v1/node-types`

        - `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}/context`

        - 1. It validates the session token with Supabase Auth, then builds a request-scoped client that acts as the caller. Nothing is held between requests.
        - 2. It validates the input with the shared Zod schemas (typed input and output definitions).
        - 3. It calls one `packages/database` function.

      - **The contract is `/api/v1`** (the versioned route prefix).
        - Installed MCP copies can't be force-updated, so `/api/v1` changes only additively, and a breaking change needs `/api/v2`.

    - ### 2. Reuse the discovery read path

        - **Discourse context** finds the readable relation instances that touch the node.
          - Candidates come from `refs`, the list of referenced IDs.
          - Direction comes from the `source` and `destination` keys of `reference_content` (the relation's endpoint map).

    - ### 3. Hand over a session through `mcp-session-access`

          - 1. The plugin opens a new session for the space account, using a second client that neither persists nor auto-refreshes.
          - 2. It registers the session with `register_mcp_session(label)`.
          - 3. It shows the bundle once: Supabase URL, anon key, space ID and refresh token. It keeps no copy.
        - **Registry.** `mcp_session` (list of handed-over sessions) records the session ID (taken from the caller's own token), the label, the space account and the creation time.
        - **Sign-out.** The holder can sign itself out with local scope (only its own session). Per-session sign-out from the plugin is proposed for right after v0.
        - **Emergency switch.** Until then, the cut-off is to sign out every other session of the space account. That also signs out the other plugin instances, which sign back in with the space login.
        - **Who can connect.** Any plugin user of the space.
      - **Tokens.** Two tokens are involved:
        - the **session token** is the session's short-lived access token, the one the API takes;
        - the **refresh token** renews the session token, and it rotates on every use.

    - ### 4. The database makes handed-over sessions read-only (A2)
      - Under Option A2 ([decision](((guIcK3Z9M)))), the agent signs in as the space account, but the database makes its session read-only. The session token also works against Supabase directly, outside the API, so the database is what enforces read-only.
      - **The hook.** A custom access token hook (a database function Supabase calls on every token issue and refresh) checks the token's `session_id`. When the session is in `mcp_session` (list of handed-over sessions), it sets the token's `role` claim to `mcp_reader` (read-only database role; name proposed). Other sessions keep `authenticated`.
      - **The role.** `mcp_reader`:
        - is granted to `authenticator` (the role Supabase's REST layer logs in as), so requests can switch to it;
        - has `SELECT` on the tables and views retrieval reads, and no `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE`;
        - has `EXECUTE` only on an allowlist: the search RPC, plus the access helpers that the policies and views call.
      - **Locking down functions.** `PUBLIC` (every database role) holds `EXECUTE` on every function, so the allowlist needs two changes:
        - `REVOKE EXECUTE ON ALL FUNCTIONS IN SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC`;
        - the matching default-privilege change, so new functions aren't executable by default either.
      - `anon` and `authenticated` keep their explicit grants. A test lists every function `mcp_reader` can execute and compares the list with the allowlist. Policies without a `TO` clause cover `mcp_reader`, so its reads follow the space account's current access.
      - **Supabase Auth acts on the space account, not on a database role.** The database role doesn't cover Auth requests. Two things follow:
        - **Replacing the space login.** With only its session token, a handed-over session could ask Supabase Auth to set a new space login. That would lock out every plugin, and let the holder sign in again with sessions that aren't registered and can write. This change turns on the **space login lock**: the Supabase Auth settings `secure_password_change` and "require current password". Together they refuse any change that doesn't supply the current space login, which the holder never has.
        - **Signing out the plugins.** A session could sign out the plugins' sessions. That's disruptive but not an escalation, because the plugins sign back in.
      - **A switched-off hook fails open.** Handed-over sessions would then get `authenticated`. The MCP refuses to start unless its session token carries `mcp_reader`, which catches a misconfigured project at setup.
      - **Revocation waits for token expiry.** Sign-out stops refresh, but the current session token stays valid for up to `jwt_expiry` (session token lifetime, 3600 s). The 2026-11-10 meeting accepted this.

    - ### 5. Nodes are CrossApp nodes, identified by `rid`
      - **Identifiers**
        - **Nodes.** A node's ID is its `rid` (global node ID), built by `spaceUriAndLocalIdToRid`.

          - Otherwise, it's `orn:<platform>.note:…/<localId>`.
          - Look nodes up by space and `localId`, never by `localId` alone.

        - **Provenance.** It's the `rid` plus its `spaces` entry. Nothing implies the node exists in the caller's vault.

        - **Listings and search** skip rows the converter can't convert, as discovery does.
        - **Get-node doesn't skip:**
          - `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID) returns `null` for a missing or unreadable node, which maps to `not_found`.
