# Design

<!-- Supersedes the 2026-09-25 version of this change in Roam (block LPDwCRT6_). -->

## Context

These facts from `origin/main` shape the design.

**Identity and data**

- **Space accounts.** Plugins sign in as a per-space account with `signInWithPassword` (Supabase's sign-in call) in `packages/database/src/lib/contextFunctions.ts`. This spec calls that credential the **space login**. It is a random secret stored in the plugin; there are no personal user accounts yet. `mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/kPg_0_-lh)) adds the handoff and the `mcp_session` registry (list of handed-over sessions). None of it is in the repo yet.
- **Concepts and content.**
  - `Concept` (the node, type and relation table) holds node instances, schemas and relations, flagged by `is_schema` and `is_relation`.
  - `Content` (the text table) joins it on `(space_id, source_local_id)`. Its variants are `direct` (title), `direct_and_children`, `direct_and_description` (title plus description) and `full` (body).
- **Readability.** The `my_*` views (views filtered to what the caller can read), and helpers such as `in_space` and `can_view_specific_resource`, express read access.

**Discovery and embeddings**

- **Discovery.** [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091) made discovery return shared nodes.
  - `packages/database/src/lib/sharedNodes.ts` returns a `SharedNodeListing`: `{ nodes, spaces }` of `DbCrossAppNode` (shared node format).
  - `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID) reads one readable node by `rid` (global node ID).
  - `dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` converts nodes, node types and relations into that format.
  - Neither the listing nor the converter includes `content.full` (the body); import fetches it separately.
- **Embeddings.** `embedding.sql` stores 1536-dimension `text-embedding-3-small` vectors, each with an `obsolete` flag.
  - `match_content_embeddings` (the existing semantic search query) applies a similarity threshold and has no type filter.
  - Obsidian embeds the title (`direct`). Roam embeds the title plus description (`direct_and_description`) when there is a description, and the title alone otherwise.
  - The website embeds text with the team's OpenAI key (`/api/embeddings/openai/small`).

**Database access controls**

- **Row-level security.** 61 of the 65 row-level security policies have no `TO` clause, so they apply to every database role. The other four are `TO authenticated` on `storage.objects` (file storage), which retrieval doesn't read. Table grants go only to `authenticated` (the signed-in role) and `service_role`.
- **Function privileges.** `PUBLIC` (every database role) can execute every function in the `public` schema, because no schema file revokes that default. Some write functions are `SECURITY DEFINER` (they run as their owner, not as the caller), such as `create_secret_token` and `accept_group_invitation`. So table grants alone don't stop them.
- **Auth settings.** `config.toml` sets `jwt_expiry = 3600` (a session token lasts one hour). The custom access token hook is commented out.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:**

- One retrieval service: every client, the MCP included, goes through the API.
- Reuse existing data, vectors, converters and access rules.
- The database enforces the agent session's read-only access, not the MCP.
- Sync gaps are reported as errors, never as partial content.

**Non-Goals:**

- A new identity system.
- A hosted MCP.
- A second embedding pipeline.
- Attachment access.
- Auditing.

## Decisions

### 1. The API is the retrieval service; the MCP is its client

```
Roam / Obsidian --connect command--> bundle (shown once)
                                        |
             npx @discourse-graphs/mcp connect --> local state file
                                        |
agent client --stdio--> local MCP (thin client)
                            |
                            | HTTPS + session token
                            v
developer ----------> apps/website /api/v1 --+--> packages/database functions --> Supabase
                                             +--> OpenAI (search queries only)
```

Each capability spec covers one layer:

```
agent client --> MCP tools ----+     discourse-mcp: tools pass API results through
                               v
developer ---------------> API routes     headless-retrieval-api: HTTP, auth, envelope, versioning
                               |
                               v
              retrieval functions in packages/database
                                          discourse-retrieval: what the four operations return
```

- **The API holds all retrieval logic.** It is four routes in `apps/website`. They call `packages/database` functions with the caller's session, so row-level security applies.
- **The MCP** holds a session and maps each tool to one API call. It never reads the database or calls OpenAI.
- **Developers** call the same routes directly.

**The contract is `/api/v1`** (the versioned route prefix).
- Installed MCP copies can't be force-updated, so `/api/v1` changes only additively, and a breaking change needs `/api/v2`.
- Schema, query and converter fixes behind the API ship by deploying the website, without an MCP release.

**Alternatives:**
- **The MCP reads the database directly.**
  - Installed copies would then depend on view shapes, and every fix would need an MCP release.
  - The MCP would bundle database code and call an embedding route outside the API's auth.
  - The API and the MCP would be two adapters to keep in parity.
- **A hosted MCP in `apps/website` (the 2026-09-25 version).** It reaches ChatGPT but needs a hosted credential store. The 2026-11-10 meeting chose a local MCP. A hosted MCP can still wrap this API later.

### 2. Reuse the discovery read path

The API's routes call TypeScript functions in `packages/database`. These build on Sid's discovery code from [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091):

- **Get-node** calls `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID), then fetches the `full` Content (the body) the way import does.
- **Type discovery** reads node types from readable node instances and labels them with `dbNodeSchemasToCrossApp` (converts node types).
- **Discourse context** finds the readable relation instances that touch the node.
  - Candidates come from `refs`, the list of referenced IDs.
  - Direction comes from the `source` and `destination` keys of `reference_content` (the relation's endpoint map).
  - Relations are converted with `dbRelationsToCrossApp` (converts relations).

Only search needs a new RPC (database function); see Decision 6.

**Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** four new RPCs, which would duplicate the converters.

### 3. Hand over a session through `mcp-session-access`

`mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/kPg_0_-lh)) defines the handoff:

- **Handoff.**
  1. The plugin opens a new session for the space account, using a second client that neither persists nor auto-refreshes.
  2. It registers the session with `register_mcp_session(label)`.
  3. It shows the bundle once: Supabase URL, anon key, space ID and refresh token. It keeps no copy.
- **Registry.** `mcp_session` (list of handed-over sessions) records the session ID (taken from the caller's own token), the label, the space account and the creation time.
- **Sign-out.** The holder can sign itself out with local scope (only its own session). Per-session sign-out from the plugin is proposed for right after v0.
- **Emergency switch.** Until then, the cut-off is to sign out every other session of the space account. That also signs out the other plugin instances, which sign back in with the space login.
- **Who can connect.** Any plugin user of the space.

**Tokens.** Two tokens are involved:

- the **session token** is the session's short-lived access token, the one the API takes;
- the **refresh token** renews the session token, and it rotates on every use.

The bundle carries only the refresh token. So the holder's first session token comes from a refresh, and it already carries `mcp_reader` (read-only database role; Decision 4). The plugin discards the `authenticated` session token it used to register.

**Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** Option B, a separate agent account for each grant, with a credential issued from a website page. The 2026-11-10 meeting judged its security gain marginal for the extra work.

### 4. The database makes handed-over sessions read-only (A2)

Under Option A2 ([decision](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/guIcK3Z9M)), the agent signs in as the space account, but the database makes its session read-only. The session token also works against Supabase directly, outside the API, so the database is what enforces read-only.

**The hook.** A custom access token hook (a database function Supabase calls on every token issue and refresh) checks the token's `session_id`. When the session is in `mcp_session` (list of handed-over sessions), it sets the token's `role` claim to `mcp_reader` (read-only database role; name proposed). Other sessions keep `authenticated`.

**The role.** `mcp_reader`:

- is granted to `authenticator` (the role Supabase's REST layer logs in as), so requests can switch to it;
- has `SELECT` on the tables and views retrieval reads, and no `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE`;
- has `EXECUTE` only on an allowlist: the search RPC, plus the access helpers that the policies and views call.

**Locking down functions.** `PUBLIC` (every database role) holds `EXECUTE` on every function, so the allowlist needs two changes:

- `REVOKE EXECUTE ON ALL FUNCTIONS IN SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC`;
- the matching default-privilege change, so new functions aren't executable by default either.

`anon` and `authenticated` keep their explicit grants. A test lists every function `mcp_reader` can execute and compares the list with the allowlist. Policies without a `TO` clause cover `mcp_reader`, so its reads follow the space account's current access.

**Supabase Auth acts on the space account, not on a database role.** The database role doesn't cover Auth requests. Two things follow:

- **Replacing the space login.** With only its session token, a handed-over session could ask Supabase Auth to set a new space login. That would lock out every plugin, and let the holder sign in again with sessions that aren't registered and can write. This change turns on the **space login lock**: the Supabase Auth settings `secure_password_change` and "require current password". Together they refuse any change that doesn't supply the current space login, which the holder never has.
- **Signing out the plugins.** A session could sign out the plugins' sessions. That's disruptive but not an escalation, because the plugins sign back in.

**A switched-off hook fails open.** Handed-over sessions would then get `authenticated`. The MCP refuses to start unless its session token carries `mcp_reader`, which catches a misconfigured project at setup.

**Revocation waits for token expiry.** Sign-out stops refresh, but the current session token stays valid for up to `jwt_expiry` (session token lifetime, 3600 s). The 2026-11-10 meeting accepted this.

**Alternative: plain Option A** (the agent signs in as the space account, with read-only enforced only in the MCP's tools). Any process holding the bundle could then write. The 2026-11-10 meeting chose A2 because the threat is overeager agent harnesses that bypass the MCP.

### 5. Nodes are CrossApp nodes, identified by `rid`

**Identifiers**

- **Nodes.** A node's ID is its `rid` (global node ID), built by `spaceUriAndLocalIdToRid`.
  - For an `http` space URI, it's `<space URI>/<localId>`.
  - Otherwise, it's `orn:<platform>.note:…/<localId>`.
  - Look nodes up by space and `localId`, never by `localId` alone.
- **Types.** A type's ID is its `rid`, from `getNodeTypeRid`, never the space-relative `nodeType`. Type filters take type `rid`s, and same-named types in different spaces stay separate.

**Payload**

- **Envelope.** Each operation returns `DbCrossAppNode`s (shared node format) in discovery's `{ nodes, spaces }` envelope.
- **Extra fields.** Each node gets a `typeRid`. Search also adds a `score` and an `excerpt`. There's no separate agent node type.
- **Title and body.** The title is `content.direct`. Get-node adds `content.full` (the body) as stored text or markdown, never rendered HTML.
- **Links and assets.** Source links stay as text. Assets aren't fetched, and no storage URLs are minted.
- **Provenance.** It's the `rid` plus its `spaces` entry. Nothing implies the node exists in the caller's vault.

**Gaps are errors**

- **Listings and search** skip rows the converter can't convert, as discovery does.
- **Get-node doesn't skip:**
  - `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID) returns `null` for a missing or unreadable node, which maps to `not_found`.
  - A conversion failure or a missing body maps to `content_unavailable`.
- A stored empty body is not a missing row.

**Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** an agent-specific payload keyed by `Concept.id` (internal database row ID), which no plugin uses. It would give each node a second identity.

### 6. Semantic search through one new RPC

**Embedding the query.** The API embeds the query on the server with `text-embedding-3-small` at 1536 dimensions. It uses the OpenAI client that `/api/embeddings/openai/small` builds inline today, extracted into a shared helper. Embedding happens only after the API has authenticated the caller. Neither the MCP nor a developer calls the embedding route.

**The search RPC** (`SECURITY INVOKER`, so it runs as the caller) takes the query vector, optional type `rid`s and a limit. It:

- joins the current, non-obsolete `direct` (title) and `direct_and_description` (title plus description) embeddings of readable node instances;
- keeps each node's best similarity, once;
- applies authorization, the type filter and deduplication before the limit;
- sorts by similarity, then by `rid`;
- has no similarity threshold, so negative similarities stay eligible.

`score` is the cosine similarity. `match_content_embeddings` (the existing semantic search query) stays unchanged.

**Other behavior**

- Nodes without a usable embedding are absent from search, but the other operations still reach them.
- Embedding failures are errors, not empty results.

**The excerpt** is the first 300 Unicode code points of the body (`content.full`). When the body is missing, it falls back to `content.direct` (the title). The excerpt isn't evidence that the body matched.

**Proposed for after v0: hybrid search.** Adapt [Supabase's hybrid search recipe](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai/hybrid-search). The recipe is a SQL function to copy, not a built-in. It:

- ranks rows by keyword (`websearch_to_tsquery`) and by vector similarity;
- merges the two rankings with Reciprocal Rank Fusion.

Here it would need two schema additions on `Content` (the text table): a generated full-text column and a GIN index. The search RPC would gain a keyword list and a fusion step. The `/api/v1` search route keeps its inputs, so this is an additive change. Exact words such as names, acronyms and titles would then rank well even when the embedding misses them.

### 7. One-hop discourse context

Return each readable relation instance that touches the node, with:

- its `rid` (global node ID);
- its type;
- its direction;
- a summary of the connected node.

Rules:

- The relation, its type and both endpoints must be readable.
- Keep relations distinct even when they share a label.
- A self-link appears as both incoming and outgoing.
- Don't follow ordinary backlinks, and don't go past one hop.

### 8. API contract

| API route | MCP tool | Input |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}` | `get_node` | node `rid` |
| `POST /api/v1/nodes/search` | `search_nodes` | query, optional type `rid`s, optional limit |
| `GET /api/v1/node-types` | `get_node_types` | none |
| `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}/context` | `get_discourse_context` | node `rid` |

`rid`s (global node IDs) contain `/` and `:`, so they go URL-encoded in the path.

**Each route does three things:**

1. It validates the session token with Supabase Auth, then builds a request-scoped client that acts as the caller. Nothing is held between requests.
2. It validates the input with the shared Zod schemas (typed input and output definitions).
3. It calls one `packages/database` function.

**Any session token is accepted.** The API accepts any valid space-account session token: a plugin's own session, or a handed-over one. The API exposes only reads, and the database keeps handed-over sessions read-only (Decision 4), so the API doesn't check the role.

**Zod schemas.** The input and output schemas live in `packages/database`, so the API and the MCP share them:

- the API validates requests with them;
- the MCP generates its tool input definitions from them;
- the API docs are checked against them.

**Response envelope.** Every response carries a request ID, plus either `data` or an error object with a stable code and a safe message.

**Validation.** Reject the following with `invalid_request`:

- a blank query;
- a malformed `rid`;
- an explicitly empty type list;
- a limit outside 1-30.

The default limit is 10. Unknown type `rid`s match nothing.

**Error codes:**

| Code | HTTP status | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unauthenticated` | 401 | Token is missing, invalid or expired |
| `not_found` | 404 | Node is missing or unreadable |
| `content_unavailable` | 409 | Node lacks its body or can't be converted |
| `invalid_request` | 422 | Input fails validation |
| `result_too_large` | 422 | Response exceeds the budget |
| `dependency_error` | 503 | Database or embedding failure |

The two 422 errors are told apart by the code in the envelope. Errors are never returned as empty results.

**Response budget.** A response is either complete or fails with `result_too_large`. The proposed budget is 1 MiB serialized, to be validated in each client.

**Logs** hold only the request ID, operation, duration, result count and error category. They never include the `Authorization` header (which carries the session token), the query text or node bodies.

### 9. The local MCP

**Tools.**

- Each tool calls exactly one API operation.
- It returns the API's result as structured content, plus a short text form.
- It turns API errors into tool errors with the same code. An unreachable API is a `dependency_error`.
- Every tool is annotated read-only.

**Runtime.** Logs go to stderr, because stdout carries the MCP protocol.

**Session**

- **Connect.** `npx @discourse-graphs/mcp connect --name <name>` does the following:
  - reads the bundle from stdin;
  - refreshes once and checks that the role is `mcp_reader` (read-only database role);
  - writes the session to `~/.discourse-graphs/mcp/<name>.json` with mode 0600.

  The client config then holds only the launch command and `--name`, never a token.
- **Refresh.** The MCP refreshes against Supabase Auth. It writes each rotated refresh token to the state file atomically, before using the new session token. If the state file is lost, the user connects again with a new bundle.
- **One process per connection.** A lock file next to the state file stops a second process. Two processes refreshing the same token can make Supabase revoke the session. A user with two clients connects each one with its own bundle and `--name`.
- **Token for developers.** `npx @discourse-graphs/mcp token --name <name>` prints a current session token for that connection, refreshing it under the lock. A developer connects with their own bundle and never handles refresh-token rotation.

**Distribution and setup**

- **Package.** `@discourse-graphs/mcp` (name proposed), published to npm from `apps/mcp` with semver releases. Setup docs launch it with `npx -y @discourse-graphs/mcp@latest`.
- **Per-client setup** is documented for Claude Code (`claude mcp add`), Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`) and Codex (`~/.codex/config.toml`). The docs also cover:
  - the risk that the state file can read everything the space can read, and that any process running as the user can read it;
  - one bundle per client;
  - search limits;
  - sync-gap errors;
  - that ChatGPT is unsupported.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [The hook runs on every sign-in] → A failing hook blocks every token, including the plugins'. Keep it to one indexed lookup on `mcp_session`, return other claims unchanged, and test plugin sign-in and refresh with the hook on.
- [A switched-off hook fails open] → Handed-over sessions would get `authenticated`, which can write. The MCP's startup role check catches this. A harness that calls Supabase directly would still get a write-capable session.
- [A grant is missing from `mcp_reader`] → Retrieval fails or returns fewer rows. Cucumber scenarios run every operation as `mcp_reader`.
- [Revoking from `PUBLIC` breaks a function that relied on it] → Run the full cucumber suite as `anon` and `authenticated` after the revoke.
- [The MCP depends on the website] → If the website is down, MCP retrieval fails with `dependency_error`, and every call takes one extra network hop. Accepted in exchange for one contract and server-side fixes.
- [`/api/v1` is pinned by installed copies] → Change it only additively. A breaking change ships as `/api/v2` alongside `v1`.
- [Session tokens that can write pass through the website] → The API accepts plugin sessions too. Routes only read, and the `Authorization` header stays out of logs. A leaked token stays valid until it expires, up to one hour.
- [The state file is readable by any process running as the user] → Accepted for v0, and stated in the setup docs.
- [One session reads one space] → A user with several spaces adds one MCP entry per space.
- [Embedding inputs differ by platform] → Document the difference. Test correctness with deterministic vector fixtures, and tune relevance once real queries exist.
- [Shared nodes look unfamiliar] → Label provenance as origin, and say that results reflect readable synced data, not local imports.

## Migration Plan

1. Land `mcp-session-access` (registry, handoff helper and connect command).
2. Add `mcp_reader`, the function allowlist and the access token hook, and turn on the space login lock. Enable the hook and the lock on the hosted project.
3. Add the retrieval functions and the search RPC through the declarative schema workflow. Existing RPCs and clients keep their behavior.
4. Deploy the API routes.
5. Build and publish the MCP.
6. Validate in Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex with Roam and Obsidian closed, then release to a limited cohort.
7. To roll back, deprecate the npm package, disable the routes and sign out the registered sessions. The additive role, functions and RPC can stay.

## Open Questions

- Whether one agent should span several spaces.
- Example queries for the docs, and a relevance evaluation set. Neither changes the architecture.

208	- Embedding failures are errors, not empty results.
209	
210	**The excerpt** is the first 300 Unicode code points of the body (`content.full`). When the body is missing, it falls back to `content.direct` (the title). The excerpt isn't evidence that the body matched.
211	
212	**Proposed for after v0: hybrid search.** Adapt [Supabase's hybrid search recipe](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai/hybrid-search). The recipe is a SQL function to copy, not a built-in. It:
213	
214	- ranks rows by keyword (`websearch_to_tsquery`) and by vector similarity;
215	- merges the two rankings with Reciprocal Rank Fusion.
216	
217	Here it would need two schema additions on `Content` (the text table): a generated full-text column and a GIN index. The search RPC would gain a keyword list and a fusion step. The `/api/v1` search route keeps its inputs, so this is an additive change. Exact words such as names, acronyms and titles would then rank well even when the embedding misses them.
218	
219	### 7. One-hop discourse context
220	
221	Return each readable relation instance that touches the node, with:
222	
223	- its `rid` (global node ID);
224	- its type;
225	- its direction;
226	- a summary of the connected node.
227	
228	Rules:
229	
230	- The relation, its type and both endpoints must be readable.
231	- Keep relations distinct even when they share a label.
232	- A self-link appears as both incoming and outgoing.
233	- Don't follow ordinary backlinks, and don't go past one hop.
234	
235	### 8. API contract
236	
237	| API route | MCP tool | Input |
238	| --- | --- | --- |
239	| `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}` | `get_node` | node `rid` |
240	| `POST /api/v1/nodes/search` | `search_nodes` | query, optional type `rid`s, optional limit |
241	| `GET /api/v1/node-types` | `get_node_types` | none |
242	| `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}/context` | `get_discourse_context` | node `rid` |
243	
244	`rid`s (global node IDs) contain `/` and `:`, so they go URL-encoded in the path.
245	
246	**Each route does three things:**
247	
248	1. It validates the session token with Supabase Auth, then builds a request-scoped client that acts as the caller. Nothing is held between requests.
249	2. It validates the input with the shared Zod schemas (typed input and output definitions).
250	3. It calls one `packages/database` function.
251	
252	**Any session token is accepted.** The API accepts any valid space-account session token: a plugin's own session, or a handed-over one. The API exposes only reads, and the database keeps handed-over sessions read-only (Decision 4), so the API doesn't check the role.
253	
254	**Zod schemas.** The input and output schemas live in `packages/database`, so the API and the MCP share them:
255	
256	- the API validates requests with them;
257	- the MCP generates its tool input definitions from them;
258	- the API docs are checked against them.
259	
260	**Response envelope.** Every response carries a request ID, plus either `data` or an error object with a stable code and a safe message.
261	
262	**Validation.** Reject the following with `invalid_request`:
263	
264	- a blank query;
265	- a malformed `rid`;
266	- an explicitly empty type list;
267	- a limit outside 1-30.
268	
269	The default limit is 10. Unknown type `rid`s match nothing.
270	
271	**Error codes:**
272	
273	| Code | HTTP status | When |
274	| --- | --- | --- |
275	| `unauthenticated` | 401 | Token is missing, invalid or expired |
276	| `not_found` | 404 | Node is missing or unreadable |
277	| `content_unavailable` | 409 | Node lacks its body or can't be converted |
278	| `invalid_request` | 422 | Input fails validation |
279	| `result_too_large` | 422 | Response exceeds the budget |
280	| `dependency_error` | 503 | Database or embedding failure |
281	
282	The two 422 errors are told apart by the code in the envelope. Errors are never returned as empty results.
283	
284	**Response budget.** A response is either complete or fails with `result_too_large`. The proposed budget is 1 MiB serialized, to be validated in each client.
285	
286	**Logs** hold only the request ID, operation, duration, result count and error category. They never include the `Authorization` header (which carries the session token), the query text or node bodies.
287	
288	### 9. The local MCP
289	
290	**Tools.**
291	
292	- Each tool calls exactly one API operation.
293	- It returns the API's result as structured content, plus a short text form.
294	- It turns API errors into tool errors with the same code. An unreachable API is a `dependency_error`.
295	- Every tool is annotated read-only.
296	
297	**Runtime.** Logs go to stderr, because stdout carries the MCP protocol.
298	
299	**Session**
300	
301	- **Connect.** `npx @discourse-graphs/mcp connect --name <name>` does the following:
302	  - reads the bundle from stdin;
303	  - refreshes once and checks that the role is `mcp_reader` (read-only database role);
304	  - writes the session to `~/.discourse-graphs/mcp/<name>.json` with mode 0600.
305	
306	  The client config then holds only the launch command and `--name`, never a token.
307	- **Refresh.** The MCP refreshes against Supabase Auth. It writes each rotated refresh token to the state file atomically, before using the new session token. If the state file is lost, the user connects again with a new bundle.
308	- **One process per connection.** A lock file next to the state file stops a second process. Two processes refreshing the same token can make Supabase revoke the session. A user with two clients connects each one with its own bundle and `--name`.
309	- **Token for developers.** `npx @discourse-graphs/mcp token --name <name>` prints a current session token for that connection, refreshing it under the lock. A developer connects with their own bundle and never handles refresh-token rotation.
310	
311	**Distribution and setup**
312	
313	- **Package.** `@discourse-graphs/mcp` (name proposed), published to npm from `apps/mcp` with semver releases. Setup docs launch it with `npx -y @discourse-graphs/mcp@latest`.
314	- **Per-client setup** is documented for Claude Code (`claude mcp add`), Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`) and Codex (`~/.codex/config.toml`). The docs also cover:
315	  - the risk that the state file can read everything the space can read, and that any process running as the user can read it;
316	  - one bundle per client;
317	  - search limits;
318	  - sync-gap errors;
319	  - that ChatGPT is unsupported.
320	
321	## Risks / Trade-offs
322	
323	- [The hook runs on every sign-in] → A failing hook blocks every token, including the plugins'. Keep it to one indexed lookup on `mcp_session`, return other claims unchanged, and test plugin sign-in and refresh with the hook on.
324	- [A switched-off hook fails open] → Handed-over sessions would get `authenticated`, which can write. The MCP's startup role check catches this. A harness that calls Supabase directly would still get a write-capable session.
325	- [A grant is missing from `mcp_reader`] → Retrieval fails or returns fewer rows. Cucumber scenarios run every operation as `mcp_reader`.
326	- [Revoking from `PUBLIC` breaks a function that relied on it] → Run the full cucumber suite as `anon` and `authenticated` after the revoke.
327	- [The MCP depends on the website] → If the website is down, MCP retrieval fails with `dependency_error`, and every call takes one extra network hop. Accepted in exchange for one contract and server-side fixes.
328	- [`/api/v1` is pinned by installed copies] → Change it only additively. A breaking change ships as `/api/v2` alongside `v1`.
329	- [Session tokens that can write pass through the website] → The API accepts plugin sessions too. Routes only read, and the `Authorization` header stays out of logs. A leaked token stays valid until it expires, up to one hour.
330	- [The state file is readable by any process running as the user] → Accepted for v0, and stated in the setup docs.
331	- [One session reads one space] → A user with several spaces adds one MCP entry per space.
332	- [Embedding inputs differ by platform] → Document the difference. Test correctness with deterministic vector fixtures, and tune relevance once real queries exist.
333	- [Shared nodes look unfamiliar] → Label provenance as origin, and say that results reflect readable synced data, not local imports.
334	
335	## Migration Plan
336	
337	1. Land `mcp-session-access` (registry, handoff helper and connect command).
338	2. Add `mcp_reader`, the function allowlist and the access token hook, and turn on the space login lock. Enable the hook and the lock on the hosted project.
339	3. Add the retrieval functions and the search RPC through the declarative schema workflow. Existing RPCs and clients keep their behavior.
340	4. Deploy the API routes.
341	5. Build and publish the MCP.
342	6. Validate in Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex with Roam and Obsidian closed, then release to a limited cohort.
343	7. To roll back, deprecate the npm package, disable the routes and sign out the registered sessions. The additive role, functions and RPC can stay.
344	
345	## Open Questions
346	
347	- Whether one agent should span several spaces.
348	- Example queries for the docs, and a relevance evaluation set. Neither changes the architecture.
349

1	# Design

4	
5	## Context
6	
7	These facts from `origin/main` shape the design.
8	
9	**Identity and data**
10	
11	- **Space accounts.** Plugins sign in as a per-space account with `signInWithPassword` (Supabase's sign-in call) in `packages/database/src/lib/contextFunctions.ts`. This spec calls that credential the **space login**. It is a random secret stored in the plugin; there are no personal user accounts yet. `mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/kPg_0_-lh)) adds the handoff and the `mcp_session` registry (list of handed-over sessions). None of it is in the repo yet.
12	- **Concepts and content.**
13	  - `Concept` (the node, type and relation table) holds node instances, schemas and relations, flagged by `is_schema` and `is_relation`.
14	  - `Content` (the text table) joins it on `(space_id, source_local_id)`. Its variants are `direct` (title), `direct_and_children`, `direct_and_description` (title plus description) and `full` (body).
15	- **Readability.** The `my_*` views (views filtered to what the caller can read), and helpers such as `in_space` and `can_view_specific_resource`, express read access.
16	
17	**Discovery and embeddings**
18	
19	- **Discovery.** [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091) made discovery return shared nodes.
20	  - `packages/database/src/lib/sharedNodes.ts` returns a `SharedNodeListing`: `{ nodes, spaces }` of `DbCrossAppNode` (shared node format).
21	  - `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID) reads one readable node by `rid` (global node ID).
22	  - `dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` converts nodes, node types and relations into that format.
23	  - Neither the listing nor the converter includes `content.full` (the body); import fetches it separately.
24	- **Embeddings.** `embedding.sql` stores 1536-dimension `text-embedding-3-small` vectors, each with an `obsolete` flag.
25	  - `match_content_embeddings` (the existing semantic search query) applies a similarity threshold and has no type filter.
26	  - Obsidian embeds the title (`direct`). Roam embeds the title plus description (`direct_and_description`) when there is a description, and the title alone otherwise.
27	  - The website embeds text with the team's OpenAI key (`/api/embeddings/openai/small`).
28	
29	**Database access controls**
30	
31	- **Row-level security.** 61 of the 65 row-level security policies have no `TO` clause, so they apply to every database role. The other four are `TO authenticated` on `storage.objects` (file storage), which retrieval doesn't read. Table grants go only to `authenticated` (the signed-in role) and `service_role`.
32	- **Function privileges.** `PUBLIC` (every database role) can execute every function in the `public` schema, because no schema file revokes that default. Some write functions are `SECURITY DEFINER` (they run as their owner, not as the caller), such as `create_secret_token` and `accept_group_invitation`. So table grants alone don't stop them.
33	- **Auth settings.** `config.toml` sets `jwt_expiry = 3600` (a session token lasts one hour). The custom access token hook is commented out.
34	
35	## Goals / Non-Goals
36	
37	**Goals:**
38	
39	- One retrieval service: every client, the MCP included, goes through the API.
40	- Reuse existing data, vectors, converters and access rules.
41	- The database enforces the agent session's read-only access, not the MCP.
42	- Sync gaps are reported as errors, never as partial content.
43	
44	**Non-Goals:**
45	
46	- A new identity system.
47	- A hosted MCP.
48	- A second embedding pipeline.
49	- Attachment access.
50	- Auditing.
51	
52	## Decisions
53	
54	### 1. The API is the retrieval service; the MCP is its client
55	
56	```
57	Roam / Obsidian --connect command--> bundle (shown once)
58	                                        |
59	             npx @discourse-graphs/mcp connect --> local state file
60	                                        |
61	agent client --stdio--> local MCP (thin client)
62	                            |
63	                            | HTTPS + session token
64	                            v
65	developer ----------> apps/website /api/v1 --+--> packages/database functions --> Supabase
66	                                             +--> OpenAI (search queries only)
67	```
68	
69	Each capability spec covers one layer:
70	
71	```
72	agent client --> MCP tools ----+     discourse-mcp: tools pass API results through
73	                               v
74	developer ---------------> API routes     headless-retrieval-api: HTTP, auth, envelope, versioning
75	                               |
76	                               v
77	              retrieval functions in packages/database
78	                                          discourse-retrieval: what the four operations return
79	```
80	
81	- **The API holds all retrieval logic.** It is four routes in `apps/website`. They call `packages/database` functions with the caller's session, so row-level security applies.
82	- **The MCP** holds a session and maps each tool to one API call. It never reads the database or calls OpenAI.
83	- **Developers** call the same routes directly.
84	
85	**The contract is `/api/v1`** (the versioned route prefix).
86	- Installed MCP copies can't be force-updated, so `/api/v1` changes only additively, and a breaking change needs `/api/v2`.
87	- Schema, query and converter fixes behind the API ship by deploying the website, without an MCP release.
88	
89	**Alternatives:**
90	- **The MCP reads the database directly.**
91	  - Installed copies would then depend on view shapes, and every fix would need an MCP release.
92	  - The MCP would bundle database code and call an embedding route outside the API's auth.
93	  - The API and the MCP would be two adapters to keep in parity.
94	- **A hosted MCP in `apps/website` (the 2026-09-25 version).** It reaches ChatGPT but needs a hosted credential store. The 2026-11-10 meeting chose a local MCP. A hosted MCP can still wrap this API later.
95	
96	### 2. Reuse the discovery read path
97	
98	The API's routes call TypeScript functions in `packages/database`. These build on Sid's discovery code from [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091):
99	
100	- **Get-node** calls `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID), then fetches the `full` Content (the body) the way import does.
101	- **Type discovery** reads node types from readable node instances and labels them with `dbNodeSchemasToCrossApp` (converts node types).
102	- **Discourse context** finds the readable relation instances that touch the node.
103	  - Candidates come from `refs`, the list of referenced IDs.
104	  - Direction comes from the `source` and `destination` keys of `reference_content` (the relation's endpoint map).
105	  - Relations are converted with `dbRelationsToCrossApp` (converts relations).
106	
107	Only search needs a new RPC (database function); see Decision 6.
108	
109	**Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** four new RPCs, which would duplicate the converters.
110	
111	### 3. Hand over a session through `mcp-session-access`
112	
113	`mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/kPg_0_-lh)) defines the handoff:
114	
115	- **Handoff.**
116	  1. The plugin opens a new session for the space account, using a second client that neither persists nor auto-refreshes.
117	  2. It registers the session with `register_mcp_session(label)`.
118	  3. It shows the bundle once: Supabase URL, anon key, space ID and refresh token. It keeps no copy.
119	- **Registry.** `mcp_session` (list of handed-over sessions) records the session ID (taken from the caller's own token), the label, the space account and the creation time.
120	- **Sign-out.** The holder can sign itself out with local scope (only its own session). Per-session sign-out from the plugin is proposed for right after v0.
121	- **Emergency switch.** Until then, the cut-off is to sign out every other session of the space account. That also signs out the other plugin instances, which sign back in with the space login.
122	- **Who can connect.** Any plugin user of the space.
123	
124	**Tokens.** Two tokens are involved:
125	
126	- the **session token** is the session's short-lived access token, the one the API takes;
127	- the **refresh token** renews the session token, and it rotates on every use.
128	
129	The bundle carries only the refresh token. So the holder's first session token comes from a refresh, and it already carries `mcp_reader` (read-only database role; Decision 4). The plugin discards the `authenticated` session token it used to register.
130	
131	**Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** Option B, a separate agent account for each grant, with a credential issued from a website page. The 2026-11-10 meeting judged its security gain marginal for the extra work.
132	
133	### 4. The database makes handed-over sessions read-only (A2)
134	
135	Under Option A2 ([decision](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/guIcK3Z9M)), the agent signs in as the space account, but the database makes its session read-only. The session token also works against Supabase directly, outside the API, so the database is what enforces read-only.
136	
137	**The hook.** A custom access token hook (a database function Supabase calls on every token issue and refresh) checks the token's `session_id`. When the session is in `mcp_session` (list of handed-over sessions), it sets the token's `role` claim to `mcp_reader` (read-only database role; name proposed). Other sessions keep `authenticated`.
138	
139	**The role.** `mcp_reader`:
140	
141	- is granted to `authenticator` (the role Supabase's REST layer logs in as), so requests can switch to it;
142	- has `SELECT` on the tables and views retrieval reads, and no `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE`;
143	- has `EXECUTE` only on an allowlist: the search RPC, plus the access helpers that the policies and views call.
144	
145	**Locking down functions.** `PUBLIC` (every database role) holds `EXECUTE` on every function, so the allowlist needs two changes:
146	
147	- `REVOKE EXECUTE ON ALL FUNCTIONS IN SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC`;
148	- the matching default-privilege change, so new functions aren't executable by default either.
149	
150	`anon` and `authenticated` keep their explicit grants. A test lists every function `mcp_reader` can execute and compares the list with the allowlist. Policies without a `TO` clause cover `mcp_reader`, so its reads follow the space account's current access.
151	
152	**Supabase Auth acts on the space account, not on a database role.** The database role doesn't cover Auth requests. Two things follow:
153	
154	- **Replacing the space login.** With only its session token, a handed-over session could ask Supabase Auth to set a new space login. That would lock out every plugin, and let the holder sign in again with sessions that aren't registered and can write. This change turns on the **space login lock**: the Supabase Auth settings `secure_password_change` and "require current password". Together they refuse any change that doesn't supply the current space login, which the holder never has.
155	- **Signing out the plugins.** A session could sign out the plugins' sessions. That's disruptive but not an escalation, because the plugins sign back in.
156	
157	**A switched-off hook fails open.** Handed-over sessions would then get `authenticated`. The MCP refuses to start unless its session token carries `mcp_reader`, which catches a misconfigured project at setup.
158	
159	**Revocation waits for token expiry.** Sign-out stops refresh, but the current session token stays valid for up to `jwt_expiry` (session token lifetime, 3600 s). The 2026-11-10 meeting accepted this.
160	
161	**Alternative: plain Option A** (the agent signs in as the space account, with read-only enforced only in the MCP's tools). Any process holding the bundle could then write. The 2026-11-10 meeting chose A2 because the threat is overeager agent harnesses that bypass the MCP.
162	
163	### 5. Nodes are CrossApp nodes, identified by `rid`
164	
165	**Identifiers**
166	
167	- **Nodes.** A node's ID is its `rid` (global node ID), built by `spaceUriAndLocalIdToRid`.
168	  - For an `http` space URI, it's `<space URI>/<localId>`.
169	  - Otherwise, it's `orn:<platform>.note:…/<localId>`.
170	  - Look nodes up by space and `localId`, never by `localId` alone.
171	- **Types.** A type's ID is its `rid`, from `getNodeTypeRid`, never the space-relative `nodeType`. Type filters take type `rid`s, and same-named types in different spaces stay separate.
172	
173	**Payload**
174	
175	- **Envelope.** Each operation returns `DbCrossAppNode`s (shared node format) in discovery's `{ nodes, spaces }` envelope.
176	- **Extra fields.** Each node gets a `typeRid`. Search also adds a `score` and an `excerpt`. There's no separate agent node type.
177	- **Title and body.** The title is `content.direct`. Get-node adds `content.full` (the body) as stored text or markdown, never rendered HTML.
178	- **Links and assets.** Source links stay as text. Assets aren't fetched, and no storage URLs are minted.
179	- **Provenance.** It's the `rid` plus its `spaces` entry. Nothing implies the node exists in the caller's vault.
180	
181	**Gaps are errors**
182	
183	- **Listings and search** skip rows the converter can't convert, as discovery does.
184	- **Get-node doesn't skip:**
185	  - `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID) returns `null` for a missing or unreadable node, which maps to `not_found`.
186	  - A conversion failure or a missing body maps to `content_unavailable`.
187	- A stored empty body is not a missing row.
188	
189	**Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** an agent-specific payload keyed by `Concept.id` (internal database row ID), which no plugin uses. It would give each node a second identity.
190	
191	### 6. Semantic search through one new RPC
192	
193	**Embedding the query.** The API embeds the query on the server with `text-embedding-3-small` at 1536 dimensions. It uses the OpenAI client that `/api/embeddings/openai/small` builds inline today, extracted into a shared helper. Embedding happens only after the API has authenticated the caller. Neither the MCP nor a developer calls the embedding route.
194	
195	**The search RPC** (`SECURITY INVOKER`, so it runs as the caller) takes the query vector, optional type `rid`s and a limit. It:
196	
197	- joins the current, non-obsolete `direct` (title) and `direct_and_description` (title plus description) embeddings of readable node instances;
198	- keeps each node's best similarity, once;
199	- applies authorization, the type filter and deduplication before the limit;
200	- sorts by similarity, then by `rid`;
201	- has no similarity threshold, so negative similarities stay eligible.
202	
203	`score` is the cosine similarity. `match_content_embeddings` (the existing semantic search query) stays unchanged.
204	
205	**Other behavior**
206	
207	- Nodes without a usable embedding are absent from search, but the other operations still reach them.
208	- Embedding failures are errors, not empty results.
209	
210	**The excerpt** is the first 300 Unicode code points of the body (`content.full`). When the body is missing, it falls back to `content.direct` (the title). The excerpt isn't evidence that the body matched.
211	
212	**Proposed for after v0: hybrid search.** Adapt [Supabase's hybrid search recipe](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai/hybrid-search). The recipe is a SQL function to copy, not a built-in. It:
213	
214	- ranks rows by keyword (`websearch_to_tsquery`) and by vector similarity;
215	- merges the two rankings with Reciprocal Rank Fusion.
216	
217	Here it would need two schema additions on `Content` (the text table): a generated full-text column and a GIN index. The search RPC would gain a keyword list and a fusion step. The `/api/v1` search route keeps its inputs, so this is an additive change. Exact words such as names, acronyms and titles would then rank well even when the embedding misses them.
218	
219	### 7. One-hop discourse context
220	
221	Return each readable relation instance that touches the node, with:
222	
223	- its `rid` (global node ID);
224	- its type;
225	- its direction;
226	- a summary of the connected node.
227	
228	Rules:
229	
230	- The relation, its type and both endpoints must be readable.
231	- Keep relations distinct even when they share a label.
232	- A self-link appears as both incoming and outgoing.
233	- Don't follow ordinary backlinks, and don't go past one hop.
234	
235	### 8. API contract
236	
237	| API route | MCP tool | Input |
238	| --- | --- | --- |
239	| `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}` | `get_node` | node `rid` |
240	| `POST /api/v1/nodes/search` | `search_nodes` | query, optional type `rid`s, optional limit |
241	| `GET /api/v1/node-types` | `get_node_types` | none |
242	| `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}/context` | `get_discourse_context` | node `rid` |
243	
244	`rid`s (global node IDs) contain `/` and `:`, so they go URL-encoded in the path.
245	
246	**Each route does three things:**
247	
248	1. It validates the session token with Supabase Auth, then builds a request-scoped client that acts as the caller. Nothing is held between requests.
249	2. It validates the input with the shared Zod schemas (typed input and output definitions).
250	3. It calls one `packages/database` function.
251	
252	**Any session token is accepted.** The API accepts any valid space-account session token: a plugin's own session, or a handed-over one. The API exposes only reads, and the database keeps handed-over sessions read-only (Decision 4), so the API doesn't check the role.
253	
254	**Zod schemas.** The input and output schemas live in `packages/database`, so the API and the MCP share them:
255	
256	- the API validates requests with them;
257	- the MCP generates its tool input definitions from them;
258	- the API docs are checked against them.
259	
260	**Response envelope.** Every response carries a request ID, plus either `data` or an error object with a stable code and a safe message.
261	
262	**Validation.** Reject the following with `invalid_request`:
263	
264	- a blank query;
265	- a malformed `rid`;
266	- an explicitly empty type list;
267	- a limit outside 1-30.
268	
269	The default limit is 10. Unknown type `rid`s match nothing.
270	
271	**Error codes:**
272	
273	| Code | HTTP status | When |
274	| --- | --- | --- |
275	| `unauthenticated` | 401 | Token is missing, invalid or expired |
276	| `not_found` | 404 | Node is missing or unreadable |
277	| `content_unavailable` | 409 | Node lacks its body or can't be converted |
278	| `invalid_request` | 422 | Input fails validation |
279	| `result_too_large` | 422 | Response exceeds the budget |
280	| `dependency_error` | 503 | Database or embedding failure |
281	
282	The two 422 errors are told apart by the code in the envelope. Errors are never returned as empty results.
283	
284	**Response budget.** A response is either complete or fails with `result_too_large`. The proposed budget is 1 MiB serialized, to be validated in each client.
285	
286	**Logs** hold only the request ID, operation, duration, result count and error category. They never include the `Authorization` header (which carries the session token), the query text or node bodies.
287	
288	### 9. The local MCP
289	
290	**Tools.**
291	
292	- Each tool calls exactly one API operation.
293	- It returns the API's result as structured content, plus a short text form.
294	- It turns API errors into tool errors with the same code. An unreachable API is a `dependency_error`.
295	- Every tool is annotated read-only.
296	
297	**Runtime.** Logs go to stderr, because stdout carries the MCP protocol.
298	
299	**Session**
300	
301	- **Connect.** `npx @discourse-graphs/mcp connect --name <name>` does the following:
302	  - reads the bundle from stdin;
303	  - refreshes once and checks that the role is `mcp_reader` (read-only database role);
304	  - writes the session to `~/.discourse-graphs/mcp/<name>.json` with mode 0600.
305	
306	  The client config then holds only the launch command and `--name`, never a token.
307	- **Refresh.** The MCP refreshes against Supabase Auth. It writes each rotated refresh token to the state file atomically, before using the new session token. If the state file is lost, the user connects again with a new bundle.
308	- **One process per connection.** A lock file next to the state file stops a second process. Two processes refreshing the same token can make Supabase revoke the session. A user with two clients connects each one with its own bundle and `--name`.
309	- **Token for developers.** `npx @discourse-graphs/mcp token --name <name>` prints a current session token for that connection, refreshing it under the lock. A developer connects with their own bundle and never handles refresh-token rotation.
310	
311	**Distribution and setup**
312	
313	- **Package.** `@discourse-graphs/mcp` (name proposed), published to npm from `apps/mcp` with semver releases. Setup docs launch it with `npx -y @discourse-graphs/mcp@latest`.
314	- **Per-client setup** is documented for Claude Code (`claude mcp add`), Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`) and Codex (`~/.codex/config.toml`). The docs also cover:
315	  - the risk that the state file can read everything the space can read, and that any process running as the user can read it;
316	  - one bundle per client;
317	  - search limits;
318	  - sync-gap errors;
319	  - that ChatGPT is unsupported.
320	
321	## Risks / Trade-offs
322	
323	- [The hook runs on every sign-in] → A failing hook blocks every token, including the plugins'. Keep it to one indexed lookup on `mcp_session`, return other claims unchanged, and test plugin sign-in and refresh with the hook on.
324	- [A switched-off hook fails open] → Handed-over sessions would get `authenticated`, which can write. The MCP's startup role check catches this. A harness that calls Supabase directly would still get a write-capable session.
325	- [A grant is missing from `mcp_reader`] → Retrieval fails or returns fewer rows. Cucumber scenarios run every operation as `mcp_reader`.
326	- [Revoking from `PUBLIC` breaks a function that relied on it] → Run the full cucumber suite as `anon` and `authenticated` after the revoke.
327	- [The MCP depends on the website] → If the website is down, MCP retrieval fails with `dependency_error`, and every call takes one extra network hop. Accepted in exchange for one contract and server-side fixes.
328	- [`/api/v1` is pinned by installed copies] → Change it only additively. A breaking change ships as `/api/v2` alongside `v1`.
329	- [Session tokens that can write pass through the website] → The API accepts plugin sessions too. Routes only read, and the `Authorization` header stays out of logs. A leaked token stays valid until it expires, up to one hour.
330	- [The state file is readable by any process running as the user] → Accepted for v0, and stated in the setup docs.
331	- [One session reads one space] → A user with several spaces adds one MCP entry per space.
332	- [Embedding inputs differ by platform] → Document the difference. Test correctness with deterministic vector fixtures, and tune relevance once real queries exist.
333	- [Shared nodes look unfamiliar] → Label provenance as origin, and say that results reflect readable synced data, not local imports.
334	
335	## Migration Plan
336	
337	1. Land `mcp-session-access` (registry, handoff helper and connect command).
338	2. Add `mcp_reader`, the function allowlist and the access token hook, and turn on the space login lock. Enable the hook and the lock on the hosted project.
339	3. Add the retrieval functions and the search RPC through the declarative schema workflow. Existing RPCs and clients keep their behavior.
340	4. Deploy the API routes.
341	5. Build and publish the MCP.
342	6. Validate in Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex with Roam and Obsidian closed, then release to a limited cohort.
343	7. To roll back, deprecate the npm package, disable the routes and sign out the registered sessions. The additive role, functions and RPC can stay.
344	
345	## Open Questions
346	
347	- Whether one agent should span several spaces.
348	- Example queries for the docs, and a relevance evaluation set. Neither changes the architecture.
349

**Supabase Auth acts on the space account, not on a database role.** The database role doesn't cover Auth requests. Two things follow:

- **Replacing the space login.** With only its session token, a handed-over session could ask Supabase Auth to set a new space login. That would lock out every plugin, and let the holder sign in again with sessions that aren't registered and can write. This change turns on the **space login lock**: the Supabase Auth settings `secure_password_change` and "require current password". Together they refuse any change that doesn't supply the current space login, which the holder never has.
- **Signing out the plugins.** A session could sign out the plugins' sessions. That's disruptive but not an escalation, because the plugins sign back in.

content.text:
I made the clear-cut edits to `design.md`, and `openspec validate --strict` passes. One decision is still open: the function lockdown.

**Space login wording:** your reading is right, with one correction. The plugin signs in, not the website. Context now has two bullets:
- **Space accounts:** each plugin signs in with the space login, a random secret it stores.
- **Session handoff:** the plugin uses that login to open one extra session, and hands only that session's refresh token to the MCP. The MCP never stores the space login.

**Mermaid:** both diagrams in Decision 1 are now Mermaid flowcharts.
- The architecture chart labels each arrow and shows the agent clients by name.
- The layer chart groups each spec as a box, with the read-only session hanging off the MCP.

**OpenAI in the chart:** that's the embeddings service. It turns a search query into a vector, the same service sync already uses, and has nothing to do with ChatGPT. The node is now labelled "OpenAI embeddings API: turns query text into a vector", with a one-line note under the chart.

**Supabase Auth paragraph:** cut to three sentences.
- A handed-over session could ask Supabase Auth to replace the space login.
- The space login lock refuses that.
- Signing out the plugins only makes them sign back in, and signing out the handed-over session ends it.

**One-hop context (your question):** yes, it only returns what the space can read.
- Relations come from `my_concepts` with the caller's session. That view filters by `my_accessible_resources` (`concept.sql:201`), so an unreadable relation never comes back.
- The endpoint and the relation type also have to be readable.
- I found one catch: `dbRelationsToCrossApp` throws when an endpoint is missing, rather than skipping it. Decision 7 now says to drop such relations before converting, so one hidden endpoint can't fail the whole call.

**Function lockdown (your concern):** it isn't covered in `Spec: MCP token handoff`. That spec gives v0 sessions full permissions, so it never needed this.
- **Plugins and sync should be safe.** `base.sql` runs first and grants every later function to `anon` and `authenticated` explicitly, so plugins don't depend on `PUBLIC`. Revoking `PUBLIC` shouldn't change what they can call.
- **Unverified for hosted.** The hosted database was built from migrations, and early migrations may have created functions before those grants existed.
- **Why `PUBLIC` must be touched at all.** Postgres has no "deny" grant, and every role inherits `PUBLIC`. So `mcp_reader` can only be blocked by removing that default.
- **A narrower option.** Only `SECURITY DEFINER` functions can bypass `mcp_reader`'s missing table write grants: 27 of them, many of them triggers or read helpers. Revoking `PUBLIC` on just the definer functions that write, while keeping explicit grants for `anon` and `authenticated`, leaves every other function's permissions untouched.

Should I narrow the lockdown to the `SECURITY DEFINER` functions that write, or keep the broad revoke? Either way, I can then sync these changes to the Roam copy.

file.content:
# Spec Delta

## Purpose

The session an agent holds. A plugin hands it over, it reads the space's synced discourse graph with the space account's current access, and the database keeps it read-only. This follows Option A2 ([decision](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/guIcK3Z9M)): the agent signs in as the space account, but its session can't write.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Session handed over through `mcp-session-access`

The MCP SHALL use a session that a plugin handed over and registered through `mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/kPg_0_-lh)). No website session or agent-management page SHALL be required. The MCP SHALL NOT receive the space login, which is the credential plugins use to sign in.

#### Scenario: Connect from either platform

- **WHEN** a user runs the connect command in a signed-in Roam or Obsidian client
- **THEN** the plugin shows a bundle for a new, registered session of that client's space account
- **AND** the plugin's own session is unchanged

### Requirement: Per-space principal

The system SHALL treat the space account whose session was handed over as the principal, meaning the identity whose access is used. Retrieval SHALL use that account's readable collection. It SHALL NOT combine the access of other space accounts that the same person uses. Reading another space's synced but unpublished nodes SHALL require a bundle from that space.

#### Scenario: Another space's private synced nodes

- **GIVEN** a person uses spaces A and B, and a node in B is not readable by A's space account
- **WHEN** an agent uses a bundle from space A
- **THEN** it cannot retrieve the node in B

#### Scenario: Accessible shared node

- **GIVEN** a node from another space is readable by the space account through sharing
- **WHEN** the agent retrieves that node
- **THEN** the node is returned, even though the space account didn't import or author it

### Requirement: Current permissions

The system SHALL evaluate retrieval against the space account's current read permissions.

- Removing access SHALL stop later retrieval of the affected data.
- Adding access SHALL make the affected synced data eligible.

Neither change SHALL require a new bundle.

#### Scenario: Permissions change after handoff

- **WHEN** a space account gains access to node A and loses access to node B after a bundle is handed over
- **THEN** later requests with that bundle can retrieve A and cannot retrieve B

### Requirement: Session sign-out

The MCP SHALL be able to sign its own session out. A signed-out session SHALL NOT refresh. A session token the MCP already holds MAY stay valid until it expires, which is up to one hour.

#### Scenario: Signed-out session

- **WHEN** a handed-over session is signed out
- **THEN** the MCP cannot refresh it
- **AND** requests fail once its current session token expires

### Requirement: The database refuses writes from handed-over sessions

The database SHALL refuse every create, modify or delete made with a handed-over session, whichever client makes it. That includes calls to write functions. The session SHALL keep the space account's read access, and plugin sessions SHALL keep their permissions. Missing or expired sessions SHALL NOT authorize retrieval.

#### Scenario: Write made outside the MCP's tools

- **GIVEN** a process holds a handed-over session, and the space account can edit a node
- **WHEN** the process modifies the node, or calls a write function, directly with that session
- **THEN** the database refuses it
- **AND** the node remains unchanged

#### Scenario: Plugin session keeps write access

- **GIVEN** a plugin has handed over a session
- **WHEN** the plugin writes with its own session
- **THEN** the write succeeds

#### Scenario: Unauthenticated retrieval

- **WHEN** a retrieval request has a missing or expired session
- **THEN** no discourse data is returned

### Requirement: Handed-over sessions cannot replace the space login

A handed-over session SHALL NOT be able to replace the space login, which is the credential plugins use to sign in, using only its session token.

#### Scenario: Agent tries to replace the space login

- **WHEN** a process asks Supabase Auth to set a new space login, using a handed-over session token
- **THEN** Supabase Auth refuses the request
- **AND** the space's plugins still sign in with the existing space login

content.text:
No, nothing is missing. "Spec Delta" is OpenSpec's term for any spec file inside a change folder, and it doesn't mean older specs exist.

**How OpenSpec splits specs**
- `openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` holds the **current** spec, describing how the system behaves today.
- `openspec/changes/<change>/specs/<capability>/spec.md` holds a **delta**: what this change does to the current spec. Its sections say how: `ADDED`, `MODIFIED`, `REMOVED` or `RENAMED Requirements`.

**What exists today:** `openspec/specs/` holds only a `.gitkeep`, and `openspec list --specs` reports "No specs found". So all four capabilities are brand new. That's why every delta has only an `## ADDED Requirements` section, and why the proposal says "Modified Capabilities: None".

**When the change is archived** (`/opsx:archive`), OpenSpec merges each delta into `openspec/specs/agent-read-access/spec.md` and the other three capability files. Those become the first current specs, and future changes will write `MODIFIED` deltas against them.

The `# Spec Delta` title itself is just the template's heading. If it reads as misleading, I can rename each one to the capability name, for example `# agent-read-access`. Validation doesn't depend on the title.

# Spec Delta

## Purpose

What the API's four retrieval operations return, whichever client calls them: which nodes are eligible, node payloads, semantic search, type discovery, and one-hop discourse context. All of it stays within the caller's current read access. The API exposes these operations over HTTP (`headless-retrieval-api`), and the MCP passes their results through (`discourse-mcp`).

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Readable synced collection <!-- roam:RfGa1ASkz -->

All retrieval operations SHALL use already-synced discourse data readable by the caller's space account. Local import status and authorship SHALL NOT restrict that collection. Results MUST NOT imply that the returned nodes were imported into the client application.

#### Scenario: Readable but unimported node

- **GIVEN** a synced discourse node is readable by the caller, but was authored elsewhere and never imported into its client
- **WHEN** the caller fetches it or searches for it
- **THEN** the node is eligible for retrieval and search ranking
- **AND** the response does not claim the node was imported locally

#### Scenario: Unreadable node

- **WHEN** a caller requests a node it cannot read
- **THEN** retrieval returns neither the node's content nor its metadata

### Requirement: Nodes and types are identified by rid

Every operation SHALL identify a node by its `rid` (global node ID), and a node type by the type's `rid`. Type filters SHALL take type `rid`s. Types with the same name in different spaces SHALL stay separate.

#### Scenario: Same-named types in two spaces

- **GIVEN** two readable spaces each define a type named "Claim"
- **WHEN** the caller discovers node types
- **THEN** it sees two types with different `rid`s

### Requirement: Full node text <!-- roam:M6O5NmufQ -->

Getting a readable node SHALL return the following:

- its `rid` (global node ID);
- its title;
- its type `rid`;
- its full synced text body;
- its provenance.

The body SHALL be the stored synced text, not content fetched live from the client application. Attachment downloads and file contents SHALL stay outside this operation.

#### Scenario: Get a node with body text and attachment links

- **WHEN** a caller fetches a readable synced node whose text links to an attachment
- **THEN** it receives the required node fields and the full stored text, including the source links in that text
- **AND** the response doesn't download or embed the attachment's file contents

### Requirement: Semantic search over existing embeddings <!-- roam:Mcp8fO0Ya -->

Search SHALL rank nodes by semantic similarity using the stored embeddings, including Roam's title-plus-description embeddings, without re-embedding. Matching SHALL reflect those embedding inputs: the title, plus the description where one exists. It doesn't promise full-body coverage. V0 SHALL NOT require keyword matching or hybrid ranking.

#### Scenario: Matching by meaning

- **WHEN** a caller submits a query, and eligible nodes have current embeddings
- **THEN** a node can rank even when its title lacks the query's exact words

#### Scenario: Existing title-plus-description embedding

- **GIVEN** a readable Roam node has an embedding generated from its title and description
- **WHEN** the caller searches
- **THEN** that embedding contributes to ranking

#### Scenario: Body-only changes

- **GIVEN** the title, description, permissions and filters are unchanged
- **WHEN** only a node's full synced body changes
- **THEN** the node's search ranking doesn't change

### Requirement: Search result fields

Each search result SHALL contain the node's `rid` (global node ID), title, type `rid`, a short excerpt, provenance and a relevance score. Results SHALL be ordered by relevance.

#### Scenario: Result fields

- **WHEN** a search returns results
- **THEN** each result has those fields, and the results are ordered by score

### Requirement: Bounded search without a relevance cutoff <!-- roam:C7DJ2nVgj -->

Search SHALL default to 10 results and accept a limit from 1 to 30. A limit outside that range SHALL be rejected. V0 SHALL NOT paginate. Search SHALL NOT discard eligible nodes because their relevance is low. An empty result SHALL mean that no searchable nodes meet the access and type constraints.

#### Scenario: Default and explicit limits

- **GIVEN** at least 30 eligible searchable nodes
- **WHEN** the caller searches without a limit, and then with a limit of 20
- **THEN** the responses contain 10 results and 20 results
- **AND** neither response offers a continuation page

#### Scenario: Weak matches

- **GIVEN** three eligible searchable nodes that match the query weakly, and a limit of 10
- **WHEN** the caller searches
- **THEN** all three are returned in relevance order

#### Scenario: Limit above the maximum

- **WHEN** a request asks for more than 30 results
- **THEN** it is rejected as an invalid request

#### Scenario: Empty eligible collection

- **WHEN** no searchable nodes meet the caller's access and type constraints
- **THEN** search returns an empty result

### Requirement: Readable type discovery and filtering <!-- roam:xtDHC9uuv -->

Type discovery SHALL return type `rid`s (global type IDs) and names, only for types present on nodes the caller can currently read. That includes types on shared nodes. Search SHALL accept one or more type `rid`s and match any of them. Without a filter, search SHALL cover all eligible types.

#### Scenario: Discover types from readable nodes

- **GIVEN** type A is on a readable shared node, and type B is only on unreadable nodes
- **WHEN** the caller discovers node types
- **THEN** type A is listed and type B is not

#### Scenario: Multiple selected types

- **WHEN** the caller searches with types A and B selected
- **THEN** every result has type A or B, and is readable by the caller

#### Scenario: No type filter

- **WHEN** the caller searches without a type filter
- **THEN** no eligible node is excluded because of its type

### Requirement: One-hop discourse context <!-- roam:IffvWYML9 -->

Discourse context SHALL return the incoming and outgoing explicit discourse relationships of a readable node. Each relationship SHALL give:

- its type;
- its direction relative to the requested node;
- the connected node's `rid` (global node ID), title and type `rid`.

Both endpoints MUST be readable. Ordinary backlinks SHALL be excluded. Connected bodies SHALL be retrieved separately, through get-node. A single call SHALL NOT go past one hop.

#### Scenario: Incoming and outgoing relationships

- **GIVEN** readable nodes A and B have an explicit relationship from A to B
- **WHEN** the caller requests discourse context for A, and then for B
- **THEN** the relationship is outgoing for A and incoming for B, each with the connected node's summary

#### Scenario: Inaccessible endpoint and ordinary backlink

- **GIVEN** readable node A has an explicit relationship to unreadable node B, and an ordinary backlink from readable node C
- **WHEN** the caller requests A's discourse context
- **THEN** neither the relationship to B nor the backlink from C is returned

#### Scenario: Repeated one-hop calls

- **GIVEN** readable nodes A, B and C have relationships from A to B and from B to C, and none from A to C
- **WHEN** the caller requests A's discourse context
- **THEN** the call doesn't traverse B to return C
- **AND** a later request for B's discourse context returns the relationship to C

content.text:
Sorry, I should have shown these before editing. Nothing has changed this time. Here are the findings, then the changes I propose.

## What "provenance" contains today

Under the current design, a node payload carries:
- **`rid`:** the space's URI plus the node's local ID.
- **`spaces` entry:** the space's name, platform (Roam or Obsidian) and URL.
- **`authorId`, `createdAt`, `modifiedAt`:** these come from `DbCrossAppNode`. But `authorId` is the platform's internal account ID (`account_local_id`), not a person's name.

What's missing:
- A readable author name. `PlatformAccount.name` exists, and `my_accounts` exposes it, so it can be looked up.
- A readable type name. Nodes carry only `typeRid`, and names appear only in the type-discovery operation.
- A link to open the node at its source.

You're right that "Trang's Claim node" can't be assembled from what's returned today.

## Proposed changes (not applied)

**1. Spell out provenance, and add readable names** (in `discourse-retrieval`, under "Full node text" and "Search result fields"). Each node would carry:
- `type`: `{ rid, name }`, for example `{ rid: "...", name: "Claim" }`;
- `author`: `{ name }`, from `PlatformAccount.name`;
- `space`: `{ name, platform, url }`, already in the `spaces` map but now named per node;
- `createdAt` and `modifiedAt`, already present;
- `sourceUrl`: only for Roam nodes, built as `<graph URL>/page/<uid>`. Obsidian has no stable web URL for a note, so Obsidian nodes return the vault file path as plain text instead. That path is already stored in the title row's metadata (`filePath`).

I'd keep these as structured fields rather than a pre-written label, so agents can phrase it themselves ("a Claim by Trang, from the Lab graph").

Discourse context's connected-node summaries would get the same `type` name, `author` name and `space` name.

**2. Design Decision 5 (Payload):** list the same fields, and note that the author name comes from `my_accounts`.

## Obsidian embeddings

Yes, Obsidian titles are embedded, but only titles. Here's what each platform embeds, from the sync code on `origin/main`:

| Platform | Embedded text | Not embedded |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Obsidian | The title (the note's file name) | Description, body, frontmatter |
| Roam | The title plus description when there's a description, otherwise the title | Body |

So the current algorithm already covers Obsidian nodes, by title. The gap is uneven coverage: Roam nodes with descriptions match on more text than Obsidian nodes. A query that matches only an Obsidian note's body won't find it.

That's an embedding-input question, not a search-algorithm one. Closing it would mean embedding more Obsidian text during sync, which is a sync change and needs re-embedding, both out of scope for v0. I'd propose adding one line to the existing "Embedding inputs differ by platform" risk saying Obsidian search matches titles only, and documenting the same in the API and MCP docs.
