# Spec Delta

## Purpose

What the API's four retrieval operations return, whichever client calls them: which nodes are eligible, node payloads, semantic search, type discovery, and one-hop discourse context. All of it stays within the caller's current read access. The API exposes these operations over HTTP (`headless-retrieval-api`), and the MCP passes their results through (`discourse-mcp`).

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Readable synced collection <!-- roam:RfGa1ASkz -->

All retrieval operations SHALL use already-synced discourse data readable by the caller's space account. Local import status and authorship SHALL NOT restrict that collection. Results MUST NOT imply that the returned nodes were imported into the client application.

#### Scenario: Readable but unimported node

- **GIVEN** a synced discourse node is readable by the caller, but was authored elsewhere and never imported into its client
- **WHEN** the caller fetches it or searches for it
- **THEN** the node is eligible for retrieval and search ranking
- **AND** the response does not claim the node was imported locally

#### Scenario: Unreadable node

- **WHEN** a caller requests a node it cannot read
- **THEN** retrieval returns neither the node's content nor its metadata

### Requirement: Nodes and types are identified by rid

Every operation SHALL identify a node by its `rid` (global node ID), and a node type by the type's `rid`. Type filters SHALL take type `rid`s. Types with the same name in different spaces SHALL stay separate.

#### Scenario: Same-named types in two spaces

- **GIVEN** two readable spaces each define a type named "Claim"
- **WHEN** the caller discovers node types
- **THEN** it sees two types with different `rid`s

### Requirement: Full node text <!-- roam:M6O5NmufQ -->

Getting a readable node SHALL return the following:

- its `rid` (global node ID);
- its title;
- its type `rid`;
- its full synced text body;
- its provenance.

The body SHALL be the stored synced text, not content fetched live from the client application. Attachment downloads and file contents SHALL stay outside this operation.

#### Scenario: Get a node with body text and attachment links

- **WHEN** a caller fetches a readable synced node whose text links to an attachment
- **THEN** it receives the required node fields and the full stored text, including the source links in that text
- **AND** the response doesn't download or embed the attachment's file contents

### Requirement: Semantic search over existing embeddings <!-- roam:Mcp8fO0Ya -->

Search SHALL rank nodes by semantic similarity using the stored embeddings, including Roam's title-plus-description embeddings, without re-embedding. Matching SHALL reflect those embedding inputs: the title, plus the description where one exists. It doesn't promise full-body coverage. V0 SHALL NOT require keyword matching or hybrid ranking.

#### Scenario: Matching by meaning

- **WHEN** a caller submits a query, and eligible nodes have current embeddings
- **THEN** a node can rank even when its title lacks the query's exact words

#### Scenario: Existing title-plus-description embedding

- **GIVEN** a readable Roam node has an embedding generated from its title and description
- **WHEN** the caller searches
- **THEN** that embedding contributes to ranking

#### Scenario: Body-only changes

- **GIVEN** the title, description, permissions and filters are unchanged
- **WHEN** only a node's full synced body changes
- **THEN** the node's search ranking doesn't change

### Requirement: Search result fields

Each search result SHALL contain the node's `rid` (global node ID), title, type `rid`, a short excerpt, provenance and a relevance score. Results SHALL be ordered by relevance.

#### Scenario: Result fields

- **WHEN** a search returns results
- **THEN** each result has those fields, and the results are ordered by score

### Requirement: Bounded search without a relevance cutoff <!-- roam:C7DJ2nVgj -->

Search SHALL default to 10 results and accept a limit from 1 to 30. A limit outside that range SHALL be rejected. V0 SHALL NOT paginate. Search SHALL NOT discard eligible nodes because their relevance is low. An empty result SHALL mean that no searchable nodes meet the access and type constraints.

#### Scenario: Default and explicit limits

- **GIVEN** at least 30 eligible searchable nodes
- **WHEN** the caller searches without a limit, and then with a limit of 20
- **THEN** the responses contain 10 results and 20 results
- **AND** neither response offers a continuation page

#### Scenario: Weak matches

- **GIVEN** three eligible searchable nodes that match the query weakly, and a limit of 10
- **WHEN** the caller searches
- **THEN** all three are returned in relevance order

#### Scenario: Limit above the maximum

- **WHEN** a request asks for more than 30 results
- **THEN** it is rejected as an invalid request

#### Scenario: Empty eligible collection

- **WHEN** no searchable nodes meet the caller's access and type constraints
- **THEN** search returns an empty result

### Requirement: Readable type discovery and filtering <!-- roam:xtDHC9uuv -->

Type discovery SHALL return type `rid`s (global type IDs) and names, only for types present on nodes the caller can currently read. That includes types on shared nodes. Search SHALL accept one or more type `rid`s and match any of them. Without a filter, search SHALL cover all eligible types.

#### Scenario: Discover types from readable nodes

- **GIVEN** type A is on a readable shared node, and type B is only on unreadable nodes
- **WHEN** the caller discovers node types
- **THEN** type A is listed and type B is not

#### Scenario: Multiple selected types

- **WHEN** the caller searches with types A and B selected
- **THEN** every result has type A or B, and is readable by the caller

#### Scenario: No type filter

- **WHEN** the caller searches without a type filter
- **THEN** no eligible node is excluded because of its type

### Requirement: One-hop discourse context <!-- roam:IffvWYML9 -->

Discourse context SHALL return the incoming and outgoing explicit discourse relationships of a readable node. Each relationship SHALL give:

- its type;
- its direction relative to the requested node;
- the connected node's `rid` (global node ID), title and type `rid`.

Both endpoints MUST be readable. Ordinary backlinks SHALL be excluded. Connected bodies SHALL be retrieved separately, through get-node. A single call SHALL NOT go past one hop.

#### Scenario: Incoming and outgoing relationships

- **GIVEN** readable nodes A and B have an explicit relationship from A to B
- **WHEN** the caller requests discourse context for A, and then for B
- **THEN** the relationship is outgoing for A and incoming for B, each with the connected node's summary

#### Scenario: Inaccessible endpoint and ordinary backlink

- **GIVEN** readable node A has an explicit relationship to unreadable node B, and an ordinary backlink from readable node C
- **WHEN** the caller requests A's discourse context
- **THEN** neither the relationship to B nor the backlink from C is returned

#### Scenario: Repeated one-hop calls

- **GIVEN** readable nodes A, B and C have relationships from A to B and from B to C, and none from A to C
- **WHEN** the caller requests A's discourse context
- **THEN** the call doesn't traverse B to return C
- **AND** a later request for B's discourse context returns the relationship to C

- **WHEN** a caller fetches a readable synced node whose text links to an attachment
- **THEN** it receives the required node fields and the full stored text, including the source links in that text
- **AND** the response doesn't download or embed the attachment's file contents

- **GIVEN** a readable Claim node written by Trang in the "Lab" space
- **WHEN** a caller fetches it
- **THEN** the response names the type "Claim", the author "Trang" and the space "Lab", alongside the type's `rid`

#### Scenario: Matching by meaning

- **WHEN** a caller submits a query, and eligible nodes have current embeddings
- **THEN** a node can rank even when its title lacks the query's exact words

#### Scenario: Existing title-plus-description embedding

- **GIVEN** a readable Roam node has an embedding generated from its title and description
- **WHEN** the caller searches
- **THEN** that embedding contributes to ranking

#### Scenario: Body-only changes

- **GIVEN** the title, description, permissions and filters are unchanged
- **WHEN** only a node's full synced body changes
- **THEN** the node's search ranking doesn't change

### Requirement: Search result fields

Each search result SHALL contain the node's `rid` (global node ID), title, type `rid`, a short excerpt, provenance and a relevance score. Results SHALL be ordered by relevance.

#### Scenario: Result fields

- **WHEN** a search returns results
- **THEN** each result has those fields, and the results are ordered by score

### Requirement: Bounded search without a relevance cutoff <!-- roam:C7DJ2nVgj -->

Search SHALL default to 10 results and accept a limit from 1 to 30. A limit outside that range SHALL be rejected. V0 SHALL NOT paginate. Search SHALL NOT discard eligible nodes because their relevance is low. An empty result SHALL mean that no searchable nodes meet the access and type constraints.

#### Scenario: Default and explicit limits

- **GIVEN** at least 30 eligible searchable nodes
- **WHEN** the caller searches without a limit, and then with a limit of 20
- **THEN** the responses contain 10 results and 20 results
- **AND** neither response offers a continuation page

#### Scenario: Weak matches

- **GIVEN** three eligible searchable nodes that match the query weakly, and a limit of 10
- **WHEN** the caller searches
- **THEN** all three are returned in relevance order

#### Scenario: Limit above the maximum

- **WHEN** a request asks for more than 30 results
- **THEN** it is rejected as an invalid request

#### Scenario: Empty eligible collection

- **WHEN** no searchable nodes meet the caller's access and type constraints
- **THEN** search returns an empty result

### Requirement: Readable type discovery and filtering <!-- roam:xtDHC9uuv -->

Type discovery SHALL return type `rid`s (global type IDs) and names, only for types present on nodes the caller can currently read. That includes types on shared nodes. Search SHALL accept one or more type `rid`s and match any of them. Without a filter, search SHALL cover all eligible types.

#### Scenario: Discover types from readable nodes

- **GIVEN** type A is on a readable shared node, and type B is only on unreadable nodes
- **WHEN** the caller discovers node types
- **THEN** type A is listed and type B is not

#### Scenario: Multiple selected types

- **WHEN** the caller searches with types A and B selected
- **THEN** every result has type A or B, and is readable by the caller

#### Scenario: No type filter

- **WHEN** the caller searches without a type filter
- **THEN** no eligible node is excluded because of its type

- its type;
- its direction relative to the requested node;
- the connected node's `rid` (global node ID), title and type `rid`.

- **GIVEN** readable nodes A and B have an explicit relationship from A to B
- **WHEN** the caller requests discourse context for A, and then for B
- **THEN** the relationship is outgoing for A and incoming for B, each with the connected node's summary

#### Scenario: Inaccessible endpoint and ordinary backlink

- **GIVEN** readable node A has an explicit relationship to unreadable node B, and an ordinary backlink from readable node C
- **WHEN** the caller requests A's discourse context
- **THEN** neither the relationship to B nor the backlink from C is returned

#### Scenario: Repeated one-hop calls

- **GIVEN** readable nodes A, B and C have relationships from A to B and from B to C, and none from A to C
- **WHEN** the caller requests A's discourse context
- **THEN** the call doesn't traverse B to return C
- **AND** a later request for B's discourse context returns the relationship to C

### Requirement: Readable synced collection <!-- roam:RfGa1ASkz -->

All retrieval operations SHALL use already-synced discourse data readable by the caller's space account. Local import status and authorship SHALL NOT restrict that collection. Results MUST NOT imply that the returned nodes were imported into the client application.

#### Scenario: Readable but unimported node

- **GIVEN** a synced discourse node is readable by the caller, but was authored elsewhere and never imported into its client
- **WHEN** the caller fetches it or searches for it
- **THEN** the node is eligible for retrieval and search ranking
- **AND** the response does not claim the node was imported locally

#### Scenario: Unreadable node

- **WHEN** a caller requests a node it cannot read
- **THEN** retrieval returns neither the node's content nor its metadata

### Requirement: Nodes and types are identified by rid

Every operation SHALL identify a node by its `rid` (global node ID), and a node type by the type's `rid`. Type filters SHALL take type `rid`s. Types with the same name in different spaces SHALL stay separate.

#### Scenario: Same-named types in two spaces

- **GIVEN** two readable spaces each define a type named "Claim"
- **WHEN** the caller discovers node types
- **THEN** it sees two types with different `rid`s

### Requirement: Full node text <!-- roam:M6O5NmufQ -->

Getting a readable node SHALL return the following:

- its `rid` (global node ID) and title;
- its type, as the type's `rid` and name (for example "Claim");
- its full synced text body;
- its provenance:
  - the author's name;
  - the space's name, platform and URL;
  - its created and modified times;
  - a link to open it at the source when the platform has one (a Roam page URL), or else its file path (an Obsidian vault path).

The body SHALL be the stored synced text, not content fetched live from the client application. Attachment downloads and file contents SHALL stay outside this operation.

#### Scenario: Get a node with body text and attachment links

- **WHEN** a caller fetches a readable synced node whose text links to an attachment
- **THEN** it receives the required node fields and the full stored text, including the source links in that text
- **AND** the response doesn't download or embed the attachment's file contents

#### Scenario: Readable type and author

- **GIVEN** a readable Claim node written by Trang in the "Lab" space
- **WHEN** a caller fetches it
- **THEN** the response names the type "Claim", the author "Trang" and the space "Lab", alongside the type's `rid`

### Requirement: Semantic search over existing embeddings <!-- roam:Mcp8fO0Ya -->

Search SHALL rank nodes by semantic similarity using the stored embeddings, without re-embedding. Sync embeds every node's title, on both platforms. Roam also embeds the description with the title when a node has one. Bodies aren't embedded on either platform, so matching covers titles (and Roam descriptions), not full bodies. V0 SHALL NOT require keyword matching or hybrid ranking.

#### Scenario: Matching by meaning

- **WHEN** a caller submits a query, and eligible nodes have current embeddings
- **THEN** a node can rank even when its title lacks the query's exact words

#### Scenario: Existing title-plus-description embedding

- **GIVEN** a readable Roam node has an embedding generated from its title and description
- **WHEN** the caller searches
- **THEN** that embedding contributes to ranking

#### Scenario: Body-only changes

- **GIVEN** the title, description, permissions and filters are unchanged
- **WHEN** only a node's full synced body changes
- **THEN** the node's search ranking doesn't change

### Requirement: Search result fields

Each search result SHALL contain the same identity, type and provenance fields as get-node, plus a short excerpt and a relevance score, but not the full body. Results SHALL be ordered by relevance.

#### Scenario: Result fields

- **WHEN** a search returns results
- **THEN** each result has those fields, and the results are ordered by score

### Requirement: Bounded search without a relevance cutoff <!-- roam:C7DJ2nVgj -->

Search SHALL default to 10 results and accept a limit from 1 to 30. A limit outside that range SHALL be rejected. V0 SHALL NOT paginate. Search SHALL NOT discard eligible nodes because their relevance is low. An empty result SHALL mean that no searchable nodes meet the access and type constraints.

#### Scenario: Default and explicit limits

- **GIVEN** at least 30 eligible searchable nodes
- **WHEN** the caller searches without a limit, and then with a limit of 20
- **THEN** the responses contain 10 results and 20 results
- **AND** neither response offers a continuation page

#### Scenario: Weak matches

- **GIVEN** three eligible searchable nodes that match the query weakly, and a limit of 10
- **WHEN** the caller searches
- **THEN** all three are returned in relevance order

#### Scenario: Limit above the maximum

- **WHEN** a request asks for more than 30 results
- **THEN** it is rejected as an invalid request

#### Scenario: Empty eligible collection

- **WHEN** no searchable nodes meet the caller's access and type constraints
- **THEN** search returns an empty result

### Requirement: Readable type discovery and filtering <!-- roam:xtDHC9uuv -->

Type discovery SHALL return type `rid`s (global type IDs) and names, only for types present on nodes the caller can currently read. That includes types on shared nodes. Search SHALL accept one or more type `rid`s and match any of them. Without a filter, search SHALL cover all eligible types.

#### Scenario: Discover types from readable nodes

- **GIVEN** type A is on a readable shared node, and type B is only on unreadable nodes
- **WHEN** the caller discovers node types
- **THEN** type A is listed and type B is not

#### Scenario: Multiple selected types

- **WHEN** the caller searches with types A and B selected
- **THEN** every result has type A or B, and is readable by the caller

#### Scenario: No type filter

- **WHEN** the caller searches without a type filter
- **THEN** no eligible node is excluded because of its type

### Requirement: One-hop discourse context <!-- roam:IffvWYML9 -->

Discourse context SHALL return the incoming and outgoing explicit discourse relationships of a readable node. Each relationship SHALL give:

- its type;
- its direction relative to the requested node;
- the connected node's `rid` (global node ID), title, type (`rid` and name), author name and space name.

Both endpoints MUST be readable. Ordinary backlinks SHALL be excluded. Connected bodies SHALL be retrieved separately, through get-node. A single call SHALL NOT go past one hop.

#### Scenario: Incoming and outgoing relationships

- **GIVEN** readable nodes A and B have an explicit relationship from A to B
- **WHEN** the caller requests discourse context for A, and then for B
- **THEN** the relationship is outgoing for A and incoming for B, each with the connected node's summary

#### Scenario: Inaccessible endpoint and ordinary backlink

- **GIVEN** readable node A has an explicit relationship to unreadable node B, and an ordinary backlink from readable node C
- **WHEN** the caller requests A's discourse context
- **THEN** neither the relationship to B nor the backlink from C is returned

#### Scenario: Repeated one-hop calls

- **GIVEN** readable nodes A, B and C have relationships from A to B and from B to C, and none from A to C
- **WHEN** the caller requests A's discourse context
- **THEN** the call doesn't traverse B to return C
- **AND** a later request for B's discourse context returns the relationship to C

# Spec Delta

## Purpose

How callers reach the retrieval operations: HTTP routes, session auth, the response envelope and the versioned contract. Developers call the API directly, and the MCP calls it on behalf of agent clients. What the operations return is specified in `discourse-retrieval` (retrieval behavior).

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Four retrieval operations <!-- roam:9iZVchr-f -->

The system SHALL provide an HTTP API for four operations: get-node, search-nodes, discover-node-types and get-discourse-context. These operations SHALL follow the `discourse-retrieval` (retrieval behavior) contract. The API SHALL be the only retrieval backend for the MCP.

#### Scenario: Developer calls each operation directly

- **WHEN** a developer calls each of the four operations with a valid session token
- **THEN** each operation applies the shared retrieval and authorization rules
- **AND** no MCP is required

### Requirement: Response envelope

Every API response SHALL carry a request ID, plus either `data` or an error object with a stable code and a safe message. An error SHALL NOT be returned as an empty `data` collection.

#### Scenario: Failed request

- **WHEN** an operation fails
- **THEN** the response has a request ID and an error object, with a stable code and a message that doesn't expose internals
- **AND** the response has no `data`

### Requirement: Authenticated sessions

The API SHALL accept a valid session token for a space account. It SHALL reject missing, invalid and expired tokens, and SHALL NOT store tokens between requests. The API SHALL expose only read operations. Read-only access for agent sessions is enforced by the database, as specified in `agent-read-access` (the agent's session).

#### Scenario: Missing or expired token

- **WHEN** a request carries no token, or an expired one
- **THEN** the API rejects it as unauthenticated, and returns no discourse data

### Requirement: Versioned contract

The API SHALL serve its operations under a version prefix such as `/api/v1`. Changes within a version SHALL be additive. A breaking change SHALL ship under a new version, alongside the old one.

#### Scenario: An installed MCP after a server change

- **GIVEN** an installed MCP built against `/api/v1`
- **WHEN** the website deploys a change within `/api/v1`
- **THEN** the installed MCP's requests keep working

### Requirement: Documented developer contract <!-- roam:OlfosIASW -->

The API documentation SHALL cover:

- authentication, including how to get a session token;
- inputs and outputs;
- errors;
- search limits;
- type-filter semantics;
- the per-space access model.

The documentation SHALL also explain that:

- readable nodes can appear even if they were never imported;
- search matches titles and descriptions by meaning, not by exact words;
- search can return weak matches;
- v0 search has no pagination.

#### Scenario: Set up a direct integration

- **WHEN** a developer follows the API documentation with a session token
- **THEN** the documentation gives a working example for each of the four operations, and explains their results and errors

### Requirement: Headless retrieval after setup <!-- roam:UCHDnQtCv -->

After handoff and sync, the API SHALL work without Roam or Obsidian open. Responses SHALL come from the database's synced state.

#### Scenario: Source application is closed

- **GIVEN** a user has synced nodes and a session token
- **WHEN** Roam and Obsidian are closed, and a caller calls the API
- **THEN** eligible synced data is returned

# Spec Delta

## Purpose

What the API's four retrieval operations return, whichever client calls them: which nodes are eligible, node payloads, semantic search, type discovery, and one-hop discourse context. All of it stays within the caller's current read access. The API exposes these operations over HTTP (`headless-retrieval-api`), and the MCP passes their results through (`discourse-mcp`).

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Readable synced collection <!-- roam:RfGa1ASkz -->

All retrieval operations SHALL use already-synced discourse data readable by the caller's space account. Local import status and authorship SHALL NOT restrict that collection. Results MUST NOT imply that the returned nodes were imported into the client application.

#### Scenario: Readable but unimported node

- **GIVEN** a synced discourse node is readable by the caller, but was authored elsewhere and never imported into its client
- **WHEN** the caller fetches it or searches for it
- **THEN** the node is eligible for retrieval and search ranking
- **AND** the response does not claim the node was imported locally

#### Scenario: Unreadable node

- **WHEN** a caller requests a node it cannot read
- **THEN** retrieval returns neither the node's content nor its metadata

### Requirement: Nodes and types are identified by rid

Every operation SHALL identify a node by its `rid` (global node ID), and a node type by the type's `rid`. Type filters SHALL take type `rid`s. Types with the same name in different spaces SHALL stay separate.

#### Scenario: Same-named types in two spaces

- **GIVEN** two readable spaces each define a type named "Claim"
- **WHEN** the caller discovers node types
- **THEN** it sees two types with different `rid`s

### Requirement: Full node text <!-- roam:M6O5NmufQ -->

Getting a readable node SHALL return the following:

- its `rid` (global node ID) and title;
- its type, as the type's `rid` and name (for example "Claim");
- its full synced text body;
- its provenance:
  - the author's name;
  - the space's name, platform and URL;
  - its created and modified times;
  - a link to open it at the source when the platform has one (a Roam page URL), or else its file path (an Obsidian vault path).

The body SHALL be the stored synced text, not content fetched live from the client application. Attachment downloads and file contents SHALL stay outside this operation.

#### Scenario: Get a node with body text and attachment links

- **WHEN** a caller fetches a readable synced node whose text links to an attachment
- **THEN** it receives the required node fields and the full stored text, including the source links in that text
- **AND** the response doesn't download or embed the attachment's file contents

#### Scenario: Readable type and author

- **GIVEN** a readable Claim node written by Trang in the "Lab" space
- **WHEN** a caller fetches it
- **THEN** the response names the type "Claim", the author "Trang" and the space "Lab", alongside the type's `rid`

### Requirement: Semantic search over existing embeddings <!-- roam:Mcp8fO0Ya -->

Search SHALL rank nodes by semantic similarity using the stored embeddings, without re-embedding. Sync embeds every node's title, on both platforms. Roam also embeds the description with the title when a node has one. Bodies aren't embedded on either platform, so matching covers titles (and Roam descriptions), not full bodies. V0 SHALL NOT require keyword matching or hybrid ranking.

#### Scenario: Matching by meaning

- **WHEN** a caller submits a query, and eligible nodes have current embeddings
- **THEN** a node can rank even when its title lacks the query's exact words

#### Scenario: Titles on both platforms

- **GIVEN** a readable Roam node and a readable Obsidian node whose titles both match the query's meaning
- **WHEN** the caller searches
- **THEN** both nodes can rank

#### Scenario: Existing title-plus-description embedding

- **GIVEN** a readable Roam node has an embedding generated from its title and description
- **WHEN** the caller searches
- **THEN** that embedding contributes to ranking

#### Scenario: Body-only changes

- **GIVEN** the title, description, permissions and filters are unchanged
- **WHEN** only a node's full synced body changes
- **THEN** the node's search ranking doesn't change

### Requirement: Search result fields

Each search result SHALL contain the same identity, type and provenance fields as get-node, plus a short excerpt and a relevance score, but not the full body. Results SHALL be ordered by relevance.

#### Scenario: Result fields

- **WHEN** a search returns results
- **THEN** each result has those fields, and the results are ordered by score

### Requirement: Bounded search without a relevance cutoff <!-- roam:C7DJ2nVgj -->

Search SHALL default to 10 results and accept a limit from 1 to 30. A limit outside that range SHALL be rejected. V0 SHALL NOT paginate. Search SHALL NOT discard eligible nodes because their relevance is low. An empty result SHALL mean that no searchable nodes meet the access and type constraints.

#### Scenario: Default and explicit limits

- **GIVEN** at least 30 eligible searchable nodes
- **WHEN** the caller searches without a limit, and then with a limit of 20
- **THEN** the responses contain 10 results and 20 results
- **AND** neither response offers a continuation page

#### Scenario: Weak matches

- **GIVEN** three eligible searchable nodes that match the query weakly, and a limit of 10
- **WHEN** the caller searches
- **THEN** all three are returned in relevance order

#### Scenario: Limit above the maximum

- **WHEN** a request asks for more than 30 results
- **THEN** it is rejected as an invalid request

#### Scenario: Empty eligible collection

- **WHEN** no searchable nodes meet the caller's access and type constraints
- **THEN** search returns an empty result

### Requirement: Readable type discovery and filtering <!-- roam:xtDHC9uuv -->

Type discovery SHALL return type `rid`s (global type IDs) and names, only for types present on nodes the caller can currently read. That includes types on shared nodes. Search SHALL accept one or more type `rid`s and match any of them. Without a filter, search SHALL cover all eligible types.

#### Scenario: Discover types from readable nodes

- **GIVEN** type A is on a readable shared node, and type B is only on unreadable nodes
- **WHEN** the caller discovers node types
- **THEN** type A is listed and type B is not

#### Scenario: Multiple selected types

- **WHEN** the caller searches with types A and B selected
- **THEN** every result has type A or B, and is readable by the caller

#### Scenario: No type filter

- **WHEN** the caller searches without a type filter
- **THEN** no eligible node is excluded because of its type

### Requirement: One-hop discourse context <!-- roam:IffvWYML9 -->

Discourse context SHALL return the incoming and outgoing explicit discourse relationships of a readable node. Each relationship SHALL give:

- its type;
- its direction relative to the requested node;
- the connected node's `rid` (global node ID), title, type (`rid` and name), author name and space name.

Both endpoints MUST be readable. Ordinary backlinks SHALL be excluded. Connected bodies SHALL be retrieved separately, through get-node. A single call SHALL NOT go past one hop.

#### Scenario: Incoming and outgoing relationships

- **GIVEN** readable nodes A and B have an explicit relationship from A to B
- **WHEN** the caller requests discourse context for A, and then for B
- **THEN** the relationship is outgoing for A and incoming for B, each with the connected node's summary

#### Scenario: Inaccessible endpoint and ordinary backlink

- **GIVEN** readable node A has an explicit relationship to unreadable node B, and an ordinary backlink from readable node C
- **WHEN** the caller requests A's discourse context
- **THEN** neither the relationship to B nor the backlink from C is returned

#### Scenario: Repeated one-hop calls

- **GIVEN** readable nodes A, B and C have relationships from A to B and from B to C, and none from A to C
- **WHEN** the caller requests A's discourse context
- **THEN** the call doesn't traverse B to return C
- **AND** a later request for B's discourse context returns the relationship to C

# Spec Delta

## Purpose

How callers reach the retrieval operations: HTTP routes, session auth, the response envelope and the versioned contract. Developers call the API directly, and the MCP calls it on behalf of agent clients. What the operations return is specified in `discourse-retrieval` (retrieval behavior).

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Four retrieval operations <!-- roam:9iZVchr-f -->

The system SHALL provide an HTTP API for four operations: get-node, search-nodes, discover-node-types and get-discourse-context. These operations SHALL follow the `discourse-retrieval` (retrieval behavior) contract. The API SHALL be the only retrieval backend for the MCP.

#### Scenario: Developer calls each operation directly

- **WHEN** a developer calls each of the four operations with a valid session token
- **THEN** each operation applies the shared retrieval and authorization rules
- **AND** no MCP is required

### Requirement: Response envelope

Every API response SHALL carry a request ID, plus either `data` or an error object with a stable code and a safe message. An error SHALL NOT be returned as an empty `data` collection.

#### Scenario: Failed request

- **WHEN** an operation fails
- **THEN** the response has a request ID and an error object, with a stable code and a message that doesn't expose internals
- **AND** the response has no `data`

### Requirement: Authenticated sessions

The API SHALL accept a valid session token for a space account. It SHALL reject missing, invalid and expired tokens, and SHALL NOT store tokens between requests. The API SHALL expose only read operations. Read-only access for agent sessions is enforced by the database, as specified in `agent-read-access` (the agent's session).

#### Scenario: Missing or expired token

- **WHEN** a request carries no token, or an expired one
- **THEN** the API rejects it as unauthenticated, and returns no discourse data

### Requirement: Versioned contract

The API SHALL serve its operations under a version prefix such as `/api/v1`. Changes within a version SHALL be additive. A breaking change SHALL ship under a new version, alongside the old one.

#### Scenario: An installed MCP after a server change

- **GIVEN** an installed MCP built against `/api/v1`
- **WHEN** the website deploys a change within `/api/v1`
- **THEN** the installed MCP's requests keep working

### Requirement: Documented developer contract <!-- roam:OlfosIASW -->

The API documentation SHALL cover:

- authentication, including how to get a session token;
- inputs and outputs;
- errors;
- search limits;
- type-filter semantics;
- the per-space access model.

The documentation SHALL also explain that:

- readable nodes can appear even if they were never imported;
- search matches node titles (and Roam descriptions) by meaning, not by exact words, and doesn't search bodies;
- search can return weak matches;
- v0 search has no pagination.

#### Scenario: Set up a direct integration

- **WHEN** a developer follows the API documentation with a session token
- **THEN** the documentation gives a working example for each of the four operations, and explains their results and errors

### Requirement: Headless retrieval after setup <!-- roam:UCHDnQtCv -->

After handoff and sync, the API SHALL work without Roam or Obsidian open. Responses SHALL come from the database's synced state.

#### Scenario: Source application is closed

- **GIVEN** a user has synced nodes and a session token
- **WHEN** Roam and Obsidian are closed, and a caller calls the API
- **THEN** eligible synced data is returned

## What Changes

- **A retrieval API** at `/api/v1` (versioned HTTP routes) in `apps/website`, with four read-only operations: get a node, search nodes, list node types, and get discourse context. It is the one retrieval service: documented for developers, and the only backend of the MCP.
- **A local MCP** that exposes each API operation as a tool. Users install it from npm, and the agent client launches it. Supported clients: Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex.
- **Identity follows Option A2** ([decision](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/guIcK3Z9M), [options compared](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/bTMUCrCnD)): the agent signs in as the space account, but the database makes its session read-only. It was decided at the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product meeting. The session is handed over through `mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/kPg_0_-lh)).

# Proposal

<!-- Supersedes the 2026-09-25 version of this change in Roam (block LPDwCRT6_). -->

## Why

Users want to retrieve relevant synced discourse nodes from their agent, or from their own code, without opening Roam or Obsidian, and without a separate integration for each platform. This v0 ships a retrieval API and a local MCP that exposes that API to agent clients. The MCP uses a read-only session of the space account, handed over by the plugin.

## What Changes

- **A retrieval API** at `/api/v1` (versioned HTTP routes) in `apps/website`, with four read-only operations: get a node, search nodes, list node types, and get discourse context. It is the one retrieval service: documented for developers, and the only backend of the MCP.
- **A local MCP** that exposes each API operation as a tool. Users install it from npm, and the agent client launches it. Supported clients: Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex.
- **Identity follows Option A2** ([decision](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/guIcK3Z9M), [options compared](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/bTMUCrCnD)): the agent signs in as the space account, but the database makes its session read-only. It was decided at the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product meeting. The session is handed over through `mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/kPg_0_-lh)).
- **Coverage.** Retrieval covers every synced discourse node the space account can read under its current access, including shared nodes that were never imported into the client.
- **Node shape.** Nodes come back as `DbCrossAppNode`s (the shared node format from [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091)), identified by `rid` (global node ID). They reuse discovery's converters and its `{ nodes, spaces }` envelope. Node types are identified by type `rid`.
- **Search is semantic.** It reuses the stored embeddings through one new search RPC (database function), with type filtering and no relevance cutoff.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `discourse-retrieval`: **what the API's four operations return.** Covers which nodes are eligible, node payloads, semantic search, type discovery and one-hop discourse context.
- `headless-retrieval-api`: **how callers reach those operations.** Covers the HTTP routes, session auth, the response envelope and the versioned contract.
- `discourse-mcp`: **how agent clients reach the API.** Covers four tools that pass API results through, plus setup and distribution.
- `agent-read-access`: **the session an agent holds.** It is handed over by the plugin, reads with the space account's current access, and the database keeps it read-only.

### Modified Capabilities

- None. The repository has no OpenSpec capability specs yet.

## Out of scope for v0

- A hosted MCP and ChatGPT support. ChatGPT can't launch a local MCP; a hosted MCP can later wrap the same API.
- Option B, a separate agent account.
- Writes, candidate nodes, non-discourse content, canvas functions, and attachment contents.
- Multi-hop traversal, re-embedding, pagination, relevance thresholds, and imported-only filtering.
- Keyword or hybrid search. It's proposed for after v0, adapting [Supabase's hybrid search recipe](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai/hybrid-search) (design Decision 6).
- One session that spans several spaces.

## Impact

- **`packages/database`:**
  - `mcp_reader` (read-only database role);
  - a custom access token hook (assigns that role at sign-in);
  - an `EXECUTE` allowlist (which database functions the role may call);
  - the space login lock (stops a session from replacing the space login);
  - retrieval functions built on the discovery converters;
  - one semantic search RPC (database function).
- **`apps/website`:** the four API routes and their documentation.
- **A new MCP package** (`apps/mcp`, location proposed), published to npm.
- **Hosted Supabase settings:** the access token hook and the space login lock (design Decision 4).
- **Depends on `mcp-session-access`** (the [session handoff spec](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/kPg_0_-lh)) for the handoff, the `mcp_session` registry (list of handed-over sessions) and sign-out.
- **Builds on** [ENG-1985](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1985) (database-to-node converter) and [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091) (discovery returns shared nodes), both merged. They provide `dbNodeToCrossApp` (converts one node), `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID) and `SharedNodeListing` (nodes plus their spaces).

## Open decisions

- Whether one agent should span several spaces.
- Michael hasn't confirmed reusing `CrossAppNode` (the shared node format) and `rid` (global node ID) for the agent API ([Roam block](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/SRa9xHk30)).
- No relevance or latency target is agreed, and the real-query evaluation set doesn't exist yet.

# Spec Delta

## Purpose

How callers reach the retrieval operations: HTTP routes, session auth, the response envelope and the versioned contract. Developers call the API directly, and the MCP calls it on behalf of agent clients. What the operations return is specified in `discourse-retrieval` (retrieval behavior).

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Four retrieval operations <!-- roam:9iZVchr-f -->

The system SHALL provide an HTTP API for four operations: get-node, search-nodes, discover-node-types and get-discourse-context. These operations SHALL follow the `discourse-retrieval` (retrieval behavior) contract. The API SHALL be the only retrieval backend for the MCP.

#### Scenario: Developer calls each operation directly

- **WHEN** a developer calls each of the four operations with a valid session token
- **THEN** each operation applies the shared retrieval and authorization rules
- **AND** no MCP is required

### Requirement: Response envelope

Every API response SHALL carry a request ID, plus either `data` or an error object with a stable code and a safe message. An error SHALL NOT be returned as an empty `data` collection.

#### Scenario: Failed request

- **WHEN** an operation fails
- **THEN** the response has a request ID and an error object, with a stable code and a message that doesn't expose internals
- **AND** the response has no `data`

### Requirement: Authenticated sessions

The API SHALL accept a valid session token for a space account. It SHALL reject missing, invalid and expired tokens, and SHALL NOT store tokens between requests. The API SHALL expose only read operations. Read-only access for agent sessions is enforced by the database, as specified in `agent-read-access` (the agent's session).

#### Scenario: Missing or expired token

- **WHEN** a request carries no token, or an expired one
- **THEN** the API rejects it as unauthenticated, and returns no discourse data

### Requirement: Versioned contract

The API SHALL serve its operations under a version prefix such as `/api/v1`. Changes within a version SHALL be additive. A breaking change SHALL ship under a new version, alongside the old one.

#### Scenario: An installed MCP after a server change

- **GIVEN** an installed MCP built against `/api/v1`
- **WHEN** the website deploys a change within `/api/v1`
- **THEN** the installed MCP's requests keep working

### Requirement: Headless retrieval after setup <!-- roam:UCHDnQtCv -->

After handoff and sync, the API SHALL work without Roam or Obsidian open. Responses SHALL come from the database's synced state.

#### Scenario: Source application is closed

- **GIVEN** a user has synced nodes and a session token
- **WHEN** Roam and Obsidian are closed, and a caller calls the API
- **THEN** eligible synced data is returned

lines: The client config then holds only the launch command and `--name`, never a token.

- **Refresh.** The MCP refreshes against Supabase Auth. It writes each rotated refresh token to the state file atomically, before using the new session token. If the state file is lost, the user connects again with a new bundle.

- **One process per connection.** A lock file next to the state file stops a second process. Two processes refreshing the same token can make Supabase revoke the session. A user with two clients connects each one with its own bundle and `--name`.

-- **Token for developers.** `npx @discourse-graphs/mcp token --name <name>` prints a current session token for that connection, refreshing it under the lock. A developer connects with their own bundle and never handles refresh-token rotation.

content.text:
## Can cucumber test Roam or Obsidian?

No, and the task's wording made that unclear. The cucumber suite in `packages/database/features` runs against a local Supabase database. A step like "the user opens the Roam plugin in space s1" simulates the plugin's database calls; it doesn't run Roam. There are Roam-style steps today but no Obsidian ones.

So "Roam and Obsidian fixtures" can only mean database rows shaped like each platform's sync output:
- **Roam-style rows:** a title, or a title plus description.
- **Obsidian-style rows:** a title taken from the file name, with `filePath` stored in the title row's metadata.

That needs a new Obsidian step definition.

## Is it the right place to test retrieval?

You're right that it's the wrong layer for most of it. `apps/website` already has `test:integration`: vitest tests that call real routes against the local database (for example `test/integration/listGroupMembers.test.ts`). That suits retrieval behavior, because it exercises the routes, the functions and row-level security together, the way the MCP will.

**Proposed split (not applied):**

| Layer | Test with | Tasks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Database permissions: the read-only role, the hook, refused writes, the space login lock | Cucumber, because these are database rules | Group 1 (no change) |
| Search query logic: filtering before the limit, deduplication, negative similarity, deterministic vectors | Cucumber, because it's SQL behavior | 3.1 (no change) |
| Retrieval behavior: payload fields, `not_found` vs `content_unavailable`, type and author names, source link or path, relation readability, shared vs private nodes | API integration tests in `apps/website`, seeded with Roam-style and Obsidian-style rows | 2.1–2.4 and 3.2 move their verify steps here |

**Edits that split implies:**
- Tasks 2.1–2.4 and 3.2 change "cucumber scenarios on Roam and Obsidian fixtures" to "`apps/website` integration tests through the `/api/v1` routes, with Roam-style and Obsidian-style seed rows".
- Task 4.3 says it reuses that seeding.
- A small new task adds a seeding helper for both row shapes.

## API docs

They're missing because I removed them last round, when you said external developers aren't a concern. The only docs left are the MCP setup README for agent users. The contract itself lives in design Decision 8 plus the shared Zod schemas.

Two options:
- **A. Internal API reference.** A short `README` next to the routes covers each route, its input and output, the envelope, error codes and auth. It's for whoever maintains the MCP or wraps the API later, with no `curl` tutorials or developer onboarding. This adds one task.
- **B. No API docs in v0.** Decision 8 and the Zod schemas serve as the reference until external developers matter.

I lean towards A. It's cheap, and the `/api/v1` contract has to stay stable for installed MCP copies, so it's worth writing down next to the code.

content.text:
I applied the test split and added the internal API reference. `openspec validate --strict` passes.

**Test split (`tasks.md`)**
- **Cucumber now covers only database rules:**
  - group 1: the read-only role, the hook, refused writes and the space login lock;
  - task 3.1: the search query's logic, using deterministic vectors.
- **New task 4.5: API integration tests in `apps/website`.**
  - They call the `/api/v1` routes with a handed-over session, against the local database.
  - A seeding helper writes Roam-style rows and Obsidian-style rows, so no Roam or Obsidian app is involved.
  - They cover every case the cucumber steps listed for get-node, type discovery, discourse context and access (shared vs private, access changing after handoff), plus the search result fields on each platform.
- **Group 2:** its tasks now point to 4.5 for verification. A note says group 2 lands before group 4 or together with it, because it's tested through the routes. The old task 2.4 ("run as `mcp_reader`") is folded into 4.5's access cases.
- **Task 2.3:** now says to drop relations with an unreadable type or endpoint before converting, matching the design.
- **Task 3.2:** keeps unit tests for the excerpt, which is a pure function, and leaves the result fields to 4.5.

**Internal API reference**
- **New task 4.6:** a `README` next to the routes for whoever maintains the MCP or the API. It covers inputs and outputs, the envelope, error codes and HTTP statuses, session auth and the additive-only rule for `/api/v1`. The PR reviewer checks it against the Zod schemas.
- **Design Decision 8:** gets a one-line pointer to that `README`.

**Design risk line:** the missing-grant risk now says the API integration tests run every operation as `mcp_reader`.

One thing I haven't checked: whether `apps/website`'s integration setup can sign in as a handed-over session. That depends on `mcp-session-access` landing first, which the tasks header already lists as a dependency.

content.content:
- # Proposal
  - ## Why
    - Users want to retrieve relevant synced discourse nodes from their agent, or from their own code, without opening Roam or Obsidian, and without a separate integration for each platform. This v0 ships a retrieval API and a local MCP that exposes that API to agent clients. The MCP uses a read-only session of the space account, handed over by the plugin.
  - ## What Changes
    - **A retrieval API** at `/api/v1` (versioned HTTP routes) in `apps/website`, with four read-only operations: get a node, search nodes, list node types, and get discourse context. It is the one retrieval service and the only backend of the MCP.
    - **A local MCP** that exposes each API operation as a tool. Users install it from npm, and the agent client launches it. Supported clients: Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex.
    - **Identity follows Option A2** ([decision](((guIcK3Z9M))), [options compared](((bTMUCrCnD)))): the agent signs in as the space account, but the database makes its session read-only. It was decided at the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product meeting. The session is handed over through `mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec]([[Spec: MCP token handoff]])).
    - **Coverage.** Retrieval covers every synced discourse node the space account can read under its current access, including shared nodes that were never imported into the client.
    - **Node shape.** Nodes come back as `DbCrossAppNode`s (the shared node format from [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091)), identified by `rid` (global node ID). They reuse discovery's converters and its `{ nodes, spaces }` envelope. Node types are identified by type `rid`.
    - **Search is semantic.** It reuses the stored embeddings through one new search RPC (database function), with type filtering and no relevance cutoff.
  - ## Capabilities
    - ### New Capabilities
      - `discourse-retrieval`: **what the API's four operations return.** Covers which nodes are eligible, node payloads, semantic search, type discovery and one-hop discourse context.
      - `headless-retrieval-api`: **how callers reach those operations.** Covers the HTTP routes, session auth, the response envelope and the versioned contract.
      - `discourse-mcp`: **how agent clients reach the API.** Covers four tools that pass API results through, plus setup and distribution.
      - `agent-read-access`: **the session an agent holds.** It is handed over by the plugin, reads with the space account's current access, and the database keeps it read-only.
    - ### Modified Capabilities
      - None. The repository has no OpenSpec capability specs yet.
  - ## Out of scope for v0
    - A hosted MCP and ChatGPT support. ChatGPT can't launch a local MCP; a hosted MCP can later wrap the same API.
    - Option B, a separate agent account.
    - Writes, candidate nodes, non-discourse content, canvas functions, and attachment contents.
    - Multi-hop traversal, re-embedding, pagination, relevance thresholds, and imported-only filtering.
    - Keyword or hybrid search. It's proposed for after v0, adapting [Supabase's hybrid search recipe](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai/hybrid-search) (design Decision 6).
    - One session that spans several spaces.
  - ## Impact
    - **`packages/database`:**
      - `mcp_reader` (read-only database role);
      - a custom access token hook (assigns that role at sign-in);
      - an `EXECUTE` allowlist (which database functions the role may call);
      - the space login lock (stops a session from replacing the space login);
      - retrieval functions built on the discovery converters;
      - one semantic search RPC (database function).
    - **`apps/website`:** the four API routes and their documentation.
    - **A new MCP package** (`apps/mcp`, location proposed), published to npm.
    - **Hosted Supabase settings:** the access token hook and the space login lock (design Decision 4).
    - **Depends on `mcp-session-access`** (the [session handoff spec]([[Spec: MCP token handoff]])) for the handoff, the `mcp_session` registry (list of handed-over sessions) and sign-out.
    - **Builds on** [ENG-1985](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1985) (database-to-node converter) and [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091) (discovery returns shared nodes), both merged. They provide `dbNodeToCrossApp` (converts one node), `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID) and `SharedNodeListing` (nodes plus their spaces).
  - ## Open decisions
    - Whether one agent should span several spaces.
    - Michael hasn't confirmed reusing `CrossAppNode` (the shared node format) and `rid` (global node ID) for the agent API ([Roam block](((SRa9xHk30)))).
    - No relevance or latency target is agreed, and the real-query evaluation set doesn't exist yet.

# Proposal

<!-- Supersedes the 2026-09-25 version of this change in Roam (block LPDwCRT6_). -->

## Why

Users want to retrieve relevant synced discourse nodes from their agent, or from their own code, without opening Roam or Obsidian, and without a separate integration for each platform. This v0 ships a retrieval API and a local MCP that exposes that API to agent clients. The MCP uses a read-only session of the space account, handed over by the plugin.

## What Changes

- **A retrieval API** at `/api/v1` (versioned HTTP routes) in `apps/website`, with four read-only operations: get a node, search nodes, list node types, and get discourse context. It is the one retrieval service and the only backend of the MCP.
- **A local MCP** that exposes each API operation as a tool. Users install it from npm, and the agent client launches it. Supported clients: Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex.
- **Identity follows Option A2** ([decision](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/guIcK3Z9M), [options compared](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/bTMUCrCnD)): the agent signs in as the space account, but the database makes its session read-only. It was decided at the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product meeting. The session is handed over through `mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/kPg_0_-lh)).
- **Coverage.** Retrieval covers every synced discourse node the space account can read under its current access, including shared nodes that were never imported into the client.
- **Node shape.** Nodes come back as `DbCrossAppNode`s (the shared node format from [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091)), identified by `rid` (global node ID). They reuse discovery's converters and its `{ nodes, spaces }` envelope. Node types are identified by type `rid`.
- **Search is semantic.** It reuses the stored embeddings through one new search RPC (database function), with type filtering and no relevance cutoff.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `discourse-retrieval`: **what the API's four operations return.** Covers which nodes are eligible, node payloads, semantic search, type discovery and one-hop discourse context.
- `headless-retrieval-api`: **how callers reach those operations.** Covers the HTTP routes, session auth, the response envelope and the versioned contract.
- `discourse-mcp`: **how agent clients reach the API.** Covers four tools that pass API results through, plus setup and distribution.
- `agent-read-access`: **the session an agent holds.** It is handed over by the plugin, reads with the space account's current access, and the database keeps it read-only.

### Modified Capabilities

- None. The repository has no OpenSpec capability specs yet.

## Out of scope for v0

- A hosted MCP and ChatGPT support. ChatGPT can't launch a local MCP; a hosted MCP can later wrap the same API.
- Option B, a separate agent account.
- Writes, candidate nodes, non-discourse content, canvas functions, and attachment contents.
- Multi-hop traversal, re-embedding, pagination, relevance thresholds, and imported-only filtering.
- Keyword or hybrid search. It's proposed for after v0, adapting [Supabase's hybrid search recipe](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai/hybrid-search) (design Decision 6).
- One session that spans several spaces.

## Impact

- **`packages/database`:**
  - `mcp_reader` (read-only database role);
  - a custom access token hook (assigns that role at sign-in);
  - an `EXECUTE` allowlist (which database functions the role may call);
  - the space login lock (stops a session from replacing the space login);
  - retrieval functions built on the discovery converters;
  - one semantic search RPC (database function).
- **`apps/website`:** the four API routes and their documentation.
- **A new MCP package** (`apps/mcp`, location proposed), published to npm.
- **Hosted Supabase settings:** the access token hook and the space login lock (design Decision 4).
- **Depends on `mcp-session-access`** (the [session handoff spec](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/kPg_0_-lh)) for the handoff, the `mcp_session` registry (list of handed-over sessions) and sign-out.
- **Builds on** [ENG-1985](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1985) (database-to-node converter) and [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091) (discovery returns shared nodes), both merged. They provide `dbNodeToCrossApp` (converts one node), `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID) and `SharedNodeListing` (nodes plus their spaces).

## Open decisions

- Whether one agent should span several spaces.
- Michael hasn't confirmed reusing `CrossAppNode` (the shared node format) and `rid` (global node ID) for the agent API ([Roam block](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/SRa9xHk30)).
- No relevance or latency target is agreed, and the real-query evaluation set doesn't exist yet.

1 - # Design 2 - ## Context 3 - These facts from `origin/main` shape the design. 4 - **Identity and data** 5 - **Space accounts.** Each plugin signs in as its space's account using the **space login**, a random secret stored in the plugin (`signInWithPassword` in `packages/database/src/lib/contextFunctions.ts`). There are no personal user accounts yet. 6 - **Session handoff.** `mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec]([[Spec: MCP token handoff]])) lets the plugin use the space login to open one extra session, and hand that session's refresh token to the MCP. The MCP stores only that session, never the space login. Each handed-over session is recorded in `mcp_session` (list of handed-over sessions). Roam embeds the title plus description instead (`direct_and_description`) when a node has a description. apps/website /api/v1"] 46 - api --> fns["Retrieval functions
packages/database"] 47 - fns --> db[("Supabase Postgres
row-level security")] 48 - api -- "search text only" --> emb["OpenAI embeddings API
turns query text into a vector"] 49 - OpenAI here is only the embeddings service that turns a search query into a vector, the same one sync already uses. It isn't ChatGPT, which stays unsupported. 50 - Each capability spec covers one layer: 51 - {{[[mermaid]]}} 52 - flowchart TB 53 - agent["Agent client"] --> tools 54 - subgraph mcpLayer["discourse-mcp: how agent clients reach the API"] 55 - tools["Four MCP tools
pass API results through"] 56 - end 57 - subgraph apiLayer["headless-retrieval-api: how callers reach the operations"] 58 - routes["API routes

They call `packages/database` functions with the caller's session, so row-level security applies. 66 - **The MCP** holds a session and maps each tool to one API call.
