The 2026-11-10 meeting chose a local MCP. A hosted MCP can still wrap this API later. 76 - ### 2. Reuse the discovery read path 77 - The API's routes call TypeScript functions in `packages/database`. These build on Sid's discovery code from [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091): 78 - **Get-node** calls `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID), then fetches the `full` Content (the body) the way import does. 79 - **Type discovery** reads node types from readable node instances and labels them with `dbNodeSchemasToCrossApp` (converts node types). 80 - **Discourse context** finds the readable relation instances that touch the node. 81 - Candidates come from `refs`, the list of referenced IDs. 82 - Direction comes from the `source` and `destination` keys of `reference_content` (the relation's endpoint map). 83 - Relations are converted with `dbRelationsToCrossApp` (converts relations). 84 - Only search needs a new RPC (database function); see Decision 6. 85 - **Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** four new RPCs, which would duplicate the converters. 86 - ### 3. Hand over a session through `mcp-session-access` 87 - `mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec]([[Spec: MCP token handoff]])) defines the handoff: 88 - **Handoff.** 89 - 1. The plugin opens a new session for the space account, using a second client that neither persists nor auto-refreshes. 90 - 2. It registers the session with `register_mcp_session(label)`. 91 - 3. It shows the bundle once: Supabase URL, anon key, space ID and refresh token. It keeps no copy. 92 - **Registry.** `mcp_session` (list of handed-over sessions) records the session ID (taken from the caller's own token), the label, the space account and the creation time. 93 - **Sign-out.** The holder can sign itself out with local scope (only its own session). Per-session sign-out from the plugin is proposed for right after v0. 94 - **Emergency switch.** Until then, the cut-off is to sign out every other session of the space account. That also signs out the other plugin instances, which sign back in with the space login. 95 - **Who can connect.** Any plugin user of the space. 96 - **Tokens.** Two tokens are involved: 97 - the **session token** is the session's short-lived access token, the one the API takes; 98 - the **refresh token** renews the session token, and it rotates on every use. 99 - The bundle carries only the refresh token. So the holder's first session token comes from a refresh, and it already carries `mcp_reader` (read-only database role; Decision 4). The plugin discards the `authenticated` session token it used to register. 100 - **Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** Option B, a separate agent account for each grant, with a credential issued from a website page. The 2026-11-10 meeting judged its security gain marginal for the extra work. 101 - ### 4. The database makes handed-over sessions read-only (A2) 102 - Under Option A2 ([decision](((guIcK3Z9M)))), the agent signs in as the space account, but the database makes its session read-only. The session token also works against Supabase directly, outside the API, so the database is what enforces read-only. 103 - **The hook.** A custom access token hook (a database function Supabase calls on every token issue and refresh) checks the token's `session_id`. When the session is in `mcp_session` (list of handed-over sessions), it sets the token's `role` claim to `mcp_reader` (read-only database role; name proposed). Other sessions keep `authenticated`. 104 - **The role.** `mcp_reader`: 105 - is granted to `authenticator` (the role Supabase's REST layer logs in as), so requests can switch to it; 106 - has `SELECT` on the tables and views retrieval reads, and no `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE`; 107 - has `EXECUTE` only on an allowlist: the search RPC, plus the access helpers that the policies and views call. 108 - **Locking down functions.** `PUBLIC` (every database role) holds `EXECUTE` on every function, so the allowlist needs two changes: 109 - `REVOKE EXECUTE ON ALL FUNCTIONS IN SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC`; 110 - the matching default-privilege change, so new functions aren't executable by default either. 111 - **This doesn't change what plugins or sync can do.** `base.sql` runs first and sets default privileges that grant every later function to `anon` and `authenticated` explicitly. So the plugins' roles don't rely on `PUBLIC`, and they keep every function they can call today. Postgres has no deny grant, and every role inherits `PUBLIC`, so removing that default is the only way to keep a function from `mcp_reader`. Before the revoke, a check on the hosted database confirms that `anon` and `authenticated` hold `EXECUTE` on every function. Its migrations predate the schema files, so it could differ. 112 - A test lists every function `mcp_reader` can execute and compares the list with the allowlist. Policies without a `TO` clause cover `mcp_reader`, so its reads follow the space account's current access. 113 - **Supabase Auth requests aren't covered by the role.** A handed-over session could ask Auth to replace the space login, which would lock out the plugins and let it open sessions that can write. This change turns on the **space login lock** (`secure_password_change` and "require current password"), which refuses that without the current space login. A session could also sign out the plugins' sessions; the plugins just sign back in, and signing out the handed-over session ends it. 114 - **A switched-off hook fails open.** Handed-over sessions would then get `authenticated`. The MCP refuses to start unless its session token carries `mcp_reader`, which catches a misconfigured project at setup. 115 - **Revocation waits for token expiry.** Sign-out stops refresh, but the current session token stays valid for up to `jwt_expiry` (session token lifetime, 3600 s). The 2026-11-10 meeting accepted this. 116 - **Alternative: plain Option A** (the agent signs in as the space account, with read-only enforced only in the MCP's tools). Any process holding the bundle could then write. The 2026-11-10 meeting chose A2 because the threat is overeager agent harnesses that bypass the MCP. 117 - ### 5. Nodes are CrossApp nodes, identified by `rid` 118 - **Identifiers** 119 - **Nodes.** A node's ID is its `rid` (global node ID), built by `spaceUriAndLocalIdToRid`. 120 - For an `http` space URI, it's `/`. 121 - Otherwise, it's `orn:.note:…/`. 122 - Look nodes up by space and `localId`, never by `localId` alone. 123 - **Types.** A type's ID is its `rid`, from `getNodeTypeRid`, never the space-relative `nodeType`. Type filters take type `rid`s, and same-named types in different spaces stay separate. 124 - **Payload** 125 - **Envelope.** Each operation returns `DbCrossAppNode`s (shared node format) in discovery's `{ nodes, spaces }` envelope. 126 - **Extra fields.** `DbCrossAppNode` carries IDs, not names, so each node also gets: 127 - `type`: `{ rid, name }`, with the name from `dbNodeSchemasToCrossApp` (converts node types); 128 - `author`: `{ name }`, from `PlatformAccount.name` through `my_accounts` (accounts the caller can see), because `authorId` is the platform's internal account ID; 129 - `sourceUrl` for Roam nodes, built as `/page/`, or `sourcePath` for Obsidian nodes, from the `filePath` in the title row's metadata, since an Obsidian note has no stable web URL. 130 - Search also adds a `score` and an `excerpt`. There's no separate agent node type. 131 - **Title and body.** The title is `content.direct`. Get-node adds `content.full` (the body) as stored text or markdown, never rendered HTML. 132 - **Links and assets.** Source links stay as text. Assets aren't fetched, and no storage URLs are minted. 133 - **Provenance.** It's the author's name, the space's name, platform and URL (from the `spaces` entry), the created and modified times, and the source link or path. Nothing implies the node exists in the caller's vault. 134 - **Gaps are errors** 135 - **Listings and search** skip rows the converter can't convert, as discovery does. 136 - **Get-node doesn't skip:** 137 - `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID) returns `null` for a missing or unreadable node, which maps to `not_found`. 138 - A conversion failure or a missing body maps to `content_unavailable`. 139 - A stored empty body is not a missing row. 140 - **Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** an agent-specific payload keyed by `Concept.id` (internal database row ID), which no plugin uses. It would give each node a second identity. 141 - ### 6. Semantic search through one new RPC 142 - **Embedding the query.** The API embeds the query on the server with `text-embedding-3-small` at 1536 dimensions. It uses the OpenAI client that `/api/embeddings/openai/small` builds inline today, extracted into a shared helper. Embedding happens only after the API has authenticated the caller. The MCP doesn't call the embedding route. 143 - **The search RPC** (`SECURITY INVOKER`, so it runs as the caller) takes the query vector, optional type `rid`s and a limit. It: 144 - joins the current, non-obsolete `direct` (title) and `direct_and_description` (title plus description) embeddings of readable node instances; 145 - keeps each node's best similarity, once; 146 - applies authorization, the type filter and deduplication before the limit; 147 - sorts by similarity, then by `rid`; 148 - has no similarity threshold, so negative similarities stay eligible. 149 - `score` is the cosine similarity. `match_content_embeddings` (the existing semantic search query) stays unchanged. 150 - **Other behavior** 151 - Nodes without a usable embedding are absent from search, but the other operations still reach them. 152 - Embedding failures are errors, not empty results. 153 - **The excerpt** is the first 300 Unicode code points of the body (`content.full`). When the body is missing, it falls back to `content.direct` (the title). The excerpt isn't evidence that the body matched. 154 - **Proposed for after v0: hybrid search.** Adapt [Supabase's hybrid search recipe](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai/hybrid-search). The recipe is a SQL function to copy, not a built-in. It: 155 - ranks rows by keyword (`websearch_to_tsquery`) and by vector similarity; 156 - merges the two rankings with Reciprocal Rank Fusion. 157 - Here it would need two schema additions on `Content` (the text table): a generated full-text column and a GIN index. The search RPC would gain a keyword list and a fusion step. The `/api/v1` search route keeps its inputs, so this is an additive change. Exact words such as names, acronyms and titles would then rank well even when the embedding misses them. 158 - ### 7. One-hop discourse context 159 - Return each readable relation instance that touches the node, with: 160 - its `rid` (global node ID); 161 - its type; 162 - its direction; 163 - a summary of the connected node. 164 - Rules: 165 - The relation, its type and both endpoints must be readable. Relations are read through `my_concepts` (filtered to what the caller can read) with the caller's session, so an unreadable relation never comes back. Drop a relation whose type or endpoint the caller can't read before converting it, because `dbRelationsToCrossApp` throws on a missing endpoint instead of skipping it. 166 - Keep relations distinct even when they share a label. 167 - A self-link appears as both incoming and outgoing. 168 - Don't follow ordinary backlinks, and don't go past one hop. 169 - ### 8. API contract 170 - {{[[table]]}} 171 - API route 172 - MCP tool 173 - Input 174 - `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}` 175 - `get_node` 176 - node `rid` 177 - `POST /api/v1/nodes/search` 178 - `search_nodes` 179 - query, optional type `rid`s, optional limit 180 - `GET /api/v1/node-types` 181 - `get_node_types` 182 - none 183 - `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}/context` 184 - `get_discourse_context` 185 - node `rid` 186 - `rid`s (global node IDs) contain `/` and `:`, so they go URL-encoded in the path. 187 - **Each route does three things:** 188 - 1. It validates the session token with Supabase Auth, then builds a request-scoped client that acts as the caller. Nothing is held between requests. 189 - 2. It validates the input with the shared Zod schemas (typed input and output definitions). 190 - 3. It calls one `packages/database` function. 191 - **Any session token is accepted.** The API accepts any valid space-account session token: a plugin's own session, or a handed-over one. The API exposes only reads, and the database keeps handed-over sessions read-only (Decision 4), so the API doesn't check the role. 192 - **Zod schemas.** The input and output schemas live in `packages/database`, so the API and the MCP share them: 193 - the API validates requests with them; 194 - the MCP generates its tool input definitions from them. 195 - **Response envelope.** Every response carries a request ID, plus either `data` or an error object with a stable code and a safe message. 196 - **Internal reference.** A `README` next to the routes documents this contract for whoever maintains the MCP or the API. It isn't developer onboarding. 197 - **Validation.** Reject the following with `invalid_request`: 198 - a blank query; 199 - a malformed `rid`; 200 - an explicitly empty type list; 201 - a limit outside 1-30. 202 - The default limit is 10. Unknown type `rid`s match nothing. 203 - **Error codes:** 204 - {{[[table]]}} 205 - Code 206 - HTTP status 207 - When 208 - `unauthenticated` 209 - 401 210 - Token is missing, invalid or expired 211 - `not_found` 212 - 404 213 - Node is missing or unreadable 214 - `content_unavailable` 215 - 409 216 - Node lacks its body or can't be converted 217 - `invalid_request` 218 - 422 219 - Input fails validation 220 - `result_too_large` 221 - 422 222 - Response exceeds the budget 223 - `dependency_error` 224 - 503 225 - Database or embedding failure 226 - The two 422 errors are told apart by the code in the envelope. Errors are never returned as empty results. 227 - **Response budget.** A response is either complete or fails with `result_too_large`. The proposed budget is 1 MiB serialized, to be validated in each client. 228 - **Logs** hold only the request ID, operation, duration, result count and error category. They never include the `Authorization` header (which carries the session token), the query text or node bodies. 229 - ### 9. The local MCP 230 - **Tools.** 231 - Each tool calls exactly one API operation. 232 - It returns the API's result as structured content, plus a short text form. 233 - It turns API errors into tool errors with the same code. An unreachable API is a `dependency_error`. 234 - Every tool is annotated read-only. 235 - **Runtime.** Logs go to stderr, because stdout carries the MCP protocol. 236 - **Session** 237 - **Connect.** `npx @discourse-graphs/mcp connect --name ` does the following: 238 - reads the bundle from stdin; 239 - refreshes once and checks that the role is `mcp_reader` (read-only database role); 240 - writes the session to `~/.discourse-graphs/mcp/.json` with mode 0600. 241 - The client config then holds only the launch command and `--name`, never a token. 242 - **Refresh.** The MCP refreshes against Supabase Auth. It writes each rotated refresh token to the state file atomically, before using the new session token. If the state file is lost, the user connects again with a new bundle. 243 - **One process per connection.** A lock file next to the state file stops a second process. Two processes refreshing the same token can make Supabase revoke the session. A user with two clients connects each one with its own bundle and `--name`. 244 - **Distribution and setup** 245 - **Package.** `@discourse-graphs/mcp` (name proposed), published to npm from `apps/mcp` with semver releases. Setup docs launch it with `npx -y @discourse-graphs/mcp@latest`. 246 - **Per-client setup** is documented for Claude Code (`claude mcp add`), Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`) and Codex (`~/.codex/config.toml`). The docs also cover: 247 - the risk that the state file can read everything the space can read, and that any process running as the user can read it; 248 - one bundle per client; 249 - search limits; 250 - sync-gap errors; 251 - that ChatGPT is unsupported. 252 - ## Risks / Trade-offs 253 - [The hook runs on every sign-in] → A failing hook blocks every token, including the plugins'. Keep it to one indexed lookup on `mcp_session`, return other claims unchanged, and test plugin sign-in and refresh with the hook on. 254 - [A switched-off hook fails open] → Handed-over sessions would get `authenticated`, which can write. The MCP's startup role check catches this. A harness that calls Supabase directly would still get a write-capable session. 255 - [A grant is missing from `mcp_reader`] → Retrieval fails or returns fewer rows. The API integration tests run every operation with a handed-over session, so as `mcp_reader`. 256 - [Revoking from `PUBLIC` breaks a function that relied on it] → Unlikely, because `base.sql` grants every function to `anon` and `authenticated` explicitly (Decision 4). Check the hosted database's grants before the revoke, and run the full cucumber suite as `anon` and `authenticated` after it. 257 - [The MCP depends on the website] → If the website is down, MCP retrieval fails with `dependency_error`, and every call takes one extra network hop. Accepted in exchange for one contract and server-side fixes. 258 - [`/api/v1` is pinned by installed copies] → Change it only additively. A breaking change ships as `/api/v2` alongside `v1`. 259 - [Session tokens that can write pass through the website] → The API accepts plugin sessions too. Routes only read, and the `Authorization` header stays out of logs. A leaked token stays valid until it expires, up to one hour. 260 - [The state file is readable by any process running as the user] → Accepted for v0, and stated in the setup docs. 261 - [One session reads one space] → A user with several spaces adds one MCP entry per space. 262 - [Search covers titles, not bodies] → Every node's title is embedded, and Roam nodes with a description match on that too. A query that matches only a node's body won't find it, on either platform. Document this in the MCP setup docs. Test correctness with deterministic vector fixtures, and tune relevance once real queries exist. Embedding more text needs a sync change and re-embedding, so it's out of v0. 263 - [Shared nodes look unfamiliar] → Label provenance as origin, and say that results reflect readable synced data, not local imports. 264 - ## Migration Plan 265 - 1. Land `mcp-session-access` (registry, handoff helper and connect command). 266 - 2. Add `mcp_reader`, the function allowlist and the access token hook, and turn on the space login lock. Enable the hook and the lock on the hosted project. 267 - 3. Add the retrieval functions and the search RPC through the declarative schema workflow. Existing RPCs and clients keep their behavior. 268 - 4. Deploy the API routes. 269 - 5. Build and publish the MCP. 270 - 6. Validate in Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex with Roam and Obsidian closed, then release to a limited cohort. 271 - 7. To roll back, deprecate the npm package, disable the routes and sign out the registered sessions. The additive role, functions and RPC can stay. 272

It never reads the database or calls the embeddings service. - **The contract is `/api/v1`** (the versioned route prefix). - Installed MCP copies can't be force-updated, so `/api/v1` changes only additively, and a breaking change needs `/api/v2`. - Schema, query and converter fixes behind the API ship by deploying the website, without an MCP release. - **Alternatives:** - **The MCP reads the database directly.** - Installed copies would then depend on view shapes, and every fix would need an MCP release. - The MCP would bundle database code and call an embedding route outside the API's auth. - The API and the MCP would be two adapters to keep in parity. - **A hosted MCP in `apps/website` (the 2026-09-25 version).** It reaches ChatGPT but needs a hosted credential store. The 2026-11-10 meeting chose a local MCP. A hosted MCP can still wrap this API later. - ### 2. Reuse the discovery read path - The API's routes call TypeScript functions in `packages/database`. These build on Sid's discovery code from [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091): - **Get-node** calls `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID), then fetches the `full` Content (the body) the way import does. - **Type discovery** reads node types from readable node instances and labels them with `dbNodeSchemasToCrossApp` (converts node types). - **Discourse context** finds the readable relation instances that touch the node. - Candidates come from `refs`, the list of referenced IDs. - Direction comes from the `source` and `destination` keys of `reference_content` (the relation's endpoint map). - Relations are converted with `dbRelationsToCrossApp` (converts relations). - Only search needs a new RPC (database function); see Decision 6. - **Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** four new RPCs, which would duplicate the converters. - ### 3. Hand over a session through `mcp-session-access` - `mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec]([[Spec: MCP token handoff]])) defines the handoff: - **Handoff.** - 1. The plugin opens a new session for the space account, using a second client that neither persists nor auto-refreshes. - 2. It registers the session with `register_mcp_session(label)`. - 3. It shows the bundle once: Supabase URL, anon key, space ID and refresh token. It keeps no copy. - **Registry.** `mcp_session` (list of handed-over sessions) records the session ID (taken from the caller's own token), the label, the space account and the creation time. - **Sign-out.** The holder can sign itself out with local scope (only its own session). Per-session sign-out from the plugin is proposed for right after v0. - **Emergency switch.** Until then, the cut-off is to sign out every other session of the space account. That also signs out the other plugin instances, which sign back in with the space login. - **Who can connect.** Any plugin user of the space. - **Tokens.** Two tokens are involved: - the **session token** is the session's short-lived access token, the one the API takes; - the **refresh token** renews the session token, and it rotates on every use. - The bundle carries only the refresh token. So the holder's first session token comes from a refresh, and it already carries `mcp_reader` (read-only database role; Decision 4). The plugin discards the `authenticated` session token it used to register. - **Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** Option B, a separate agent account for each grant, with a credential issued from a website page. The 2026-11-10 meeting judged its security gain marginal for the extra work. - ### 4. The database makes handed-over sessions read-only (A2) - Under Option A2 ([decision](((guIcK3Z9M)))), the agent signs in as the space account, but the database makes its session read-only. The session token also works against Supabase directly, outside the API, so the database is what enforces read-only. - **The hook.** A custom access token hook (a database function Supabase calls on every token issue and refresh) checks the token's `session_id`. When the session is in `mcp_session` (list of handed-over sessions), it sets the token's `role` claim to `mcp_reader` (read-only database role; name proposed). Other sessions keep `authenticated`. - **The role.** `mcp_reader`: - is granted to `authenticator` (the role Supabase's REST layer logs in as), so requests can switch to it; - has `SELECT` on the tables and views retrieval reads, and no `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE`; - has `EXECUTE` only on an allowlist: the search RPC, plus the access helpers that the policies and views call. - **Locking down functions.** `PUBLIC` (every database role) holds `EXECUTE` on every function, so the allowlist needs two changes: - `REVOKE EXECUTE ON ALL FUNCTIONS IN SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC`; - the matching default-privilege change, so new functions aren't executable by default either. - **This doesn't change what plugins or sync can do.** `base.sql` runs first and sets default privileges that grant every later function to `anon` and `authenticated` explicitly. So the plugins' roles don't rely on `PUBLIC`, and they keep every function they can call today. Postgres has no deny grant, and every role inherits `PUBLIC`, so removing that default is the only way to keep a function from `mcp_reader`. Before the revoke, a check on the hosted database confirms that `anon` and `authenticated` hold `EXECUTE` on every function. Its migrations predate the schema files, so it could differ. - A test lists every function `mcp_reader` can execute and compares the list with the allowlist. Policies without a `TO` clause cover `mcp_reader`, so its reads follow the space account's current access. - **Supabase Auth requests aren't covered by the role.** A handed-over session could ask Auth to replace the space login, which would lock out the plugins and let it open sessions that can write. This change turns on the **space login lock** (`secure_password_change` and "require current password"), which refuses that without the current space login. A session could also sign out the plugins' sessions; the plugins just sign back in, and signing out the handed-over session ends it. - **A switched-off hook fails open.** Handed-over sessions would then get `authenticated`. The MCP refuses to start unless its session token carries `mcp_reader`, which catches a misconfigured project at setup. - **Revocation waits for token expiry.** Sign-out stops refresh, but the current session token stays valid for up to `jwt_expiry` (session token lifetime, 3600 s). The 2026-11-10 meeting accepted this. - **Alternative: plain Option A** (the agent signs in as the space account, with read-only enforced only in the MCP's tools). Any process holding the bundle could then write. The 2026-11-10 meeting chose A2 because the threat is overeager agent harnesses that bypass the MCP. - ### 5. Nodes are CrossApp nodes, identified by `rid` - **Identifiers** - **Nodes.** A node's ID is its `rid` (global node ID), built by `spaceUriAndLocalIdToRid`. - For an `http` space URI, it's `/`. - Otherwise, it's `orn:.note:…/`. - Look nodes up by space and `localId`, never by `localId` alone. - **Types.** A type's ID is its `rid`, from `getNodeTypeRid`, never the space-relative `nodeType`. Type filters take type `rid`s, and same-named types in different spaces stay separate. - **Payload** - **Envelope.** Each operation returns `DbCrossAppNode`s (shared node format) in discovery's `{ nodes, spaces }` envelope. - **Extra fields.** `DbCrossAppNode` carries IDs, not names, so each node also gets: - `type`: `{ rid, name }`, with the name from `dbNodeSchemasToCrossApp` (converts node types); - `author`: `{ name }`, from `PlatformAccount.name` through `my_accounts` (accounts the caller can see), because `authorId` is the platform's internal account ID; - `sourceUrl` for Roam nodes, built as `/page/`, or `sourcePath` for Obsidian nodes, from the `filePath` in the title row's metadata, since an Obsidian note has no stable web URL. - Search also adds a `score` and an `excerpt`. There's no separate agent node type. - **Title and body.** The title is `content.direct`. Get-node adds `content.full` (the body) as stored text or markdown, never rendered HTML. - **Links and assets.** Source links stay as text. Assets aren't fetched, and no storage URLs are minted. - **Provenance.** It's the author's name, the space's name, platform and URL (from the `spaces` entry), the created and modified times, and the source link or path. Nothing implies the node exists in the caller's vault. - **Gaps are errors** - **Listings and search** skip rows the converter can't convert, as discovery does. - **Get-node doesn't skip:** - `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID) returns `null` for a missing or unreadable node, which maps to `not_found`. - A conversion failure or a missing body maps to `content_unavailable`. - A stored empty body is not a missing row. - **Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** an agent-specific payload keyed by `Concept.id` (internal database row ID), which no plugin uses. It would give each node a second identity. - ### 6. Semantic search through one new RPC - **Embedding the query.** The API embeds the query on the server with `text-embedding-3-small` at 1536 dimensions. It uses the OpenAI client that `/api/embeddings/openai/small` builds inline today, extracted into a shared helper. Embedding happens only after the API has authenticated the caller. The MCP doesn't call the embedding route. - **The search RPC** (`SECURITY INVOKER`, so it runs as the caller) takes the query vector, optional type `rid`s and a limit. It: - joins the current, non-obsolete `direct` (title) and `direct_and_description` (title plus description) embeddings of readable node instances; - keeps each node's best similarity, once; - applies authorization, the type filter and deduplication before the limit; - sorts by similarity, then by `rid`; - has no similarity threshold, so negative similarities stay eligible. - `score` is the cosine similarity. `match_content_embeddings` (the existing semantic search query) stays unchanged. - **Other behavior** - Nodes without a usable embedding are absent from search, but the other operations still reach them. - Embedding failures are errors, not empty results. - **The excerpt** is the first 300 Unicode code points of the body (`content.full`). When the body is missing, it falls back to `content.direct` (the title). The excerpt isn't evidence that the body matched. - **Proposed for after v0: hybrid search.** Adapt [Supabase's hybrid search recipe](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai/hybrid-search). The recipe is a SQL function to copy, not a built-in. It: - ranks rows by keyword (`websearch_to_tsquery`) and by vector similarity; - merges the two rankings with Reciprocal Rank Fusion. - Here it would need two schema additions on `Content` (the text table): a generated full-text column and a GIN index. The search RPC would gain a keyword list and a fusion step. The `/api/v1` search route keeps its inputs, so this is an additive change. Exact words such as names, acronyms and titles would then rank well even when the embedding misses them. - ### 7. One-hop discourse context - Return each readable relation instance that touches the node, with: - its `rid` (global node ID); - its type; - its direction; - a summary of the connected node. - Rules: - The relation, its type and both endpoints must be readable. Relations are read through `my_concepts` (filtered to what the caller can read) with the caller's session, so an unreadable relation never comes back. Drop a relation whose type or endpoint the caller can't read before converting it, because `dbRelationsToCrossApp` throws on a missing endpoint instead of skipping it. - Keep relations distinct even when they share a label. - A self-link appears as both incoming and outgoing. - Don't follow ordinary backlinks, and don't go past one hop. - ### 8. API contract - {{[[table]]}} - API route - MCP tool - Input - `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}` - `get_node` - node `rid` - `POST /api/v1/nodes/search` - `search_nodes` - query, optional type `rid`s, optional limit - `GET /api/v1/node-types` - `get_node_types` - none - `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}/context` - `get_discourse_context` - node `rid` - `rid`s (global node IDs) contain `/` and `:`, so they go URL-encoded in the path. - **Each route does three things:** - 1. It validates the session token with Supabase Auth, then builds a request-scoped client that acts as the caller. Nothing is held between requests. - 2. It validates the input with the shared Zod schemas (typed input and output definitions). - 3. It calls one `packages/database` function. - **Any session token is accepted.** The API accepts any valid space-account session token: a plugin's own session, or a handed-over one. The API exposes only reads, and the database keeps handed-over sessions read-only (Decision 4), so the API doesn't check the role. - **Zod schemas.** The input and output schemas live in `packages/database`, so the API and the MCP share them: - the API validates requests with them; - the MCP generates its tool input definitions from them. - **Response envelope.** Every response carries a request ID, plus either `data` or an error object with a stable code and a safe message. - **Internal reference.** A `README` next to the routes documents this contract for whoever maintains the MCP or the API. It isn't developer onboarding. - **Validation.** Reject the following with `invalid_request`: - a blank query; - a malformed `rid`; - an explicitly empty type list; - a limit outside 1-30. - The default limit is 10. Unknown type `rid`s match nothing. - **Error codes:** - {{[[table]]}} - Code - HTTP status - When - `unauthenticated` - 401 - Token is missing, invalid or expired - `not_found` - 404 - Node is missing or unreadable - `content_unavailable` - 409 - Node lacks its body or can't be converted - `invalid_request` - 422 - Input fails validation - `result_too_large` - 422 - Response exceeds the budget - `dependency_error` - 503 - Database or embedding failure - The two 422 errors are told apart by the code in the envelope. Errors are never returned as empty results. - **Response budget.** A response is either complete or fails with `result_too_large`. The proposed budget is 1 MiB serialized, to be validated in each client. - **Logs** hold only the request ID, operation, duration, result count and error category. They never include the `Authorization` header (which carries the session token), the query text or node bodies. - ### 9. The local MCP - **Tools.** - Each tool calls exactly one API operation. - It returns the API's result as structured content, plus a short text form. - It turns API errors into tool errors with the same code. An unreachable API is a `dependency_error`. - Every tool is annotated read-only. - **Runtime.** Logs go to stderr, because stdout carries the MCP protocol. - **Session** - **Connect.** `npx @discourse-graphs/mcp connect --name ` does the following: - reads the bundle from stdin; - refreshes once and checks that the role is `mcp_reader` (read-only database role); - writes the session to `~/.discourse-graphs/mcp/.json` with mode 0600. - The client config then holds only the launch command and `--name`, never a token. - **Refresh.** The MCP refreshes against Supabase Auth. It writes each rotated refresh token to the state file atomically, before using the new session token. If the state file is lost, the user connects again with a new bundle. - **One process per connection.** A lock file next to the state file stops a second process. Two processes refreshing the same token can make Supabase revoke the session. A user with two clients connects each one with its own bundle and `--name`. - **Distribution and setup** - **Package.** `@discourse-graphs/mcp` (name proposed), published to npm from `apps/mcp` with semver releases. Setup docs launch it with `npx -y @discourse-graphs/mcp@latest`. - **Per-client setup** is documented for Claude Code (`claude mcp add`), Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`) and Codex (`~/.codex/config.toml`). The docs also cover: - the risk that the state file can read everything the space can read, and that any process running as the user can read it; - one bundle per client; - search limits; - sync-gap errors; - that ChatGPT is unsupported. - ## Risks / Trade-offs - [The hook runs on every sign-in] → A failing hook blocks every token, including the plugins'. Keep it to one indexed lookup on `mcp_session`, return other claims unchanged, and test plugin sign-in and refresh with the hook on. - [A switched-off hook fails open] → Handed-over sessions would get `authenticated`, which can write. The MCP's startup role check catches this. A harness that calls Supabase directly would still get a write-capable session. - [A grant is missing from `mcp_reader`] → Retrieval fails or returns fewer rows. The API integration tests run every operation with a handed-over session, so as `mcp_reader`. - [Revoking from `PUBLIC` breaks a function that relied on it] → Unlikely, because `base.sql` grants every function to `anon` and `authenticated` explicitly (Decision 4). Check the hosted database's grants before the revoke, and run the full cucumber suite as `anon` and `authenticated` after it. - [The MCP depends on the website] → If the website is down, MCP retrieval fails with `dependency_error`, and every call takes one extra network hop. Accepted in exchange for one contract and server-side fixes. - [`/api/v1` is pinned by installed copies] → Change it only additively. A breaking change ships as `/api/v2` alongside `v1`. - [Session tokens that can write pass through the website] → The API accepts plugin sessions too. Routes only read, and the `Authorization` header stays out of logs. A leaked token stays valid until it expires, up to one hour. - [The state file is readable by any process running as the user] → Accepted for v0, and stated in the setup docs. - [One session reads one space] → A user with several spaces adds one MCP entry per space. - [Search covers titles, not bodies] → Every node's title is embedded, and Roam nodes with a description match on that too. A query that matches only a node's body won't find it, on either platform. Document this in the MCP setup docs. Test correctness with deterministic vector fixtures, and tune relevance once real queries exist. Embedding more text needs a sync change and re-embedding, so it's out of v0. - [Shared nodes look unfamiliar] → Label provenance as origin, and say that results reflect readable synced data, not local imports. - ## Migration Plan - 1. Land `mcp-session-access` (registry, handoff helper and connect command). - 2. Add `mcp_reader`, the function allowlist and the access token hook, and turn on the space login lock. Enable the hook and the lock on the hosted project. - 3. Add the retrieval functions and the search RPC through the declarative schema workflow. Existing RPCs and clients keep their behavior. - 4. Deploy the API routes. - 5. Build and publish the MCP. - 6. Validate in Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex with Roam and Obsidian closed, then release to a limited cohort. - 7. To roll back, deprecate the npm package, disable the routes and sign out the registered sessions. The additive role, functions and RPC can stay.

input.new_string: Users want to retrieve relevant synced discourse nodes from their agent without opening Roam or Obsidian,

input.markdown:
- # Proposal
  - ## Why
    - Users want to retrieve relevant synced discourse nodes from their agent without opening Roam or Obsidian, and without a separate integration for each platform. This v0 ships a retrieval API and a local MCP that exposes that API to agent clients. The MCP uses a read-only session of the space account, handed over by the plugin.
  - ## What Changes
    - **A retrieval API** at `/api/v1` (versioned HTTP routes) in `apps/website`, with four read-only operations: get a node, search nodes, list node types, and get discourse context. It is the one retrieval service and the only backend of the MCP.
    - **A local MCP** that exposes each API operation as a tool. Users install it from npm, and the agent client launches it. Supported clients: Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex.
    - **Identity follows Option A2** ([decision](((guIcK3Z9M))), [options compared](((bTMUCrCnD)))): the agent signs in as the space account, but the database makes its session read-only. It was decided at the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product meeting. The session is handed over through `mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec]([[Spec: MCP token handoff]])).
    - **Coverage.** Retrieval covers every synced discourse node the space account can read under its current access, including shared nodes that were never imported into the client.
    - **Node shape.** Nodes come back as `DbCrossAppNode`s (the shared node format from [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091)), identified by `rid` (global node ID). They reuse discovery's converters and its `{ nodes, spaces }` envelope. Node types are identified by type `rid`.
    - **Search is semantic.** It reuses the stored embeddings through one new search RPC (database function), with type filtering and no relevance cutoff.
  - ## Capabilities
    - ### New Capabilities
      - `discourse-retrieval`: **what the API's four operations return.** Covers which nodes are eligible, node payloads, semantic search, type discovery and one-hop discourse context.
      - `headless-retrieval-api`: **how callers reach those operations.** Covers the HTTP routes, session auth, the response envelope and the versioned contract.
      - `discourse-mcp`: **how agent clients reach the API.** Covers four tools that pass API results through, plus setup and distribution.
      - `agent-read-access`: **the session an agent holds.** It is handed over by the plugin, reads with the space account's current access, and the database keeps it read-only.
    - ### Modified Capabilities
      - None. The repository has no OpenSpec capability specs yet.
  - ## Out of scope for v0
    - A hosted MCP and ChatGPT support. ChatGPT can't launch a local MCP; a hosted MCP can later wrap the same API.
    - Option B, a separate agent account.
    - Writes, candidate nodes, non-discourse content, canvas functions, and attachment contents.
    - Multi-hop traversal, re-embedding, pagination, relevance thresholds, and imported-only filtering.
    - Keyword or hybrid search. It's proposed for after v0, adapting [Supabase's hybrid search recipe](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai/hybrid-search) (design Decision 6).
    - One session that spans several spaces.
  - ## Impact
    - **`packages/database`:**
      - `mcp_reader` (read-only database role);
      - a custom access token hook (assigns that role at sign-in);
      - an `EXECUTE` allowlist (which database functions the role may call);
      - the space login lock (stops a session from replacing the space login);
      - retrieval functions built on the discovery converters;
      - one semantic search RPC (database function).
    - **`apps/website`:** the four API routes and their documentation.
    - **A new MCP package** (`apps/mcp`, location proposed), published to npm.
    - **Hosted Supabase settings:** the access token hook and the space login lock (design Decision 4).
    - **Depends on `mcp-session-access`** (the [session handoff spec]([[Spec: MCP token handoff]])) for the handoff, the `mcp_session` registry (list of handed-over sessions) and sign-out.
    - **Builds on** [ENG-1985](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1985) (database-to-node converter) and [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091) (discovery returns shared nodes), both merged. They provide `dbNodeToCrossApp` (converts one node), `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID) and `SharedNodeListing` (nodes plus their spaces).
  - ## Open decisions
    - Whether one agent should span several spaces.
    - Michael hasn't confirmed reusing `CrossAppNode` (the shared node format) and `rid` (global node ID) for the agent API ([Roam block](((SRa9xHk30)))).
    - No relevance or latency target is agreed, and the real-query evaluation set doesn't exist yet.

A query that matches only a node's body won't find it, on either platform. Document this in the MCP setup docs. Test correctness with deterministic vector fixtures, and tune relevance once real queries exist. Embedding more text needs a sync change and re-embedding, so it's out of v0. 263 - [Shared nodes look unfamiliar] → Label provenance as origin, and say that results reflect readable synced data, not local imports. 264 - ## Migration Plan 265 - 1. Land `mcp-session-access` (registry, handoff helper and connect command). 266 - 2. Add `mcp_reader`, the function allowlist and the access token hook, and turn on the space login lock. Enable the hook and the lock on the hosted project. 267 - 3. Add the retrieval functions and the search RPC through the declarative schema workflow. Existing RPCs and clients keep their behavior. 268 - 4. Deploy the API routes. 269 - 5. Build and publish the MCP. 270 - 6. Validate in Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex with Roam and Obsidian closed, then release to a limited cohort. 271 - 7. To roll back, deprecate the npm package, disable the routes and sign out the registered sessions. The additive role, functions and RPC can stay. 272

None of this is in the repo yet. - **Concepts and content.** - `Concept` (the node, type and relation table) holds node instances, schemas and relations, flagged by `is_schema` and `is_relation`. - `Content` (the text table) joins it on `(space_id, source_local_id)`. API contract - {{[[table]]}} - API route - MCP tool - Input - `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}` - `get_node` - node `rid` - `POST /api/v1/nodes/search` - `search_nodes` - query, optional type `rid`s, optional limit - `GET /api/v1/node-types` - `get_node_types` - none - `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}/context` - `get_discourse_context` - node `rid` - `rid`s (global node IDs) contain `/` and `:`, so they go URL-encoded in the path. - **Each route does three things:** - 1. It validates the session token with Supabase Auth, then builds a request-scoped client that acts as the caller. Nothing is held between requests. - 2. It validates the input with the shared Zod schemas (typed input and output definitions). - 3. It calls one `packages/database` function. - **Any session token is accepted.** The API accepts any valid space-account session token: a plugin's own session, or a handed-over one. The API exposes only reads, and the database keeps handed-over sessions read-only (Decision 4), so the API doesn't check the role. - **Zod schemas.** The input and output schemas live in `packages/database`, so the API and the MCP share them: - the API validates requests with them; - the MCP generates its tool input definitions from them. - **Response envelope.** Every response carries a request ID, plus either `data` or an error object with a stable code and a safe message. - **Internal reference.** A `README` next to the routes documents this contract for whoever maintains the MCP or the API. It isn't developer onboarding. - **Validation.** Reject the following with `invalid_request`: - a blank query; - a malformed `rid`; - an explicitly empty type list; - a limit outside 1-30. - The default limit is 10. Unknown type `rid`s match nothing. - **Error codes:** - {{[[table]]}} - Code - HTTP status - When - `unauthenticated` - 401 - Token is missing, invalid or expired - `not_found` - 404 - Node is missing or unreadable - `content_unavailable` - 409 - Node lacks its body or can't be converted - `invalid_request` - 422 - Input fails validation - `result_too_large` - 422 - Response exceeds the budget - `dependency_error` - 503 - Database or embedding failure - The two 422 errors are told apart by the code in the envelope. Errors are never returned as empty results. - **Response budget.** A response is either complete or fails with `result_too_large`. The proposed budget is 1 MiB serialized, to be validated in each client. - **Logs** hold only the request ID, operation, duration, result count and error category. They never include the `Authorization` header (which carries the session token), the query text or node bodies. - ### 9. The local MCP - **Tools.** - Each tool calls exactly one API operation. - It returns the API's result as structured content, plus a short text form. - It turns API errors into tool errors with the same code. An unreachable API is a `dependency_error`. - Every tool is annotated read-only. - **Runtime.** Logs go to stderr, because stdout carries the MCP protocol. - **Session** - **Connect.** `npx @discourse-graphs/mcp connect --name ` does the following: - reads the bundle from stdin; - refreshes once and checks that the role is `mcp_reader` (read-only database role); - writes the session to `~/.discourse-graphs/mcp/.json` with mode 0600. - The client config then holds only the launch command and `--name`, never a token. - **Refresh.** The MCP refreshes against Supabase Auth. It writes each rotated refresh token to the state file atomically, before using the new session token. If the state file is lost, the user connects again with a new bundle. - **One process per connection.** A lock file next to the state file stops a second process. Two processes refreshing the same token can make Supabase revoke the session. A user with two clients connects each one with its own bundle and `--name`. - **Distribution and setup** - **Package.** `@discourse-graphs/mcp` (name proposed), published to npm from `apps/mcp` with semver releases. Setup docs launch it with `npx -y @discourse-graphs/mcp@latest`. - **Per-client setup** is documented for Claude Code (`claude mcp add`), Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`) and Codex (`~/.codex/config.toml`). The docs also cover: - the risk that the state file can read everything the space can read, and that any process running as the user can read it; - one bundle per client; - search limits; - sync-gap errors; - that ChatGPT is unsupported. - ## Risks / Trade-offs - [The hook runs on every sign-in] → A failing hook blocks every token, including the plugins'. Keep it to one indexed lookup on `mcp_session`, return other claims unchanged, and test plugin sign-in and refresh with the hook on. - [A switched-off hook fails open] → Handed-over sessions would get `authenticated`, which can write. The MCP's startup role check catches this. A harness that calls Supabase directly would still get a write-capable session. - [A grant is missing from `mcp_reader`] → Retrieval fails or returns fewer rows. The API integration tests run every operation with a handed-over session, so as `mcp_reader`. - [Revoking from `PUBLIC` breaks a function that relied on it] → Unlikely, because `base.sql` grants every function to `anon` and `authenticated` explicitly (Decision 4). Check the hosted database's grants before the revoke, and run the full cucumber suite as `anon` and `authenticated` after it. - [The MCP depends on the website] → If the website is down, MCP retrieval fails with `dependency_error`, and every call takes one extra network hop. Accepted in exchange for one contract and server-side fixes. - [`/api/v1` is pinned by installed copies] → Change it only additively. A breaking change ships as `/api/v2` alongside `v1`. - [Session tokens that can write pass through the website] → The API accepts plugin sessions too. Routes only read, and the `Authorization` header stays out of logs. A leaked token stays valid until it expires, up to one hour. - [The state file is readable by any process running as the user] → Accepted for v0, and stated in the setup docs. - [One session reads one space] → A user with several spaces adds one MCP entry per space. - [Search covers titles, not bodies] → Every node's title is embedded, and Roam nodes with a description match on that too. A query that matches only a node's body won't find it, on either platform. Document this in the MCP setup docs. Test correctness with deterministic vector fixtures, and tune relevance once real queries exist. Embedding more text needs a sync change and re-embedding, so it's out of v0. - [Shared nodes look unfamiliar] → Label provenance as origin, and say that results reflect readable synced data, not local imports. - ## Migration Plan - 1. Land `mcp-session-access` (registry, handoff helper and connect command). - 2. Add `mcp_reader`, the function allowlist and the access token hook, and turn on the space login lock. Enable the hook and the lock on the hosted project. - 3. Add the retrieval functions and the search RPC through the declarative schema workflow. Existing RPCs and clients keep their behavior. - 4. Deploy the API routes. - 5. Build and publish the MCP. - 6. Validate in Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex with Roam and Obsidian closed, then release to a limited cohort. - 7. To roll back, deprecate the npm package, disable the routes and sign out the registered sessions. The additive role, functions and RPC can stay.

1	- specs
2	  - # `headless-retrieval-api`
3	    - ## Purpose
4	      - How callers reach the retrieval operations: HTTP routes, session auth, the response envelope and the versioned contract. The MCP calls the API on behalf of agent clients. What the operations return is specified in `discourse-retrieval` (retrieval behavior).
5	    - ## ADDED Requirements
6	      - ### Requirement: Four retrieval operations
7	        - The system SHALL provide an HTTP API for four operations: get-node, search-nodes, discover-node-types and get-discourse-context. These operations SHALL follow the `discourse-retrieval` (retrieval behavior) contract. The API SHALL be the only retrieval backend for the MCP.
8	        - **Scenario: MCP calls each operation**
9	          - **WHEN** the MCP calls each of the four operations with a valid session token
10	          - **THEN** each operation applies the shared retrieval and authorization rules
11	          - **AND** no other retrieval path is required
12	      - ### Requirement: Response envelope
13	        - Every API response SHALL carry a request ID, plus either `data` or an error object with a stable code and a safe message. An error SHALL NOT be returned as an empty `data` collection.
14	        - **Scenario: Failed request**
15	          - **WHEN** an operation fails
16	          - **THEN** the response has a request ID and an error object, with a stable code and a message that doesn't expose internals
17	          - **AND** the response has no `data`
18	      - ### Requirement: Authenticated sessions
19	        - The API SHALL accept a valid session token for a space account. It SHALL reject missing, invalid and expired tokens, and SHALL NOT store tokens between requests. The API SHALL expose only read operations. Read-only access for agent sessions is enforced by the database, as specified in `agent-read-access` (the agent's session).
20	        - **Scenario: Missing or expired token**
21	          - **WHEN** a request carries no token, or an expired one
22	          - **THEN** the API rejects it as unauthenticated, and returns no discourse data
23	      - ### Requirement: Versioned contract
24	        - The API SHALL serve its operations under a version prefix such as `/api/v1`. Changes within a version SHALL be additive. A breaking change SHALL ship under a new version, alongside the old one.
25	        - **Scenario: An installed MCP after a server change**
26	          - **GIVEN** an installed MCP built against `/api/v1`
27	          - **WHEN** the website deploys a change within `/api/v1`
28	          - **THEN** the installed MCP's requests keep working
29	      - ### Requirement: Headless retrieval after setup
30	        - After handoff and sync, the API SHALL work without Roam or Obsidian open. Responses SHALL come from the database's synced state.
31	        - **Scenario: Source application is closed**
32	          - **GIVEN** a user has synced nodes and a session token
33	          - **WHEN** Roam and Obsidian are closed, and a caller calls the API
34	          - **THEN** eligible synced data is returned
35	  - # `discourse-retrieval`
36	    - ## Purpose
37	      - What the API's four retrieval operations return, whichever client calls them: which nodes are eligible, node payloads, semantic search, type discovery, and one-hop discourse context. All of it stays within the caller's current read access. The API exposes these operations over HTTP (`headless-retrieval-api`), and the MCP passes their results through (`discourse-mcp`).
38	    - ## ADDED Requirements
39	      - ### Requirement: Readable synced collection
40	        - All retrieval operations SHALL use already-synced discourse data readable by the caller's space account. Local import status and authorship SHALL NOT restrict that collection. Results MUST NOT imply that the returned nodes were imported into the client application.
41	        - **Scenario: Readable but unimported node**
42	          - **GIVEN** a synced discourse node is readable by the caller, but was authored elsewhere and never imported into its client
43	          - **WHEN** the caller fetches it or searches for it
44	          - **THEN** the node is eligible for retrieval and search ranking
45	          - **AND** the response does not claim the node was imported locally
46	        - **Scenario: Unreadable node**
47	          - **WHEN** a caller requests a node it cannot read
48	          - **THEN** retrieval returns neither the node's content nor its metadata
49	      - ### Requirement: Nodes and types are identified by rid
50	        - Every operation SHALL identify a node by its `rid` (global node ID), and a node type by the type's `rid`. Type filters SHALL take type `rid`s. Types with the same name in different spaces SHALL stay separate.
51	        - **Scenario: Same-named types in two spaces**
52	          - **GIVEN** two readable spaces each define a type named "Claim"
53	          - **WHEN** the caller discovers node types
54	          - **THEN** it sees two types with different `rid`s
55	      - ### Requirement: Full node text
56	        - Getting a readable node SHALL return its `rid` (global node ID), title, type and provenance (see "Readable type and provenance"), and its full synced text body. The body SHALL be the stored synced text, not content fetched live from the client application. Attachment downloads and file contents SHALL stay outside this operation.
57	        - **Scenario: Get a node with body text and attachment links**
58	          - **WHEN** a caller fetches a readable synced node whose text links to an attachment
59	          - **THEN** it receives the required node fields and the full stored text, including the source links in that text
60	          - **AND** the response doesn't download or embed the attachment's file contents
61	      - ### Requirement: Readable type and provenance
62	        - Every node an operation returns SHALL carry its type and its provenance in readable form:
63	          - its type, as the type's `rid` and name (for example "Claim");
64	          - the author's name;
65	          - the space's name, platform and URL;
66	          - its created and modified times;
67	          - a link to open it at the source when the platform has one (a Roam page URL), or else its file path (an Obsidian vault path).
68	        - **Scenario: Readable type and author**
69	          - **GIVEN** a readable Claim node written by Trang in the "Lab" space
70	          - **WHEN** a caller fetches it
71	          - **THEN** the response names the type "Claim", the author "Trang" and the space "Lab", alongside the type's `rid`
72	      - ### Requirement: Semantic search over existing embeddings
73	        - Search SHALL rank nodes by semantic similarity using the stored embeddings, without re-embedding. Sync embeds every node's title, on both platforms. Roam also embeds the description with the title when a node has one. Bodies aren't embedded on either platform, so matching covers titles (and Roam descriptions), not full bodies. V0 SHALL NOT require keyword matching or hybrid ranking.
74	        - **Scenario: Matching by meaning**
75	          - **WHEN** a caller submits a query, and eligible nodes have current embeddings
76	          - **THEN** a node can rank even when its title lacks the query's exact words
77	        - **Scenario: Titles on both platforms**
78	          - **GIVEN** a node whose titles both match the query's meaning
79	          - **WHEN** the caller searches
80	          - **THEN** both nodes can rank
81	        - **Scenario: Existing title-plus-description embedding**
82	          - **GIVEN** a readable Roam node has an embedding generated from its title and description
83	          - **WHEN** the caller searches
84	          - **THEN** that embedding contributes to ranking
85	        - **Scenario: Body-only changes**
86	          - **GIVEN** the title, description, permissions and filters are unchanged
87	          - **WHEN** only a node's full synced body changes
88	          - **THEN** the node's search ranking doesn't change
89	      - ### Requirement: Search result fields
90	        - Each search result SHALL contain the node's `rid` (global node ID), title, type and provenance, plus a short excerpt and a relevance score, but not the full body. Results SHALL be ordered by relevance.
91	        - **Scenario: Result fields**
92	          - **WHEN** a search returns results
93	          - **THEN** each result has those fields, and the results are ordered by score
94	      - ### Requirement: Bounded search without a relevance cutoff
95	        - Search SHALL default to 10 results and accept a limit from 1 to 30. A limit outside that range SHALL be rejected. V0 SHALL NOT paginate. Search SHALL NOT discard eligible nodes because their relevance is low. An empty result SHALL mean that no searchable nodes meet the access and type constraints.
96	        - **Scenario: Default and explicit limits**
97	          - **GIVEN** at least 30 eligible searchable nodes
98	          - **WHEN** the caller searches without a limit, and then with a limit of 20
99	          - **THEN** the responses contain 10 results and 20 results
100	          - **AND** neither response offers a continuation page
101	        - **Scenario: Weak matches**
102	          - **GIVEN** three eligible searchable nodes that match the query weakly, and a limit of 10
103	          - **WHEN** the caller searches
104	          - **THEN** all three are returned in relevance order
105	        - **Scenario: Limit above the maximum**
106	          - **WHEN** a request asks for more than 30 results
107	          - **THEN** it is rejected as an invalid request
108	        - **Scenario: Empty eligible collection**
109	          - **WHEN** no searchable nodes meet the caller's access and type constraints
110	          - **THEN** search returns an empty result
111	      - ### Requirement: Readable type discovery and filtering
112	        - Type discovery SHALL return type `rid`s (global type IDs) and names, only for types present on nodes the caller can currently read. That includes types on shared nodes. Search SHALL accept one or more type `rid`s and match any of them. Without a filter, search SHALL cover all eligible types.
113	        - **Scenario: Discover types from readable nodes**
114	          - **GIVEN** type A is on a readable shared node, and type B is only on unreadable nodes
115	          - **WHEN** the caller discovers node types
116	          - **THEN** type A is listed and type B is not
117	        - **Scenario: Multiple selected types**
118	          - **WHEN** the caller searches with types A and B selected
119	          - **THEN** every result has type A or B, and is readable by the caller
120	        - **Scenario: No type filter**
121	          - **WHEN** the caller searches without a type filter
122	          - **THEN** no eligible node is excluded because of its type
123	      - ### Requirement: One-hop discourse context
124	        - Discourse context SHALL return the incoming and outgoing explicit discourse relationships of a readable node. Each relationship SHALL give:
125	          - its type;
126	          - its direction relative to the requested node;
127	          - the connected node's `rid` (global node ID), title, type (`rid` and name), author name and space name.
128	        - Both endpoints MUST be readable. Ordinary backlinks SHALL be excluded. Connected bodies SHALL be retrieved separately, through get-node. A single call SHALL NOT go past one hop.
129	        - **Scenario: Incoming and outgoing relationships**
130	          - **GIVEN** readable nodes A and B have an explicit relationship from A to B
131	          - **WHEN** the caller requests discourse context for A, and then for B
132	          - **THEN** the relationship is outgoing for A and incoming for B, each with the connected node's summary
133	        - **Scenario: Inaccessible endpoint and ordinary backlink**
134	          - **GIVEN** readable node A has an explicit relationship to unreadable node B, and an ordinary backlink from readable node C
135	          - **WHEN** the caller requests A's discourse context
136	          - **THEN** neither the relationship to B nor the backlink from C is returned
137	        - **Scenario: Repeated one-hop calls**
138	          - **GIVEN** readable nodes A, B and C have relationships from A to B and from B to C, and none from A to C
139	          - **WHEN** the caller requests A's discourse context
140	          - **THEN** the call doesn't traverse B to return C
141	          - **AND** a later request for B's discourse context returns the relationship to C
142	  - # `agent-read-access`
143	    - ## Purpose
144	      - The session an agent holds. A plugin hands it over, it reads the space's synced discourse graph with the space account's current access, and the database keeps it read-only. This follows Option A2 ([decision](((guIcK3Z9M)))): the agent signs in as the space account, but its session can't write.
145	    - ## ADDED Requirements
146	      - ### Requirement: Session handed over through `mcp-session-access`
147	        - The MCP SHALL use a session that a plugin handed over and registered through `mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec]([[Spec: MCP token handoff]])). No website session or agent-management page SHALL be required. The MCP SHALL NOT receive the space login, which is the credential plugins use to sign in.
148	        - **Scenario: Connect from either platform**
149	          - **WHEN** a user runs the connect command in a signed-in Roam or Obsidian client
150	          - **THEN** the plugin shows a bundle for a new, registered session of that client's space account
151	          - **AND** the plugin's own session is unchanged
152	      - ### Requirement: Per-space principal
153	        - The system SHALL treat the space account whose session was handed over as the principal, meaning the identity whose access is used. Retrieval SHALL use that account's readable collection. It SHALL NOT combine the access of other space accounts that the same person uses. Reading another space's synced but unpublished nodes SHALL require a bundle from that space.
154	        - **Scenario: Another space's private synced nodes**
155	          - **GIVEN** a person uses spaces A and B, and a node in B is not readable by A's space account
156	          - **WHEN** an agent uses a bundle from space A
157	          - **THEN** it cannot retrieve the node in B
158	        - **Scenario: Accessible shared node**
159	          - **GIVEN** a node from another space is readable by the space account through sharing
160	          - **WHEN** the agent retrieves that node
161	          - **THEN** the node is returned, even though the space account didn't import or author it
162	      - ### Requirement: Current permissions
163	        - The system SHALL evaluate retrieval against the space account's current read permissions.
164	        - Removing access SHALL stop later retrieval of the affected data.
165	        - Adding access SHALL make the affected synced data eligible.
166	        - Neither change SHALL require a new bundle.
167	        - **Scenario: Permissions change after handoff**
168	          - **WHEN** a space account gains access to node A and loses access to node B after a bundle is handed over
169	          - **THEN** later requests with that bundle can retrieve A and cannot retrieve B
170	      - ### Requirement: Session sign-out
171	        - The MCP SHALL be able to sign its own session out. A signed-out session SHALL NOT refresh. A session token the MCP already holds MAY stay valid until it expires, which is up to one hour.
172	        - **Scenario: Signed-out session**
173	          - **WHEN** a handed-over session is signed out
174	          - **THEN** the MCP cannot refresh it
175	          - **AND** requests fail once its current session token expires
176	      - ### Requirement: The database refuses writes from handed-over sessions
177	        - The database SHALL refuse every create, modify or delete made with a handed-over session, whichever client makes it. That includes calls to write functions. The session SHALL keep the space account's read access, and plugin sessions SHALL keep their permissions. Missing or expired sessions SHALL NOT authorize retrieval.
178	        - **Scenario: Write made outside the MCP's tools**
179	          - **GIVEN** a process holds a handed-over session, and the space account can edit a node
180	          - **WHEN** the process modifies the node, or calls a write function, directly with that session
181	          - **THEN** the database refuses it
182	          - **AND** the node remains unchanged
183	        - **Scenario: Plugin session keeps write access**
184	          - **GIVEN** a plugin has handed over a session
185	          - **WHEN** the plugin writes with its own session
186	          - **THEN** the write succeeds
187	        - **Scenario: Unauthenticated retrieval**
188	          - **WHEN** a retrieval request has a missing or expired session
189	          - **THEN** no discourse data is returned
190	      - ### Requirement: Handed-over sessions cannot replace the space login
191	        - A handed-over session SHALL NOT be able to replace the space login, which is the credential plugins use to sign in, using only its session token.
192	        - **Scenario: Agent tries to replace the space login**
193	          - **WHEN** a process asks Supabase Auth to set a new space login, using a handed-over session token
194	          - **THEN** Supabase Auth refuses the request
195	          - **AND** the space's plugins still sign in with the existing space login
196	  - # `discourse-mcp`
197	    - ## Purpose
198	      - This spec covers how agent clients reach the retrieval API: through one local MCP that works with both Roam and Obsidian. The MCP runs on the user's machine, using a session the plugin hands over. Its four tools pass the API's results through unchanged.
199	    - ## ADDED Requirements
200	      - ### Requirement: Tools are thin clients of the API
201	        - The MCP SHALL expose tools for get-node, search-nodes, discover-node-types and get-discourse-context, and no other tools.
202	        - Each tool SHALL call exactly one operation of the retrieval API (`headless-retrieval-api`) and SHALL return that operation's result. If the operation fails, the tool SHALL return a tool error with the same code.
203	        - The MCP SHALL NOT read the database or call an embedding service itself.
204	        - **Scenario: Tool discovery**
205	          - **WHEN** an agent client lists the MCP's tools
206	          - **THEN** it sees exactly the four retrieval tools, each with its input definition and a read-only annotation
207	        - **Scenario: API error**
208	          - **WHEN** the API returns an error for a tool call
209	          - **THEN** the tool returns an error with the same code, not an empty result
210	        - **Scenario: API unreachable**
211	          - **WHEN** the API can't be reached
212	          - **THEN** the tool returns a dependency error
213	        - **Scenario: Agent asks the MCP to modify a node**
214	          - **WHEN** an agent asks the MCP to modify a node
215	          - **THEN** no MCP tool can perform the modification
216	      - ### Requirement: Distribution and setup
217	        - The MCP SHALL install from npm. It SHALL take the bundle through a connect step, which stores the session outside the agent client's configuration.
218	        - It SHALL also:
219	          - persist every rotated refresh token;
220	          - refuse to run a second process for the same connection;
221	          - refuse to start when its session lacks `mcp_reader`, the read-only database role.
222	        - **Scenario: Connect stores the session locally**
223	          - **WHEN** a user runs the connect step with a bundle
224	          - **THEN** the session is stored in a local state file that only the user can read
225	          - **AND** the agent client's configuration holds no token
226	        - **Scenario: Restart after a refresh**
227	          - **GIVEN** the MCP has refreshed its session at least once
228	          - **WHEN** the agent client restarts the MCP
229	          - **THEN** the MCP resumes with the latest refresh token
230	        - **Scenario: Second process for one connection**
231	          - **WHEN** a second MCP process starts for a connection that is already running
232	          - **THEN** it exits with a clear error and doesn't refresh the session
233	        - **Scenario: Read-only role missing**
234	          - **WHEN** the MCP's session token doesn't carry `mcp_reader`, the read-only database role
235	          - **THEN** the MCP refuses to start, and reports a project configuration error
236	      - ### Requirement: Supported agent clients
237	        - V0 SHALL document setup for Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex. All four operations SHALL work in each of them with Roam and Obsidian closed. ChatGPT isn't supported, because it can't launch a local MCP.
238	        - **Scenario: Validate each client**
239	          - **GIVEN** synced readable data, and a bundle from the supported handoff
240	          - **WHEN** setup and tool execution are validated separately in Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex, with Roam and Obsidian closed
241	          - **THEN** each client launches the MCP and completes all four retrieval operations
